more: More means a greater amount, number, or degree than before or than something else.
more 指数量、数目或程度比以前或另一对象更大。
now: Now refers to the present time rather than the past or future.
now 指现在这一刻，而不是过去或未来。
some: Some refers to an unspecified amount or number, usually not the whole.
some 指不确定的一些数量，通常不是全部。
then: Then refers to a time in the past or future, or to the next step in a sequence.
then 指过去或将来的某个时候，也可表示接下来的步骤。
up: Up usually indicates movement toward a higher position or an increase.
up 通常表示向更高处移动，或数量、程度增加。
year: A year is a period of twelve months.
year 指十二个月的时间。
after: After means later than a particular time, event, or action.
after 表示在某个时间、事件或动作之后。
any: Any can mean one or more without specifying which, often in questions and negatives.
any 指不特定的一个或一些，常用于疑问句和否定句。
great: Something great is very good, important, or large in degree.
great 指非常好、十分重要，或程度很大。
little: Little can mean small in size or a small amount.
little 可表示体积较小，或数量很少。
long: Something long extends a great distance or lasts a lot of time.
long 指长度很长，或持续时间很久。
only: Only means no more than the stated person, thing, or amount.
only 表示“仅仅、只有”，排除其他人、事物或数量。
over: Over often means above something or beyond a limit or period.
over 常表示“在上方”，也可指超过某个界限或期限。
very: Very makes an adjective or adverb stronger in degree.
very 用来加强形容词或副词表示的程度。
before: Before means earlier than a particular time or event.
before 表示在某个时间或事件之前。
day: A day is a twenty-four-hour period, or the daylight part of it.
day 指二十四小时的一天，也可特指白天。
first: First means coming before all others in order, time, or importance.
first 指在顺序、时间或重要性上排在最前面。
hand: A hand is the part at the end of your arm used for holding and touching things.
hand 指手臂末端用于抓握和触摸的手。
may: may 用来表示可能性或许可。
most: Most means the largest amount or number of something.
most 指某事物中数量最多、比例最大的一部分。
much: Much means a large amount, especially of something uncountable.
much 指大量，尤其用于不可数的事物。
such: Such refers to something of the kind just mentioned, sometimes emphasizing its degree.
such 指前文所说的那一类事物，有时还用于强调程度。
well: Well often means in a good or satisfactory way; it can also mean healthy.
well 常表示做得好、令人满意，也可指身体健康。
life: Life is the state of being alive or the experience of living.
life 指生命存在的状态，也可指生活经历。
tell: To tell someone something is to give them information by speaking or writing.
tell 指通过口头或书面方式告诉某人信息。
back: Back can mean returning to an earlier place or position, or the rear part of something.
back 可以指回到原先位置，也可以指事物的背面或后部。
many: Many means a large number of countable people or things.
many 指大量可数的人或事物。
never: Never means at no time, not even once.
never 表示“从不”，一次也没有。
thing: A thing is an object, matter, or idea that is not named more specifically.
thing 指未具体命名的物品、事情或想法。
way: A way is a method of doing something, or a route to a place.
way 指做某事的方法，也可指通往某地的路线。
people: People are human beings considered as a group.
people 指作为一个群体的人们。
again: Again means one more time or back to an earlier state.
again 表示“再一次”，也可表示回到先前状态。
call: To call someone is to say their name, contact them by phone, or give them a particular name.
call 可指喊某人、打电话联系某人，或称呼某人。
down: Down usually indicates movement toward a lower position or a decrease.
down 通常表示向低处移动，或数量、程度下降。
every: Every means each member of a group without exception.
every 表示一组中的每一个，没有例外。
just: Just can mean only, exactly, or a very short time ago.
just 可表示“仅仅”“正好”，也可表示“刚刚”。
might: Might expresses possibility, often with less certainty than will.
might 表示可能性，通常比 will 所表达的确定性低。
old: Something old has existed or lived for a long time.
old 指已经存在或生活了很长时间的。
still: Still can mean continuing up to now or remaining in the same state.
still 可表示“仍然”，强调持续至今或状态未变。
through: Through means from one side of something to the other, often passing inside it.
through 表示从某物的一侧穿到另一侧，通常经过其内部。
too: Too can mean also, or more than is desirable.
too 可表示“也”，也可表示“过于、超过合适程度”。
while: While means during the time that something happens, or introduces a contrast.
while 可表示“在……期间”，也可以引出两种情况的对比。
hear: To hear is to perceive sound with your ears, whether or not you intend to listen.
hear 指耳朵听见声音，不一定是主动去听。
world: The world is the Earth and everything on it, or a particular area of activity or experience.
world 指地球及其上的一切，也可指某个活动或经验领域。
become: To become something is to change into a new state, role, or condition.
become 指转变成新的状态、身份或情况。
speak: To speak is to use your voice to say words or communicate.
speak 指用声音说出话语或进行交流。
another: Another means one more or a different one of the same kind.
another 指同类中的另外一个，或再一个。
child: A child is a young person who has not yet reached adulthood.
child 指尚未成年的孩子。
high: Something high is far above the ground or great in amount or level.
high 指位置很高，也可指数量或程度较高。
name: A name is a word or set of words used to identify a person or thing.
name 指用来称呼、辨认某人或某物的词语。
new: Something new has recently appeared, been created, or become known.
new 指近期出现、创造出来或刚被认识到的。
off: Off often indicates separation, removal, or that something is not operating.
off 常表示分离、移开，或设备未在运行。
yet: Yet often means up to now in questions and negatives, or nevertheless.
yet 常用于疑问句和否定句表示“到现在为止”，也可表示“然而”。
begin: To begin something is to start it.
end: An end is the final part of something; to end is to bring it to a stop.
end 作名词指最后部分，作动词指使某事结束。
open: To open something is to remove a barrier or make it available for use or entry.
open 指打开阻隔，或使某物可以使用、进入。
same: The same means not different from what was mentioned or compared.
same 表示与前述或对比对象没有区别。
true: Something true agrees with the facts or reality.
true 指符合事实或现实的。
kind: A kind is a type or category; kind also means caring toward others.
kind 作名词指种类，作形容词时还表示友善、体贴。
better: Better means of higher quality or more suitable than something else.
better 指质量更好，或比另一选择更合适。
almost: Almost means very nearly, but not completely.
almost 表示“几乎”，但尚未完全达到。
always: Always means at every time or on every occasion.
always 表示“总是”，每次都如此。
accountable: If you are accountable for something, you must explain your actions and accept responsibility for the results.
accountable 指需要就自己的行为作出说明，并对结果承担责任。
adaptable: Someone or something adaptable can change easily to suit new conditions.
adaptable 指人或事物能灵活调整，以适应新的环境或条件。
adjacent: Two things are adjacent when they are next to each other.
adjacent 指两个事物彼此紧挨着、相邻。
aggregate: An aggregate is a total formed by combining several amounts or parts.
aggregate 作名词指把多个数量或部分合在一起得到的总量。
articulate: To articulate an idea is to express it clearly in words.
articulate 作动词指用语言清楚地表达一种想法。
authentic: Something authentic is real or genuine, not a copy or a pretence.
authentic 指真实、可信，并非仿制或伪装出来的。
collaborate: To collaborate is to work with others toward a shared goal.
collaborate 指与他人合作，以完成共同目标。
compile: To compile information is to collect it from different sources and put it together.
compile 指从不同来源收集信息并整理汇总。
complement: To complement something is to add what it lacks and make the whole better.
complement 作动词指补足某物欠缺的部分，使整体更加完善。
comply: To comply is to act according to a rule, request, or requirement.
comply 指遵守规则、要求或规定，并按其行事。
conceive: To conceive an idea is to think of it or imagine it for the first time.
conceive 指最初想到或设想出一个主意。
concurrent: Events are concurrent when they happen at the same time.
concurrent 指事件同时发生或并行进行。
contingency: A contingency is a possible future event that you may need to prepare for.
contingency 指未来可能发生、需要预先准备应对的情况。
contradict: To contradict a statement is to say or show that it is not true.
contradict 指用言语或证据反驳某种说法，表明它不成立。
controversial: Something controversial causes strong disagreement or public debate.
controversial 指引起明显分歧或广泛争论。
convey: To convey information or feelings is to communicate them to someone.
convey 指向他人传达信息、想法或情感。
cumulative: A cumulative amount grows as more amounts are added over time.
cumulative 指随着时间推移不断累加形成的总量。
currency: A currency is the system of money used in a particular country or region.
currency 指某个国家或地区使用的货币。
dedicate: To dedicate time or effort is to give it to a particular purpose.
dedicate 指把时间或精力投入某个特定目标。
default: A default setting is the option used automatically unless someone changes it.
default setting 指没有主动更改时系统自动采用的默认设置。
definitive: A definitive answer is considered final and authoritative rather than provisional.
definitive 指答案被认为是最终且有权威性的，而非暂定。
designate: To designate someone or something is to officially choose or name them for a role or purpose.
designate 指正式指定某人或某物承担某种角色或用途。
deviate: To deviate is to move away from an expected path, rule, or standard.
deviate 指偏离预期路线、规则或标准。
diagnose: To diagnose a problem is to identify its cause by examining the evidence.
diagnose 指通过检查证据判断问题的原因。
differentiate: To differentiate things is to recognize or show how they are different.
differentiate 指辨认或说明事物之间的区别。
diminish: To diminish is to become smaller, weaker, or less important.
diminish 指数量、强度或重要性逐渐减小。
discrete: Discrete things are separate and distinct rather than continuous or joined.
discrete 指彼此分离、界限明确，而不是连续一体。
discriminate: To discriminate between things is to notice or identify the differences between them.
discriminate between 指分辨不同事物之间的区别。
discrepancy: A discrepancy is a difference between figures, statements, or results that should agree.
discrepancy 指本应一致的数据、说法或结果之间出现的差异。
dismiss: To dismiss an idea is to decide that it is not worth serious consideration.
dismiss an idea 指认为某种观点不值得认真考虑而将其否定。
diverse: A diverse group contains people or things of many different kinds.
diverse 指一个群体由多种不同的人或事物组成。
domain: A domain is a particular area of knowledge, work, or activity.
domain 指某个特定的知识、工作或活动领域。
dominant: Something dominant has more power, influence, or importance than others.
dominant 指某事物比其他事物更有影响力、力量或重要性。
dynamic: A dynamic situation changes or develops instead of staying the same.
dynamic 指情形不断变化发展，而非保持不变。
elaborate: To elaborate on an idea is to explain it in greater detail.
elaborate on 指进一步详细说明某个想法。
encompass: To encompass something is to include it as part of a larger whole.
encompass 指把某事物包含在更大的整体之中。
encounter: To encounter something is to meet or experience it, often unexpectedly.
encounter 指遇到或经历某事，往往带有意外发生的意味。
entail: If an action entails something, it necessarily involves or requires it.
entail 指某种行动必然涉及或需要另一件事。
entity: An entity is something that exists as a separate, identifiable unit.
entity 指作为独立、可识别单位而存在的事物或组织。
equivalent: Two things are equivalent if they have the same value, meaning, or function in a particular context.
equivalent 指两个事物在特定语境中具有相同价值、意义或作用。
erode: To erode something is to wear it away slowly or gradually weaken it.
erode 指逐渐磨损某物，或逐步削弱其力量。
evoke: To evoke a feeling or memory is to bring it into someone's mind.
evoke 指唤起某人的情感或记忆。
exhibit: To exhibit a quality or behaviour is to show it clearly.
exhibit 指明显表现出某种特征或行为。
exploit: To exploit an opportunity is to make effective use of it for a purpose.
exploit an opportunity 指为达到某个目的而充分利用机会。
flexible: Something flexible can change or be adapted without great difficulty.
flexible 指能够轻松改变或调整，具有灵活性。
fluctuate: To fluctuate is to move up and down rather than stay at one level.
fluctuate 指数值或状态上下波动，而不维持在固定水平。
formulate: To formulate a plan or explanation is to develop it carefully and state it clearly.
formulate 指认真构思计划或解释，并清楚地表达出来。
genuine: Something genuine is truly what it claims to be, rather than fake.
genuine 指某事物确实如其所称，并非假冒。
gradual: A gradual change happens slowly, in small steps.
gradual 指变化缓慢、分阶段逐步发生。
hierarchy: A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged by rank or level.
hierarchy 指按等级或层次排列人或事物的体系。
incentive: An incentive is something that encourages someone to do something.
incentive 指促使某人采取行动的奖励、利益或其他激励因素。
incorporate: To incorporate something is to include it as part of a larger whole.
incorporate 指把某物纳入一个更大的整体。
inevitable: Something inevitable cannot be prevented or avoided.
inevitable 指不可避免、无法阻止的事情。
inherent: An inherent quality is a natural or essential part of something.
inherent 指某种性质是事物本身固有或不可分割的部分。
insight: An insight is a clear and often deep understanding of a problem or situation.
insight 指对问题或情况清晰而深入的理解。
integrity: Integrity is honesty and a commitment to acting according to strong principles.
integrity 指诚实守信，并坚持按原则行事。
intervene: To intervene is to become involved in a situation in order to change what happens.
intervene 指介入某种情况，以影响事件的发展。
intrinsic: An intrinsic feature belongs to the essential nature of something.
intrinsic 指某种特征属于事物的本质，而非外部附加。
isolate: To isolate something is to separate it from other things so it can be examined or dealt with alone.
isolate 指将某物与其他事物分开，以便单独研究或处理。
leverage: To leverage a resource or advantage is to use it to achieve a better result.
leverage 作动词指利用资源或优势取得更好的结果。
manifest: If a quality manifests itself, it becomes visible or clear through actions or effects.
manifest itself 指某种特征通过行为或效果显现出来。
manipulate: To manipulate information is to change or handle it deliberately, sometimes unfairly.
manipulate information 指有意处理或改变信息，有时带有不正当操控的意味。
marginal: A marginal difference is very small and may have little practical importance.
marginal 指差异很小，可能没有多少实际意义。
mediate: To mediate is to help two sides settle a disagreement or reach an agreement.
mediate 指帮助争议双方化解分歧、达成协议。
mitigate: To mitigate a problem is to make its harmful effects less serious.
mitigate 指减轻问题带来的不良影响。
neutral: A neutral position does not support either side of a disagreement.
neutral 指在争议中不偏向任何一方的立场。
occupy: To occupy a space is to take up or fill that space.
occupy 指占据或填满某个空间。
offset: To offset a disadvantage is to balance or compensate for its effect.
offset 指通过其他优势或措施抵消某种不利影响。
overlap: Two things overlap when they share some of the same space, time, or features.
overlap 指两个事物在空间、时间或特征上存在交集。
perceive: To perceive something is to notice it or understand it in a particular way.
perceive 指察觉某事，或以某种方式理解某事。
persist: To persist is to continue despite difficulties or over a long time.
persist 指尽管有困难仍继续，或长时间持续存在。
perspective: A perspective is a particular way of looking at or understanding something.
perspective 指看待或理解问题的某种角度。
phenomenon: A phenomenon is something that happens or exists and can be observed.
phenomenon 指发生或存在、可以被观察到的现象。
policy: A policy is a set of principles or rules used to guide decisions and actions.
policy 指指导决策和行动的一套原则或规则。
preliminary: A preliminary result is an early finding that may be revised after more work.
preliminary 指初步结果，之后仍可能进一步修改。
profound: Something profound has a deep or far-reaching effect or meaning.
profound 指影响或意义深刻、深远。
prohibit: To prohibit an activity is to officially forbid it.
prohibit 指通过规定或法律正式禁止某项活动。
rational: A rational decision is based on reason and evidence rather than impulse.
rational 指决策依据理性和证据，而非一时冲动。
reconcile: To reconcile different facts or views is to find a way for them to agree or fit together.
reconcile 指使不同事实或观点相互协调、一致。
reinforce: To reinforce something is to make it stronger or more convincing.
reinforce 指使某事物更牢固，或使论点更有说服力。
reject: To reject a proposal is to decide not to accept it.
reject 指决定不接受某项建议或提议。
replicate: To replicate a result is to produce the same or very similar result again.
replicate 指再次得到相同或非常相近的结果。
sophisticated: Something sophisticated is complex and carefully developed, often using advanced methods.
sophisticated 指事物结构复杂、设计精细，常采用先进方法。
stable: Something stable remains steady and is unlikely to change suddenly.
stable 指状态稳定，不容易突然变化。
standard: A standard is an agreed level of quality or a rule used for comparison.
standard 指公认的质量水平或用于比较的规范。
static: Something static stays in the same state rather than changing or moving.
static 指处于静止或不变化的状态。
synthesize: To synthesize information is to combine ideas from several sources into a new whole.
synthesize 指把不同来源的信息或观点综合成一个新的整体。
tentative: A tentative plan is not final and may be changed later.
tentative 指计划尚未最终确定，以后可能调整。
trace: To trace an effect is to follow it back to its source or cause.
trace 指追踪某种结果，找出它的来源或原因。
transition: A transition is the process of changing from one state or stage to another.
transition 指从一种状态或阶段转变到另一种的过程。
transparent: A transparent decision-making process is open and easy for others to understand.
transparent 指决策过程公开清楚，便于他人理解。
ultimate: An ultimate goal is the final or most important aim.
ultimate 指最终的或最重要的目标。
underlying: An underlying cause is a basic reason beneath the more obvious facts.
underlying 指隐藏在表面现象之下的根本原因。
viable: A viable plan is realistic enough to work successfully.
viable 指计划切实可行，有望成功实施。
virtual: Something virtual exists or is experienced through a computer rather than as a physical object.
virtual 指通过计算机存在或体验，而不是实体形式。
vulnerable: Someone or something vulnerable can be easily harmed or negatively affected.
vulnerable 指容易受到伤害或不利影响。
widespread: Something widespread exists or happens in many places or among many people.
widespread 指某种事物或现象在许多地方或人群中普遍存在。
allocate: To allocate resources is to decide how they should be divided among different needs.
allocate 指决定如何把资源分配给不同需求。
approximate: An approximate value is close to the correct value but not exact.
approximate 指数值接近真实值，但并不完全精确。
align: To align plans or goals is to make them consistent or work toward the same purpose.
align 指使计划或目标相互一致、朝同一方向配合。
authenticate: To authenticate something is to check that it is genuine or valid.
authenticate 指核实某物真实有效。
calibrate: To calibrate an instrument is to compare or adjust it against a known reference.
calibrate 指将仪器与已知参考量进行比较或调整，以确认其测量准确性。
capture: To capture information is to record or collect it so it can be used later.
capture information 指记录或收集信息，以便后续使用。
cluster: A cluster is a group of similar or nearby things.
cluster 指一组彼此相近或相似的事物。
compute: To compute a number is to calculate it from given information.
compute 指根据已有信息计算出一个数值。
consolidate: To consolidate several things is to combine them into a stronger or simpler whole.
consolidate 指将几项事物整合为更稳固或更简洁的整体。
convert: To convert something is to change it into a different form or type.
convert 指把某物转换成另一种形式或类型。
diagnosis: A diagnosis is the identification of a problem or medical condition after examination.
diagnosis 指经过检查后对问题或疾病作出的判断。
disparity: A disparity is a noticeable difference, especially one that seems unfair or unequal.
disparity 指明显差距，尤其是让人觉得不公平或不平等的差距。
distinct: Two things are distinct if they are clearly different from each other.
distinct 指两个事物彼此有清楚的区别。
impose: To impose a rule or cost is to make others accept or bear it.
impose 指强制他人接受某项规定或承担某种费用。
interpolate: To interpolate a value is to estimate it between known data points.
interpolate 指根据已知数据点估计其间的数值。
inventory: An inventory is a detailed list of goods, supplies, or other items.
inventory 指货物、物资或其他项目的详细清单。
iterate: To iterate is to repeat a process, often improving it in each round.
iterate 指反复执行某个过程，通常在每轮中进行改进。
latency: Latency is the delay between an action or signal and the response it produces.
latency 指动作或信号发生到产生响应之间的时间延迟。
magnitude: Magnitude is the size or amount of something, especially a measurable quantity.
magnitude 指事物的大小或数量，尤其用于可测量的量。
parallel: Parallel processes happen or operate at the same time rather than one after another.
parallel 指多个过程同时运行，而不是依次进行。
pipeline: A pipeline is a connected series of steps through which data or work passes.
pipeline 指数据或工作依次经过的一系列相连步骤。
probe: To probe a question is to investigate it carefully to learn more.
probe 指仔细探究问题，以获取更多信息。
quantify: To quantify something is to express or measure it using numbers.
quantify 指用数字表示或衡量某事物。
signal: A signal is a sign or transmitted message that carries information.
signal 指传递信息的标志或信号。
synchronize: To synchronize processes is to arrange them to occur at the same time or in a coordinated order.
synchronize 指让多个过程同时发生，或按协调一致的顺序进行。
lexical: Something lexical is related to words or vocabulary rather than grammar alone.
lexical 指与单词或词汇有关，而不只是与语法有关。
morphology: Morphology is the study of how words are built from smaller meaningful parts.
morphology 指研究单词如何由更小的有意义部分构成的学问。
prefix: A prefix is a group of letters added to the beginning of a word to change its meaning.
prefix 指加在单词开头、用来改变词义的字母组合（前缀）。
synonym: A synonym is a word with the same or a similar meaning as another word.
synonym 指与另一单词意义相同或相近的词（近义词）。
antonym: An antonym is a word with the opposite meaning to another word.
antonym 指与另一单词意义相反的词（反义词）。
pragmatic: A pragmatic approach focuses on what is practical and likely to work.
pragmatic 指做法重视实际效果与可行性。
fluency: Fluency is the ability to speak or use a language smoothly and with little hesitation.
fluency 指说话或使用语言流畅、较少停顿的能力。
receptive: Receptive language ability means understanding words or messages that you hear or read.
receptive language ability 指理解听到或读到的词语与信息的能力。
productive: Productive language ability means being able to use words and structures when speaking or writing.
productive language ability 指在口语或写作中主动运用词汇与结构的能力。
abide: To abide by a rule is to accept it and act according to it.
abide by 指遵守规则或约定，并按其要求行事。
abrupt: Something abrupt happens suddenly, often without warning or a smooth transition.
abrupt 指事情突然发生，往往缺少预兆或自然过渡。
abundance: An abundance of something means that there is a large amount of it.
abundance 指某物数量丰富、供应充足。
accessible: Something accessible is easy to reach, enter, use, or understand.
accessible 指容易接近、进入、使用或理解的。
accommodate: To accommodate someone is to provide space for them or adjust to their needs.
accommodate 指为某人提供容纳空间，或照顾其需要。
accumulate: To accumulate something is to collect or increase it gradually over time.
accumulate 指某物随着时间逐步积累或增加。
admiration: Admiration is a feeling of respect and approval for someone or something.
admiration 指对某人或某事产生的钦佩与赞赏。
adversity: Adversity refers to difficult conditions that test a person's ability to cope.
adversity 指考验一个人应对能力的困境或逆境。
advocate: To advocate a policy is to speak or act publicly in support of it.
advocate 指公开表达或采取行动支持某项政策或主张。
aesthetic: Something aesthetic is concerned with beauty or the way things look and feel.
aesthetic 指与美感、外观或感官体验有关的。
affinity: Affinity is a natural liking for something or a close similarity between things.
affinity 指天然的亲近感、喜好，或事物之间的相似性、亲和性。
agenda: An agenda is a list of topics or tasks to be discussed or dealt with.
agenda 指会议待议事项或需要处理的任务清单。
alleviate: To alleviate a problem is to make it less severe or easier to bear.
alleviate 指减轻问题的严重程度或使其更容易承受。
ambiguity: Ambiguity exists when words or situations can be understood in more than one way.
ambiguity 指表达或情况存在不止一种合理理解。
analogy: An analogy explains one thing by comparing it with a similar situation or idea.
analogy 指通过比较类似情形或概念来解释某事。
apparatus: An apparatus is a set of equipment used for a particular task or experiment.
apparatus 指为特定工作或实验配置的一套设备。
appeal: An appeal is a request for help, support, or a change in a decision.
appeal 指请求帮助、支持，或要求改变某项决定。
applicable: A rule or idea is applicable when it can be used in a particular situation.
applicable 指规则或观点适用于某个具体情形。
archive: An archive is a collection of records kept for future reference.
archive 指为日后查阅而保存的档案或资料集合。
aspire: To aspire to something is to hope and work toward a meaningful goal.
aspire 指渴望实现有意义的目标，并为之努力。
asset: An asset is something valuable that a person or organization owns or can use.
asset 指个人或组织拥有、可使用的有价值资源或财产。
attain: To attain a goal is to reach it through effort or progress.
attain 指通过努力或进展实现目标。
autonomous: Someone or something autonomous can make decisions or operate independently.
autonomous 指能够自主决策或独立运作的。
bizarre: Something bizarre is extremely unusual and hard to explain or expect.
bizarre 指非常怪异、令人难以理解或预料的。
blend: To blend things is to mix them so that they form a smooth combination.
blend 指把不同事物混合，使其协调融合。
bold: A bold decision is confident and willing to take risks.
bold 指决定大胆、有魄力，愿意承担风险。
bond: A bond is a connection or relationship that holds people or things together.
bond 指使人或事物紧密联系在一起的纽带。
boost: To boost something is to increase or improve it.
boost 指增加某物的数量、水平或表现。
breach: A breach is a failure to obey an agreement, rule, or security boundary.
breach 指违反协议、规则，或突破安全防线。
brief: Something brief lasts only a short time or uses few words.
brief 指持续时间短，或表达简洁。
burden: A burden is a heavy responsibility, cost, or difficulty that someone carries.
burden 指需要承担的沉重责任、费用或困难。
bureaucracy: Bureaucracy is a system of administration with many formal rules and procedures.
bureaucracy 指依靠正式规则和程序运转的行政管理体系。
bypass: To bypass something is to go around it rather than through it.
bypass 指绕开某个地方、步骤或障碍。
cautious: Someone cautious acts carefully to avoid mistakes or danger.
cautious 指做事谨慎，以避免错误或危险。
cease: To cease doing something is to stop doing it.
cease 指停止某项活动或行为。
collision: A collision happens when two objects or forces strike each other.
collision 指两个物体或力量发生碰撞。
commodity: A commodity is a basic product, often traded in large quantities.
commodity 指通常大量交易的基础商品或原材料。
commonplace: Something commonplace is ordinary and seen or experienced often.
commonplace 指很常见、没有什么特别之处的。
compact: Something compact is small and arranged to use little space.
compact 指结构紧凑、占用空间少的。
competent: Someone competent has the skill and knowledge needed to do a task well.
competent 指具备完成任务所需的技能与知识。
compliance: Compliance means following a rule, request, or official requirement.
compliance 指遵守规则、要求或正式规定。
conceal: To conceal something is to keep it from being seen or known.
conceal 指将某事物隐藏起来，不让人看到或得知。
concentration: Concentration is the act of focusing attention or gathering something in one place.
concentration 指集中注意力，或把某物集中到一处。
conditional: Something conditional happens or applies only if a certain requirement is met.
conditional 指只有满足特定条件才会发生或适用的。
consensus: A consensus is a general agreement reached by members of a group.
consensus 指群体成员形成的大体一致意见。
conserve: To conserve something is to protect it from waste or loss.
conserve 指保护资源，避免浪费或损失。
convention: A convention is a widely accepted practice or established way of doing something.
convention 指社会或领域内普遍接受的惯例。
cultivate: To cultivate a skill or attitude is to develop it through repeated attention and effort.
cultivate 指通过持续投入培养技能或态度。
curiosity: Curiosity is a desire to learn, explore, or understand something.
curiosity 指想要学习、探索或弄明白某事的好奇心。
deficit: A deficit is the amount by which what is available falls short of what is needed.
deficit 指实际拥有的数量低于所需数量的差额。
delegate: To delegate a task is to give someone else responsibility for carrying it out.
delegate 指将某项任务的执行责任交给别人。
deliberate: A deliberate action is done intentionally rather than by accident.
deliberate 指有意做出的行为，而非偶然发生。
dense: Something dense contains a lot of material or information in a small space.
dense 指在较小空间内包含大量物质或信息的。
deploy: To deploy equipment or people is to put them where they are needed for use.
deploy 指把设备或人员配置到需要使用的地方。
deprive: To deprive someone of something is to prevent them from having it.
deprive 指使某人无法获得或享有某物。
diffuse: To diffuse something is to spread it over a wider area.
diffuse 指让某物向更广的范围扩散。
dilemma: A dilemma is a difficult choice between options that each have drawbacks.
dilemma 指在各有缺点的选项之间难以抉择的处境。
disperse: To disperse a group or substance is to spread it in different directions.
disperse 指使人群或物质向不同方向散开。
diversify: To diversify something is to make it include a greater variety of types.
diversify 指使某物包含更多不同种类，增加多样性。
drastic: A drastic change is very large, sudden, or far-reaching.
drastic 指变化幅度很大、突然或影响深远的。
durable: Something durable is able to last a long time without breaking or wearing out.
durable 指经久耐用、不容易损坏的。
earnest: Someone earnest is serious and sincere about what they do or say.
earnest 指做事或说话认真、真诚的。
elevate: To elevate something is to raise its position, level, or importance.
elevate 指提高某物的位置、水平或重要性。
eliminate: To eliminate something is to remove it completely.
eliminate 指把某物彻底消除或去掉。
embed: To embed something is to place it firmly within something else.
embed 指把某物牢固地放入或嵌入另一事物中。
embrace: To embrace an idea or change is to accept it willingly.
embrace 指欣然接受某种观念或变化。
emerge: To emerge is to become visible, known, or important after being hidden or unclear.
emerge 指从隐蔽或不明朗的状态中出现、显现。
endorse: To endorse a person or idea is to express public support for them.
endorse 指公开表示支持某人或某种观点。
enforce: To enforce a rule is to make sure people obey it.
enforce 指确保规则得到遵守和执行。
eradicate: To eradicate a problem or disease is to remove it completely.
eradicate 指彻底消除某个问题或疾病。
escalate: To escalate is to become more serious, intense, or widespread.
escalate 指情况变得更加严重、激烈或扩大。
ethical: Something ethical follows accepted principles of right and wrong.
ethical 指符合公认道德原则的。
evolve: To evolve is to change and develop gradually over time.
evolve 指随着时间逐渐变化、发展。
extract: To extract something is to remove or obtain it from a larger whole.
extract 指从整体中取出或提取某物。
grasp: To grasp an idea is to understand it clearly.
grasp 指清楚地理解一个想法或概念。
ideal: Something ideal is as good or suitable as it could reasonably be.
ideal 指达到理想状态、非常合适的。
idle: Someone or something idle is not active or being used.
idle 指没有活动或暂时未被使用的。
incident: An incident is an event, often unusual or involving a problem.
incident 指发生的一件事，常带有异常或问题性质。
inherit: To inherit something is to receive it from someone or something that came before.
inherit 指从先前的人或事物那里继承、获得某物。
inhibit: To inhibit a process is to slow it down or prevent it from developing.
inhibit 指阻碍或抑制某个过程的发展。
integral: Something integral is essential to the completeness or functioning of a whole.
integral 指对整体完整性或正常运作不可或缺的。
intensity: Intensity is the degree of strength or concentration of something.
intensity 指某种作用、感受或现象的强烈程度。
interact: To interact is to act on or communicate with another person or thing.
interact 指人与人或事物之间相互作用、交流。
interfere: To interfere is to become involved in a way that interrupts or hinders something.
interfere 指介入并打断或妨碍某事。
intermediate: Something intermediate lies between two levels, stages, or positions.
intermediate 指位于两个水平、阶段或位置之间的。
intuitive: Something intuitive is easy to understand or do without detailed explanation.
intuitive 指不需详细说明就容易理解或操作的。
landmark: A landmark is a recognizable place or an important event in a process.
landmark 指显著的地标，或发展过程中重要的里程碑。
latitude: Latitude is the distance north or south of the equator, measured in degrees.
latitude 指以角度表示的某地与赤道之间的南北距离（纬度）。
liberal: A liberal interpretation allows more freedom and is less strict about details.
liberal 指解释方式较宽松、对细节限制较少的。
liable: Someone liable for a cost or damage is legally responsible for it.
liable 指依法需要对费用或损害承担责任的。
livelihood: A livelihood is the work or income that enables someone to live.
livelihood 指一个人赖以维持生活的工作或收入来源。
mentor: A mentor is an experienced person who guides someone with less experience.
mentor 指为经验较少的人提供指导的有经验者。
merge: To merge things is to join them into one combined whole.
merge 指将多个事物合并为一个整体。
migrate: To migrate is to move from one place or system to another.
migrate 指从一个地方或系统迁移到另一个。
minimal: Something minimal is as small or limited as possible.
minimal 指尽可能少或尽可能有限的。
mutual: A mutual feeling or action is shared by two or more parties.
mutual 指双方或多方共同拥有的感受或行为。
naive: Someone naive lacks experience and may trust or believe too easily.
naive 指缺乏经验、容易轻信的。
narrative: A narrative is an account that connects events into a story or explanation.
narrative 指将事件串联起来的故事或叙述。
neglect: To neglect something is to fail to give it needed attention or care.
neglect 指没有给予某事物应有的关注或照顾。
notion: A notion is an idea or belief about something.
notion 指关于某事的一种想法或看法。
oblige: To oblige someone is to require them to do something, or to do them a favor.
oblige 指要求某人履行某事，或帮某人一个忙。
obscure: Something obscure is difficult to find, see, or understand.
obscure 指难以发现、看清或理解的。
optimistic: Someone optimistic expects good things to happen or problems to improve.
optimistic 指倾向于期待好结果或情况改善的。
orient: To orient yourself is to understand where you are or how to approach a situation.
orient yourself 指弄清自己所处的位置或应对情境的方向。
outweigh: If one factor outweighs another, it has greater importance or effect.
outweigh 指某个因素的重要性或影响超过另一个。
override: To override a decision or setting is to replace it with a higher-priority one.
override 指用更高优先级的决定或设置取代原有内容。
oversee: To oversee work is to supervise it and make sure it is done properly.
oversee 指监督工作并确保其妥善完成。
paradigm: A paradigm is a model or pattern that shapes how people think about a subject.
paradigm 指影响人们理解某个领域的模式或范式。
pioneer: A pioneer is someone who is among the first to explore or develop an approach.
pioneer 指率先探索或开发某种方法的人。
pledge: A pledge is a serious promise or commitment to do something.
pledge 指郑重作出的承诺。
prevail: To prevail is to succeed or become dominant after difficulty or competition.
prevail 指经过困难或竞争后获胜、占上风。
prominent: Something prominent is important, well known, or easy to notice.
prominent 指重要、知名或容易引起注意的。
prompt: To prompt an action is to cause or encourage someone to do it.
prompt 指促使或引导某人采取行动。
prospect: A prospect is a possible future event or opportunity, especially one being considered.
prospect 指正在考虑的未来可能情况或机会。
provoke: To provoke a reaction is to cause it, sometimes deliberately.
provoke 指引起某种反应，有时是故意激起的。
readily: If something happens readily, it happens easily or without hesitation.
readily 指某事容易发生，或毫不犹豫地进行。
reassure: To reassure someone is to make them feel less worried or uncertain.
reassure 指安慰某人，使其不那么担心或不确定。
reluctant: Someone reluctant is unwilling or hesitant to do something.
reluctant 指不太愿意或犹豫着要不要做某事的。
render: To render something useless is to cause it to become useless.
render 指使某物变成某种状态，如变得无用。
reside: To reside somewhere is to live there, especially for a long period.
reside 指在某地居住，尤其是较长期居住。
restrain: To restrain someone or something is to hold them back or keep them under control.
restrain 指约束、控制某人或某物，不让其任意行动。
routine: A routine is a regular series of actions performed in a familiar order.
routine 指按照固定顺序反复进行的日常活动。
secure: To secure something is to obtain or protect it so it remains safe or available.
secure 指取得某物，或把它保护妥当以确保安全、可用。
segment: A segment is one part of a larger whole.
segment 指较大整体中的一个部分。
selective: Someone selective chooses carefully instead of accepting every option.
selective 指有所选择、不会照单全收的。
simultaneous: Simultaneous events happen at the same time.
simultaneous 指多件事情在同一时间发生。
sparse: Something sparse is thinly spread or has relatively few elements.
sparse 指分布稀疏、数量较少的。
stabilize: To stabilize something is to make it steady or less likely to change suddenly.
stabilize 指使某物趋于稳定、不易突然变化。
stimulate: To stimulate activity or growth is to encourage it to become stronger or faster.
stimulate 指促进活动或增长，使其更活跃或更快。
strain: A strain is pressure or stress that makes something hard to maintain.
strain 指使某种状态难以维持的压力或负担。
sum: A sum is a total amount obtained by adding quantities together.
sum 指把若干数量相加所得的总和。
supplement: A supplement is something added to make an existing supply more complete.
supplement 指为补充、完善已有内容而额外增加的东西。
sustainable: Something sustainable can continue over time without exhausting resources.
sustainable 指能够长期持续、不会耗尽所需资源的。
tangible: Something tangible can be touched or clearly observed, rather than merely imagined.
tangible 指能够触摸或清楚感知、并非仅存在于想象中的。
territory: A territory is an area of land belonging to or controlled by a group or state.
territory 指属于某个群体或国家、或受其控制的地域。
testify: To testify is to give a formal account of what you know, especially in court.
testify 指正式陈述所知事实，尤其是在法庭上作证。
tolerate: To tolerate something is to allow or endure it even if you dislike it.
tolerate 指即使不喜欢也允许或忍受某事。
transmit: To transmit information or energy is to send it from one place to another.
transmit 指把信息或能量从一处传送到另一处。
unify: To unify separate groups or parts is to bring them together into one whole.
unify 指将分散的群体或部分整合成一个整体。
unique: Something unique is the only one of its kind, or unlike anything else.
unique 指独一无二，或与其他事物明显不同的。
upgrade: To upgrade something is to replace or improve it with a better version.
upgrade 指把某物更新、改进为更好的版本。
uphold: To uphold a rule or principle is to support and maintain it.
uphold 指支持并维护某项规则或原则。
utility: The utility of something is how useful it is for a particular purpose.
utility 指某物对特定目的的实用价值。
versatile: Someone or something versatile can perform many different tasks or functions well.
versatile 指能胜任多种任务或用途的。
vital: Something vital is absolutely necessary or extremely important.
vital 指不可缺少或极为重要的。
warrant: To warrant an action is to provide a good reason for taking it.
warrant 指为采取某项行动提供充分理由。
amend: To amend a document or rule is to make a formal change to it.
amend 指正式修改文件、规定或法案中的某些内容。
amplify: To amplify something is to make it stronger, louder, or more noticeable.
amplify 指增强声音、信号或某种影响，使其更明显。
anchor: To anchor something is to hold it firmly in place or give it a stable base.
anchor 指固定某物的位置，或为某事提供稳定的基础。
appoint: To appoint someone is to officially choose them for a position or task.
appoint 指正式任命某人担任职位或执行任务。
assemble: To assemble something is to bring its separate parts together.
assemble 指把分散的零件或部分组装在一起。
assign: To assign a task is to decide who is responsible for doing it.
assign 指把任务指定给某人负责。
assist: To assist someone is to help them do something.
assist 指帮助某人完成某件事。
assure: To assure someone is to tell them confidently that something is true or will happen.
assure 指向某人明确保证某事属实或会发生。
authorize: To authorize an action is to officially give permission for it.
authorize 指正式批准或授权某项行动。
avert: To avert a problem is to prevent it from happening.
avert 指采取措施避免问题或危险发生。
await: To await something is to wait for it to happen or arrive.
await 指等待某件事发生或某物到来。
bind: To bind things is to tie them together or place them under an obligation.
bind 指把事物捆绑在一起，也可指使其受到义务约束。
caution: To caution someone is to warn them about a possible risk.
caution 指提醒或警告某人注意潜在风险。
coincide: When two events coincide, they happen at the same time or match.
coincide 指两件事同时发生，或在某方面一致。
compound: To compound a problem is to make it worse by adding another difficulty.
compound 作动词时可指使原本的问题因新的困难而更加严重。
comprise: To comprise several parts is to include those parts as a whole.
comprise 指一个整体包含若干组成部分。
concede: To concede a point is to admit it is true, often reluctantly.
concede 指承认某个观点有道理，通常带有不情愿的意味。
concur: To concur with someone is to agree with their opinion or decision.
concur 指赞同他人的意见或决定。
confine: To confine something is to keep it within a limited space or range.
confine 指把某物限制在特定空间或范围内。
consent: To consent is to give permission or agree to something voluntarily.
consent 指自愿同意某项安排或给予许可。
constrain: To constrain an action is to limit what can be done.
constrain 指限制可采取的行动或可用的选择。
contemplate: To contemplate a possibility is to think carefully about it.
contemplate 指认真思考某种可能性或方案。
convene: To convene a meeting is to arrange for people to gather for it.
convene 指召集人员召开会议。
coordinate: To coordinate activities is to organize them so they work well together.
coordinate 指协调各项活动，使它们能够相互配合。
curb: To curb something is to control it and prevent it from increasing.
curb 指抑制某种行为、趋势或增长。
deduct: To deduct an amount is to subtract it from a total.
deduct 指从总数中扣除某个数额。
defer: To defer a decision is to put it off until a later time.
defer 指把决定或行动推迟到以后。
depict: To depict something is to show or describe it in a picture or words.
depict 指用画面或文字描绘某个事物。
devote: To devote time to something is to use that time for it with commitment.
devote 指投入时间或精力专门用于某件事。
disclose: To disclose information is to make it known to others.
disclose 指向他人透露或公开信息。
disrupt: To disrupt a process is to interrupt it and prevent it from continuing normally.
disrupt 指打断某个过程，使其无法正常进行。
divert: To divert something is to turn it away from its original direction or use.
divert 指使某物偏离原来的方向或用途。
emphasize: To emphasize a point is to make clear that it is especially important.
emphasize 指特别强调某一点的重要性。
employ: To employ a method is to use it for a particular purpose.
employ 除了表示雇用，也可指为特定目的采用某种方法。
expose: To expose something is to make it visible or reveal it to something else.
expose 指使某物显露出来，或使其接触外部环境。
foster: To foster something is to encourage it to develop or grow.
foster 指促进某种能力、关系或趋势的发展。
fragile: Something fragile is easily broken, damaged, or weakened.
fragile 指容易破损、受损或变得不稳定。
fuel: To fuel a trend is to make it grow stronger or continue.
fuel 作动词时指推动某种趋势或情绪进一步发展。
fulfill: To fulfill a requirement is to do what the requirement demands.
fulfill 指满足要求或履行承诺。
hinder: To hinder progress is to make it more difficult or slower.
hinder 指阻碍进展，使事情更困难或更缓慢。
incline: To be inclined to do something is to tend to prefer or choose it.
be inclined to 指倾向于做某事或持有某种看法。
incur: To incur a cost is to become responsible for paying it.
incur 指因某项行动而产生需要承担的费用或责任。
induce: To induce an effect is to cause it to happen.
induce 指引起或促成某种结果。
invoke: To invoke a rule is to refer to it as an authority or reason.
invoke 指援引某条规则或原则作为依据。
mandate: To mandate an action is to make it officially required.
mandate 指以正式规定要求必须采取某项行动。
notify: To notify someone is to officially inform them about something.
notify 指正式通知某人某项信息。
outline: To outline a plan is to describe only its main points.
outline 指简要概述计划或观点的要点。
overlook: To overlook a detail is to fail to notice it.
overlook 指因疏忽而没有注意到某个细节。
portray: To portray someone is to describe or show what they are like.
portray 指通过描写或表现来呈现某人的形象。
precede: To precede something is to happen or come before it.
precede 指在时间或顺序上先于另一事物。
precipitate: To precipitate an event is to cause it to happen sooner or suddenly.
precipitate 作动词时指促使某件事突然或提前发生。
remedy: To remedy a problem is to correct or improve a situation.
remedy 作动词时指采取措施纠正问题。
retrieve: To retrieve information is to find and bring it back from storage.
retrieve 指从存储位置找回并获取信息。
rigid: Something rigid is stiff or unwilling to change.
rigid 指不易弯曲，也可形容规则或态度缺乏灵活性。
safeguard: To safeguard something is to protect it against damage or loss.
safeguard 指采取措施保护某物免受损害或损失。
saturate: To saturate something is to fill it so completely that little more can be added.
saturate 指使某物达到几乎无法再容纳更多的饱和状态。
streamline: To streamline a process is to remove unnecessary steps and make it more efficient.
streamline 指简化流程、去掉多余环节以提高效率。
terminate: To terminate something is to bring it to an end.
terminate 指正式结束某个过程、合同或活动。
undermine: To undermine something is to gradually weaken it or reduce confidence in it.
undermine 指逐渐削弱某种能力、关系或信任。
utilize: To utilize something is to use it for a practical purpose.
utilize 指为了实际目的利用某种资源或工具。
acute: An acute problem is severe or urgently felt; an acute illness develops quickly.
acute 可指问题严重而紧迫，也可指疾病起病迅速。
adverse: An adverse effect is harmful or unfavorable.
adverse 指带来不利影响或有害后果。
agile: Someone or something agile can move or adapt quickly and easily.
agile 指行动敏捷，或能够迅速适应变化。
attentive: Someone attentive pays close attention to people or details.
attentive 指专心留意他人需求或细节。
beneficial: Something beneficial produces a good or helpful effect.
beneficial 指能够带来好处或积极效果。
compelling: A compelling argument is convincing enough to hold your attention.
compelling 指论证或理由很有说服力，令人难以忽视。
concise: A concise explanation says what is needed in few words.
concise 指用简短的话准确表达必要内容。
constructive: Constructive criticism helps someone improve rather than merely find fault.
constructive 指批评或建议旨在帮助改进，而非单纯挑错。
contingent: If something is contingent on a condition, it depends on that condition being met.
be contingent on 指某事取决于某个条件是否满足。
delicate: A delicate situation needs careful handling because it can easily go wrong.
delicate 可指情况敏感，需要谨慎处理。
original: An original idea is new and not simply copied from something else.
original 指想法具有独创性，而非简单模仿。
pertinent: A pertinent detail is directly relevant to the question being discussed.
pertinent 指细节与正在讨论的问题直接相关。
pivotal: Something pivotal is so important that it can change what happens next.
pivotal 指对后续发展起决定性作用的关键因素。
prevalent: Something prevalent is common or widespread in a particular group or place.
prevalent 指在某个群体或地区普遍存在。
radical: A radical change is very large and affects the basic structure of something.
radical 指改变幅度很大，涉及事物根本结构。
resilient: Someone resilient can recover and adapt after difficulties.
resilient 指遭遇困难后仍能够恢复并适应。
respective: Respective things belong separately to the people or items mentioned.
respective 指分别属于前面提到的各个人或事物。
rigorous: A rigorous method is thorough, careful, and follows strict standards.
rigorous 指方法周密严谨，遵循严格标准。
skeptical: Someone skeptical doubts a claim until there is good evidence for it.
skeptical 指在有充分证据之前对某种说法持怀疑态度。
spontaneous: A spontaneous action happens naturally without being planned in advance.
spontaneous 指行动自然发生，没有事先安排。
stringent: Stringent rules are strict and difficult to satisfy.
stringent 指规定十分严格，难以轻易满足。
thorough: A thorough examination checks all important parts carefully.
thorough 指检查或处理细致全面，不遗漏重要部分。
trivial: A trivial matter is too small or unimportant to deserve much attention.
trivial 指事情微不足道，不值得投入太多注意力。
unprecedented: An unprecedented event has not happened before in a comparable way.
unprecedented 指此前没有类似先例的情况。
urgent: Something urgent must be dealt with very soon.
urgent 指必须尽快处理、不能拖延的事情。
vivid: A vivid description is so clear that it creates a strong mental picture.
vivid 指描述鲜明生动，使人仿佛亲眼看到。
breakthrough: A breakthrough is an important discovery or advance after a difficult effort.
breakthrough 指经过艰难努力取得的重要突破。
circumstance: A circumstance is a condition or fact that affects a situation.
circumstance 指影响某个局面的具体条件或情况。
coherence: Coherence means that ideas or parts fit together in a clear, logical way.
coherence 指思想或各部分之间衔接清楚、逻辑连贯。
controversy: A controversy is a public disagreement about an important issue.
controversy 指围绕重要问题产生的公开争议。
deficiency: A deficiency is a lack of something needed for proper function or quality.
deficiency 指缺少正常运作或达到标准所必需的东西。
dimension: A dimension is a measurable size or a particular aspect of something.
dimension 既可指可测量的尺寸，也可指问题的某个方面。
distinction: A distinction is a meaningful difference between two things.
distinction 指两件事之间有意义、值得辨认的区别。
diversity: Diversity is the presence of many different kinds of people or things.
diversity 指存在多种不同类型的人或事物。
emphasis: Emphasis is special importance given to a word, idea, or action.
emphasis 指对某个词语、观点或行动给予特别重视。
exposure: Exposure is the experience of coming into contact with something.
exposure 指接触某种事物、环境或影响的经历。
inference: An inference is a conclusion reached from evidence rather than stated directly.
inference 指依据证据推导出的、并非直接陈述的结论。
intuition: Intuition is an immediate feeling of understanding without conscious reasoning.
intuition 指不经过有意识的推理就产生的直觉判断。
justification: A justification is a reason that shows why a decision or action is reasonable.
justification 指证明某项决定或行为合理的依据。
priority: A priority is something considered more important or urgent than other things.
priority 指相比其他事情更重要或更紧急、应优先处理的事项。
relevance: Relevance is the degree to which something connects to the subject at hand.
relevance 指某事与当前主题之间的相关程度。
significance: The significance of something is the importance or meaning it has.
significance 指某事具有的重要性或意义。
speculation: Speculation is forming ideas about something without enough firm evidence.
speculation 指在缺少充分确凿证据时进行推测。
tendency: A tendency is a usual direction in which someone acts or something develops.
tendency 指行为或事态发展中反复出现的倾向。
trajectory: A trajectory is the path followed by a moving object or a developing process.
trajectory 指运动物体的路径，也可比喻事态发展的轨迹。
velocity: Velocity is speed measured together with direction.
velocity 指包含方向信息的速度，与只表示大小的速率不同。
versatility: Versatility is the ability to be useful in many different ways.
versatility 指能够适用于多种用途的灵活性。
vulnerability: Vulnerability is the state of being open to harm or attack.
vulnerability 指容易受到伤害或攻击的脆弱状态。
welfare: Welfare is the health, happiness, and general well-being of people or animals.
welfare 指人或动物的健康、幸福及整体福祉。
ascertain: To ascertain something is to find out the facts carefully and make sure they are correct.
ascertain 指通过仔细调查或核实，查明某事的真实情况。
cascade: A cascade is a series of events in which one change causes others to follow.
cascade 指一个变化接连引发其他变化，形成连锁反应。
complementary: Two things are complementary when each adds something the other lacks.
complementary 指两者互相补充，弥补彼此的不足。
compress: To compress something is to press it into less space or reduce its size.
compress 指把某物压缩到更小空间，或减小其体积。
confidential: Confidential information is meant to be known only by people who are allowed to see it.
confidential 指信息只供获准的人知晓，需要保密。
consecutive: Consecutive events happen one after another without a break.
consecutive 指事情连续发生，中间没有间断。
converge: To converge is to move toward the same point or become more alike.
converge 指向同一点靠拢，或逐渐趋于一致。
decent: Something decent is good enough to meet a reasonable standard, though not necessarily excellent.
decent 指达到合理水准、还算不错，但未必特别出色。
discern: To discern something is to notice or recognize it, often when it is difficult to see clearly.
discern 指辨认或察觉某事物，尤其是它不容易看清时。
distort: To distort something is to change its shape or meaning so it becomes misleading.
distort 指使形状或含义发生扭曲，以致失真或误导。
diverge: To diverge is to move in different directions or become less similar.
diverge 指向不同方向分开，或逐渐产生分歧。
eligible: Someone is eligible when they meet the conditions for a benefit, role, or opportunity.
eligible 指符合获得某种资格、待遇或机会的条件。
foundation: A foundation is the basic support that something is built on or depends on.
foundation 指某事物得以建立或持续存在的基础。
hypothetical: A hypothetical situation is imagined for discussion rather than known to have happened.
hypothetical 指为了讨论而假设的情形，并非已知发生的事实。
incidence: The incidence of something is how often new cases occur in a given group or period.
incidence 指某一群体或时段内新增事件或病例的发生情况。
inclined: If you are inclined to do something, you tend to want or be likely to do it.
inclined 指倾向于做某事，或比较可能采取某种做法。
indispensable: Something indispensable is so important that you cannot manage without it.
indispensable 指不可或缺、没有它就难以完成某事。
momentum: Momentum is the force or progress that keeps an activity moving forward.
momentum 指推动事情继续发展、向前推进的势头。
predominant: Something predominant is more common or important than the other things around it.
predominant 指在数量、影响或重要性上占主要地位。
prerequisite: A prerequisite is something you must have or do before another thing is possible.
prerequisite 指做某事之前必须先满足的条件。
provisional: Something provisional is temporary and may change when more information is available.
provisional 指暂定或临时性的，之后可能根据情况调整。
redundant: Something redundant is no longer needed because it repeats or adds nothing useful.
redundant 指因重复或没有额外作用而变得多余。
regulate: To regulate something is to control it using rules or adjustments.
regulate 指通过规则或调节措施来控制某事物。
supplementary: Supplementary material adds extra information or support to the main material.
supplementary 指对主要内容提供补充信息或支持的。
synthetic: Something synthetic is made artificially rather than occurring naturally.
synthetic 指人工制造或合成的，而非自然形成。
uniform: Something uniform is the same or consistent across the parts being compared.
uniform 指各部分保持一致、没有明显差异。
worthwhile: Something worthwhile gives enough value or benefit to justify the effort.
worthwhile 指有足够价值，值得为之付出时间或努力。
notwithstanding: Notwithstanding something means despite it or without being prevented by it.
notwithstanding 表示尽管有某种情况，另一件事仍然成立。
conversely: Conversely introduces a statement that considers the opposite situation or relationship.
conversely 用于引出相反情形或相反方向的关系。
furthermore: Furthermore introduces another point that strengthens what has already been said.
furthermore 用于补充一个进一步支持前述观点的理由。
comparatively: Comparatively means when judged in relation to something else.
comparatively 表示通过与其他事物比较来判断。
relatively: Relatively means to a certain degree when compared with something else.
relatively 表示相对于其他情况而言，达到某种程度。
eventually: Eventually means something happens after some time or a series of events.
eventually 指经过一段时间或若干过程之后，某事终于发生。
accordingly: Accordingly means as a result of the situation, or in a way that fits it.
accordingly 表示因此采取相应行动，或按实际情况作出调整。
likewise: Likewise means in the same way or similarly.
likewise 表示以同样的方式，或类似地。
hence: Hence introduces a result or conclusion drawn from what came before.
hence 用于引出根据前述情况得出的结果或结论。
beyond: Beyond something means farther than it, or outside its limits.
beyond 指超出某个位置、范围或能力的界限。
throughout: Throughout means in every part of a place or during the whole of a period.
throughout 表示遍及整个地方，或贯穿整个时段。
within: Within means inside a place, group, limit, or period.
within 表示处于某个地点、群体、界限或期限之内。
beneath: Beneath means directly under something, sometimes in a figurative sense.
beneath 指位于某物下方，有时也用于比喻。
underneath: Underneath means below something, often covered or hidden by it.
underneath 指在某物下面，常带有被遮住的意味。
aside: To put something aside is to move it away or stop considering it for the moment.
aside 在 put aside 中表示先把某事搁在一边，暂不考虑。
except: Except introduces the person or thing that is not included in a group.
except 用于指出某个群体或范围中被排除的对象。
rather: Rather can express preference or correct an earlier description.
rather 可表示更愿意选择某事，或修正先前的说法。
instead: Instead means doing or using one thing in place of another.
instead 表示不采用原来的选择，而换成另一种做法。
assuming: Assuming introduces a condition that is taken to be true for the discussion.
assuming 用于提出讨论中暂时视为成立的条件。
wherever: Wherever means in any place where something happens or applies.
wherever 表示在任何发生某事或适用某条件的地方。
affluent: Someone affluent has considerable money or material resources.
affluent 指经济宽裕、富有的人或群体。
aftermath: The aftermath is the period and effects that follow a serious event.
aftermath 指重大事件发生后的局面及其后果。
aggravate: To aggravate a problem is to make it worse or more severe.
aggravate 指使问题、疾病或局势恶化、更加严重。
alienate: To alienate someone is to make them feel distant, excluded, or less friendly.
alienate 指使某人感到被疏远、排斥，或不再亲近。
alternate: When things alternate, they take turns or occur in a repeating sequence.
alternate 指不同事物轮流出现或按顺序交替发生。
ambition: Ambition is a strong desire to achieve an important goal.
ambition 指实现重要目标的强烈愿望或抱负。
anecdote: An anecdote is a short story about something that happened, often used to illustrate a point.
anecdote 指关于真实经历的简短故事，常用于说明某个观点。
appraisal: An appraisal is a considered judgment of the value, quality, or performance of something.
appraisal 指对价值、质量或表现作出的评估。
apprehend: To apprehend something can mean to understand it; in law it can mean to arrest someone.
apprehend 可指理解某事；在法律语境中也可指逮捕某人。
aptitude: Aptitude is a natural ability or capacity to learn and perform certain tasks.
aptitude 指学习或完成某类任务的天赋或潜在能力。
attitude: An attitude is the way a person thinks or feels about someone or something.
attitude 指一个人对某人或某事所持的看法和态度。
audit: An audit is a systematic check of records, finances, or procedures.
audit 指对账目、记录或流程进行系统审查。
autonomy: Autonomy is the freedom to make your own decisions or govern yourself.
autonomy 指自主作出决定或自行管理的权力。
auxiliary: Something auxiliary provides additional help to the main system or activity.
auxiliary 指为主要系统或活动提供辅助支持的。
bargain: A bargain is an agreement or something bought for a surprisingly good price.
bargain 指交易或协议，也可以指价格特别划算的商品。
benign: Something benign is not harmful or threatening, even if it seems unusual.
benign 指无害或不会造成威胁的，即使看起来有些异常。
bolster: To bolster something is to strengthen or support it.
bolster 指加强或支持某事物，使其更加稳固。
casualty: A casualty is someone killed or injured in an accident, conflict, or disaster.
casualty 指在事故、冲突或灾害中伤亡的人。
cherish: To cherish someone or something is to care about and value them deeply.
cherish 指深深珍视、爱护某人或某物。
chronic: A chronic problem or condition continues for a long time or keeps returning.
chronic 指问题或状况长期持续，或反复发生。
clarity: Clarity is the quality of being easy to understand or see clearly.
clarity 指表达清楚、容易理解，或视觉上清晰。
coalition: A coalition is a group of people or organizations working together for a shared goal.
coalition 指为了共同目标而结成的联盟。
compassion: Compassion is concern for another person's suffering and a wish to help.
compassion 指体察他人痛苦并希望给予帮助的同情心。
compatible: Two things are compatible when they can work or exist together without conflict.
compatible 指两者能够兼容、共存而不发生冲突。
concession: A concession is something you agree to give up in order to reach an agreement.
concession 指为达成协议而作出的让步。
confer: To confer with someone is to discuss something together; to confer an honor is to grant it.
confer with 指与人商议；confer an honor 指授予荣誉。
conform: To conform is to follow a rule, standard, or accepted pattern.
conform 指遵守规定、符合标准或顺应既定模式。
continuity: Continuity is the state of continuing without interruption or major change.
continuity 指事情持续不断、前后保持连贯的状态。
conviction: A conviction is a firm belief; in law, it can be a finding that someone is guilty.
conviction 指坚定的信念；在法律中也可指有罪判决。
cooperate: To cooperate is to work together with others toward a shared result.
cooperate 指与他人合作，共同实现某个目标。
critique: A critique is a careful assessment that discusses strengths and weaknesses.
critique 指认真分析优点和不足的评论或评析。
curious: Someone curious wants to know or understand more about something.
curious 指对某事充满好奇，想进一步了解。
custody: Custody means having responsibility for someone's care or having someone in legal detention.
custody 指监护照管的责任，或依法羁押某人的状态。
deadline: A deadline is the latest time by which a task must be completed.
deadline 指完成某项任务的最后期限。
debris: Debris is the scattered pieces left after something breaks or is damaged.
debris 指物体损坏后散落的碎片或残骸。
deceive: To deceive someone is to make them believe something that is not true.
deceive 指使某人相信不真实的事情，从而欺骗对方。
defective: Something defective has a fault that prevents it from working as intended.
defective 指存在缺陷，无法按预期正常工作的。
diplomatic: Someone diplomatic handles difficult situations carefully to avoid causing offense.
diplomatic 指处事讲究分寸，善于避免冒犯或冲突。
discreet: Someone discreet is careful about what they say or do, especially with private information.
discreet 指言行谨慎，特别注意保护隐私。
displace: To displace something is to move it from its usual position or take its place.
displace 指使某物离开原来的位置，或取代它。
dissent: Dissent is disagreement with an official or widely held opinion.
dissent 指不同意官方立场或普遍接受的观点。
distress: Distress is severe anxiety, pain, or suffering.
distress 指强烈的焦虑、痛苦或困扰。
dormant: Something dormant is inactive now but may become active again.
dormant 指当前处于休眠或不活跃状态，但以后可能恢复活动。
drought: A drought is a long period with too little rain, causing water shortages.
drought 指长期降雨不足导致缺水的干旱期。
dwell: To dwell somewhere is to live there; to dwell on something is to keep thinking about it.
dwell 可指居住在某地；dwell on 则指反复想着某件事。
eloquent: Someone eloquent expresses ideas clearly, fluently, and persuasively.
eloquent 指表达流畅清晰、富有感染力或说服力。
empathy: Empathy is the ability to understand another person's feelings from their point of view.
empathy 指设身处地理解他人感受的能力。
enroll: To enroll is to officially join a course, school, or program.
enroll 指正式注册参加课程、学校或项目。
ethics: Ethics are principles about what is right or wrong in behavior and decisions.
ethics 指判断行为和决策是非对错的伦理原则。
exaggerate: To exaggerate is to describe something as greater or more serious than it really is.
exaggerate 指把某事说得比实际更大、更严重或更夸张。
exempt: Someone exempt from a rule does not have to follow it or meet a requirement.
exempt 指被豁免某项规定或义务，不必遵守或承担。
exert: To exert effort or influence is to use it actively to achieve a result.
exert 指主动施加力量、努力或影响以取得结果。
exhaustive: An exhaustive study examines a subject as completely as possible.
exhaustive 指调查或研究尽可能全面、不遗漏重要方面。
fatigue: Fatigue is extreme tiredness, often after prolonged effort or strain.
fatigue 指长时间劳累或压力之后出现的强烈疲倦。
fiscal: Fiscal matters concern government money, taxation, and public spending.
fiscal 指与政府财政、税收及公共支出有关的。
flourish: To flourish is to grow, develop, or succeed very well.
flourish 指蓬勃发展、兴旺或取得良好进展。
friction: Friction is resistance when surfaces rub together; it can also mean tension between people.
friction 指物体表面相互摩擦时的阻力，也可指人际摩擦。
futile: Something futile cannot achieve the result you want, however much you try.
futile 指无论如何努力都难以达到目的，因而徒劳。
gratitude: Gratitude is the feeling of being thankful for help or kindness.
gratitude 指因受到帮助或善意而产生的感激之情。
guideline: A guideline is advice or a principle that helps people make decisions or act consistently.
guideline 指指导人们决策或统一做法的原则或建议。
habitat: A habitat is the natural environment in which a plant or animal lives.
habitat 指某种动植物生存的自然环境。
hostile: Someone hostile is openly unfriendly or opposed to another person or idea.
hostile 指明显不友好，或强烈反对某人、某种观点。
humble: Someone humble does not act as though they are more important than others.
humble 指谦逊、不自以为高人一等。
immune: Someone immune to a disease is protected against it; something immune to criticism is unaffected by it.
immune 指对疾病具有免疫力；也可比喻不受某种影响。
inquiry: An inquiry is a question or a formal attempt to discover facts.
inquiry 指询问，也可指为查明事实而进行的正式调查。
intact: Something intact is complete and has not been damaged or altered.
intact 指完整无损，未被破坏或改变。
irony: Irony is a contrast between what is expected or said and what actually happens or is meant.
irony 指预期或字面表达与实际情况、真实含义之间的反差。
legacy: A legacy is something left behind by a person, event, or period for the future.
legacy 指个人、事件或时代留给后世的影响或遗产。
leisure: Leisure is time when you are free from work and other duties.
leisure 指工作和其他义务之外可自由支配的闲暇时间。
liability: A liability is a legal responsibility or debt; it can also mean a disadvantage.
liability 指法律责任或债务，也可以指会造成麻烦的负担。
literacy: Literacy is the ability to read and write; it can also mean knowledge of a particular area.
literacy 指读写能力，也可指对某一领域的基本理解能力。
merit: Merit is the quality that makes something worthy of praise or consideration.
merit 指某事物值得赞赏或认真考虑的优点与价值。
milestone: A milestone is an important point that marks progress in a process.
milestone 指一段进程中标志重要进展的里程碑。
obsolete: Something obsolete is no longer used because it has been replaced by something newer.
obsolete 指因被更新的事物取代而不再使用的。
paradox: A paradox is a statement or situation that seems contradictory but may contain truth.
paradox 指表面矛盾、却可能蕴含道理的说法或情形。
perception: Perception is the way someone notices, understands, or interprets something.
perception 指一个人感知、理解或看待事物的方式。
prestige: Prestige is respect and admiration gained through achievements or reputation.
prestige 指因成就或声誉而获得的威望与声望。
prudent: Someone prudent thinks carefully about risks and consequences before acting.
prudent 指做事谨慎，会先考虑风险和后果。
realm: A realm is an area of knowledge, activity, or authority.
realm 指某个知识、活动或权力所涉及的领域。
reputation: A reputation is the general opinion people have about someone or something.
reputation 指人们对某人或某事所形成的总体评价。
resilience: Resilience is the ability to recover or adapt after difficulties.
resilience 指遭遇困难后恢复或适应的能力。
revenue: Revenue is the money a business or organization receives from its activities.
revenue 指企业或组织从经营活动中获得的收入。
rhetoric: Rhetoric is language used to persuade, especially when style is emphasized.
rhetoric 指为了说服他人而使用的表达方式，常强调修辞效果。
sovereign: A sovereign country has independent authority over its own affairs.
sovereign 指国家拥有独立决定内部事务的主权。
stigma: A stigma is a strong negative social judgment attached to a person or condition.
stigma 指社会对某人或某种状况所附加的负面标签。
suffice: If something suffices, it is enough for the purpose.
suffice 指某事物已足够满足需要。
surplus: A surplus is an amount left over after needs have been met.
surplus 指满足需求后剩余的数量。
trait: A trait is a particular characteristic of a person or thing.
trait 指人或事物所具有的某项特征。
unanimous: A decision is unanimous when everyone involved agrees.
unanimous 指所有参与者都同意、全体一致的。
venture: A venture is a new activity or business that involves risk and uncertainty.
venture 指具有风险和不确定性的创业或新尝试。
verdict: A verdict is an official decision made by a jury, or a final judgment about something.
verdict 指陪审团的正式裁决，也可泛指最终判断。
witness: A witness is a person who sees an event or gives evidence about it.
witness 指目睹事件或提供相关证词的人。
annual: Something annual happens once every year or covers a period of one year.
annual 指每年发生一次，或涵盖一整年的。
artificial: Something artificial is made by people rather than occurring naturally.
artificial 指人为制造的，而非自然产生的。
copyright: Copyright is the legal right to control how an original work is copied or used.
copyright 指控制原创作品复制和使用方式的法律权利，即著作权。
congregation: A congregation is a group of people gathered for religious worship.
congregation 指聚集在一起参加宗教礼拜的人群。
exile: Exile is being forced to live away from your home country, or the condition of living there.
exile 指被迫离开祖国、流亡他乡，或这种流亡状态。
famine: A famine is a severe shortage of food affecting many people for a long time.
famine 指长期严重缺粮，导致大量人口遭受饥饿的灾难。
will: Will is used to talk about the future, express willingness, or describe what someone is likely to do.
will 用于谈论将来、表达意愿，也可以说明某人很可能会怎么做。
must: Must expresses a strong requirement or a conclusion that seems certain from the evidence.
must 表示必须遵守的要求，也可以表示根据证据作出的高度确信的推断。
thought: A thought is an idea or something that comes into your mind when you think.
thought 指思考时出现在脑海中的想法或念头。
part: A part is one piece of a larger whole, or a role someone plays in an activity.
part 指整体的一部分，也可以指某人在活动中承担的角色。
also: Also adds another person, fact, or idea to what has already been mentioned.
also 用于补充之前已经提到的人、事实或观点。
head: The head is the top part of your body; to head somewhere is to move in that direction.
head 作名词指头部，作动词可表示朝某个方向前进。
house: A house is a building where people live; to house people is to provide them with a place to stay.
house 作名词指住宅，作动词可表示为人们提供住处。
left: Left is the direction opposite right; it can also mean something that remains or has been departed from.
left 表示左边，也可表示剩余的事物或已经离开的状态。
nothing: Nothing means not a single thing or no amount of something.
nothing 表示什么也没有，或某物的数量为零。
office: An office is a place where people work, especially doing administrative or professional tasks.
office 指人们从事行政或专业工作的办公场所。
word: A word is a unit of language that has a meaning and can be spoken or written.
word 指具有意义、能够说出或写出的语言单位。
country: A country is a nation with its own territory and government, or a rural area away from cities.
country 指有领土和政府的国家，也可指远离城市的乡村地区。
heart: The heart pumps blood around the body; figuratively, it can mean feelings or the central part of something.
heart 指将血液泵送到全身的心脏，也可比喻情感或事物的核心。
power: Power is the ability to control events, influence people, or supply energy to a device.
power 指控制或影响事物的能力，也可指为设备提供的动力或电力。
believe: To believe something is to think it is true, often without complete proof.
believe 指认为某事是真实的，即使未必掌握完整证据。
between: Between places or people means in the space or relationship that separates or connects them.
between 表示处于两者或多者之间的空间位置或关系。
each: Each refers to every individual member of a group considered separately.
each 强调一组事物中的每一个个体，逐个看待。
ever: Ever means at any time, often in questions, negatives, or comparisons.
ever 表示在任何时候，常见于疑问句、否定句和比较结构。
general: General describes something that applies broadly rather than to one specific case.
general 形容普遍适用、并非只针对某个具体情况的事物。
govern: To govern is to lead a country or organization and make decisions about how it operates.
govern 指管理国家或组织，并决定其如何运作。
home: Home is the place where someone lives and feels they belong.
home 指一个人居住并产生归属感的地方。
live: To live is to be alive or to make your home in a particular place.
live 指活着，也可指在某地居住。
nature: Nature means the physical world, or the basic character of a person or thing.
nature 指自然界，也可指人或事物的基本性质。
near: Near means a short distance away in space, time, or relationship.
near 表示在空间、时间或关系上距离很近。
please: Please makes a request more polite; to please someone is to make them happy or satisfied.
please 用于让请求更礼貌；作动词时表示使人高兴或满意。
real: Real describes something that actually exists or is genuine, not imagined or fake.
real 形容真实存在或货真价实的事物，而非想象或伪造的。
side: A side is an edge or part of something, or one position in a disagreement.
side 指物体的一侧，也可指争论中的一方立场。
person: A person is an individual human being.
whole: Whole means complete, including every part rather than just some parts.
whole 表示完整的整体，包含所有部分，而非其中一部分。
both: Both refers to two people or things together, not just one of them.
both 表示两个都包括在内，而不只其中一个。
close: Close means nearby; to close something is to shut it or bring it to an end.
close 可表示距离近，也可作动词表示关上或结束。
late: Late means happening after the expected or usual time.
late 表示晚于预期或通常的时间。
play: To play is to take part in a game, perform music, or act in a role.
play 指参与游戏、演奏音乐，或扮演角色。
answer: An answer is a reply to a question or a solution to a problem.
answer 指对问题的回答，也可指解决问题的办法。
water: Water is a clear liquid essential to life; to water plants is to give them water.
water 指生命必需的液体水，也可作动词表示给植物浇水。
moment: A moment is a very short period of time or a particular point in time.
moment 指很短的一段时间，或某个特定时刻。
mother: A mother is a female parent or someone who takes on that parental role.
mother 指母亲，也可指承担母亲角色的人。
case: A case can be a particular situation, an example, or a protective container.
case 可表示具体情况、例子，也可指保护物品的盒子或套子。
read: To read is to understand written language by looking at words or symbols.
read 指通过观看文字或符号理解书面语言。
able: Able means having the skill, power, or opportunity to do something.
able 表示有能力、条件或机会做某事。
course: A course is a series of lessons, a direction of movement, or the way events develop.
course 可指课程、行进路线，也可指事态发展的过程。
enough: Enough means as much as is needed, without necessarily being more.
enough 表示数量或程度达到需要，不一定有余量。
foot: A foot is the part of the body used for standing and walking; it is also a unit of length.
foot 指用于站立行走的脚，也是一种长度单位。
full: Full means containing as much as possible or having no room left.
full 表示装满、没有多余空间，也可表示数量充足。
hour: An hour is a period of sixty minutes.
hour 指六十分钟的时间。
next: Next refers to the person, thing, or time that comes immediately after another.
next 表示紧随其后的下一个人、事物或时间。
room: A room is a part of a building enclosed by walls; it can also mean available space.
room 指建筑物中的房间，也可指可用的空间或余地。
city: A city is a large town where many people live and work.
city 指人口较多、居住与工作活动集中的城市。
light: Light makes things visible; as an adjective it can mean not heavy or not dark.
light 指使物体可见的光，也可形容重量轻或颜色浅。
busy: Busy means having a lot to do or being full of activity.
busy 表示事情多、很忙，或充满活动。
different: Different means not the same as something else.
different 表示与其他事物不相同。
friend: A friend is someone you like and trust, often sharing time and experiences with them.
friend 指彼此喜欢、信任并经常分享经历的人。
government: A government is the group of people and institutions responsible for running a country or region.
government 指负责治理国家或地区的人员与机构。
hard: Hard can mean solid and difficult to bend, or difficult to do or understand.
hard 可表示坚硬、不易弯曲，也可表示事情难做或难理解。
receive: To receive something is to get it when someone sends or gives it to you.
receive 指收到别人发送或给予的东西。
talk: To talk is to speak with someone or communicate ideas using words.
talk 指说话、交谈或用语言交流思想。
fact: A fact is something that is true and can be supported by evidence.
fact 指真实成立、能够由证据支持的事情。
fire: Fire is the heat and light produced by burning; to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job.
fire 指燃烧产生的火焰与热光，也可作动词表示解雇员工。
question: A question asks for information or raises something that needs to be discussed.
question 指寻求信息的提问，也可指需要讨论的问题。
sense: Sense is a way of understanding something, a meaning, or an ability to perceive the world.
sense 指对事物的理解、某种含义，也可指感知世界的感觉能力。
less: Less means a smaller amount or degree, usually compared with something else.
less 表示数量或程度比其他事物更少。
letter: A letter is a written message sent to someone, or a symbol used in an alphabet.
letter 指寄给别人的书信，也可指字母表中的字母。
quite: Quite modifies how much something is true; its strength depends on context and dialect.
quite 修饰某种程度，具体是“相当”还是“完全”等要看语境和地区用法。
sure: Sure means feeling confident that something is true or will happen.
sure 表示确信某事属实或将要发生。
voice: A voice is the sound produced when someone speaks or sings; it can also mean an opinion expressed.
voice 指说话或歌唱时发出的声音，也可指被表达出来的意见。
company: A company is a business organization; it can also mean being with other people.
company 指商业公司，也可指与他人作伴。
perhaps: Perhaps means something is possible but not certain.
perhaps 表示某事有可能发生，但并不确定。
poor: Poor means having little money; it can also describe low quality or inadequate performance.
poor 指经济贫困，也可形容质量差或表现不佳。
rest: Rest means relaxation or sleep; the rest means what remains after some has been used or taken.
rest 指休息，也可指已用掉或取走一部分后剩下的事物。
second: Second means coming after first in order; it also names a unit of time.
second 表示顺序中的第二，也表示一秒钟。
body: A body is the physical structure of a living thing or an organized group of people.
body 指生物的身体，也可指有组织的团体。
best: Best describes the highest quality or the most suitable among the alternatives.
best 表示在多个选择中质量最高或最合适的。
business: Business is commercial activity, a company, or a matter that someone is concerned with.
business 指商业活动、公司，也可指某人需要处理的事务。
deep: Deep means extending far below a surface or reaching a high level of feeling or thought.
deep 表示向下延伸很远，也可形容感情或思考深刻。
early: Early means happening near the beginning of a period or before the usual time.
early 表示处于某段时间的早期，或早于通常时间。
pretty: Pretty can mean attractive, or it can act as an informal degree word meaning fairly.
pretty 可形容漂亮，也可作口语程度副词表示“相当”。
half: Half is one of two equal parts of something.
half 指整体平分成两份后的一份。
spirit: Spirit can mean a person's attitude, courage, or a nonphysical part believed to exist.
spirit 可指人的精神、态度或勇气，也可指被认为存在的非物质灵魂。
used: Used can mean employed for a purpose, previously owned, or accustomed to something.
used 可表示被使用过、二手的，或习惯于某事。
often: Often means happening frequently or many times.
often 表示某事经常发生、次数较多。
party: A party is a social gathering, a political organization, or a person involved in an agreement.
party 指聚会、政党，也可指协议中的一方。
strong: Strong means having a lot of physical force or having an intense effect.
strong 表示力量大、结实，也可表示影响强烈。
together: Together means with other people or things in the same place, activity, or group.
together 表示与其他人或事物一起、共同处于某处或进行某事。
history: History is the study or record of what happened in the past.
history 指对过去事件的研究或记载。
along: Along means following the length or direction of something, such as a road or river.
along 表示沿着道路、河流等事物的长度方向。
character: A character is someone's personality, a person in a story, or a written symbol.
character 指人的性格、故事中的人物，也可指文字或符号。
dark: Dark means having little or no light; it can also describe a gloomy mood.
dark 表示光线少或没有光，也可形容气氛阴沉。
dear: Dear can express affection, high value, or a polite way to address someone.
dear 可表示亲爱、珍贵，也可用于礼貌称呼。
indeed: Indeed emphasizes that something is true, confirms a point, or adds emphasis.
indeed 用于强调某事确实如此、确认观点或加强语气。
public: Public describes something open or relevant to everyone, rather than private.
public 指向公众开放或与大众有关，而非私人的事物。
short: Short means not long in length or duration, or smaller than expected.
short 表示长度或时间不长，也可表示不足预期。
story: A story is an account of events, real or imagined, told in words.
story 指用语言讲述的事件，可以真实也可以虚构。
till: Till means until a particular time or event; it can also name a cash drawer.
till 表示直到某个时间或事件，也可指收银抽屉。
human: Human means relating to people; a human is a person.
human 形容与人有关的事物，作名词时指人。
above: Above means in a higher position than something else, or earlier in a piece of writing.
above 表示在某物上方，也可指文章前面提到的内容。
already: Already means that something happened before now or earlier than expected.
already 表示某事在现在之前已经发生，有时含有比预期更早的意味。
easy: Easy means requiring little effort, skill, or difficulty.
easy 表示不需要付出太多努力、技能，或难度较低。
ground: Ground is the earth's surface; it can also mean a reason or basis for a claim.
ground 指地面，也可指某项主张的理由或依据。
least: Least means the smallest amount or lowest degree among several possibilities.
least 表示多个可能性中数量最少或程度最低的。
note: A note is a short written record; to note something is to notice or mention it.
note 指简短记录，作动词时表示注意到或提及某事。
sudden: Sudden describes something happening quickly and unexpectedly.
sudden 形容事情发生得很快、出乎意料。
sound: Sound is something heard by the ears; as an adjective it can mean reliable or sensible.
sound 指听到的声音，也可形容可靠或合理。
free: Free can mean not costing money, not restricted, or available for use.
free 可表示免费、不受限制，或有空可用。
national: National means relating to an entire country rather than one local area.
national 表示与整个国家有关，而不仅限于某个地方。
subject: A subject is a topic of study or discussion, or a person or thing described in a sentence.
subject 指学习或讨论的主题，也可指句子中的主语。
observe: To observe is to watch carefully or notice what happens; it can also mean obey a rule.
observe 指仔细观察或注意到情况，也可表示遵守规则。
alone: Alone means without other people, or done by a single person.
alone 表示独自一人，或由一个人独立完成。
behind: Behind means at the back of something or later than an expected stage.
behind 表示在后方，也可表示进度落后。
drive: To drive is to control a vehicle, or to push a process forward.
drive 指驾驶车辆，也可表示推动某个过程发展。
fight: To fight is to use force against someone, or struggle strongly to overcome a problem.
fight 指与人打斗，也可指努力对抗问题。
minute: A minute is sixty seconds; as an adjective, minute can mean extremely small.
minute 作名词指一分钟，作形容词时可指极其微小。
step: A step is one movement of walking or one stage of a process.
step 指走路的一步，也可指过程中的一个步骤。
command: A command is an order telling someone or a machine what to do.
command 指要求人或机器执行某项操作的命令。
desire: Desire is a strong wish for something; to desire is to want it strongly.
desire 指强烈的愿望，作动词时表示强烈希望得到某物。
ready: Ready means prepared and able to begin or be used.
ready 表示准备妥当、可以开始或投入使用。
deal: A deal is an agreement, or a particular arrangement; to deal with something is to handle it.
deal 指协议或安排；deal with 表示处理某事。
either: Either refers to one of two alternatives; in negative statements it can mean neither one.
either 表示两个选择中的任一个，在否定语境中也可表示两个都不。
fortune: Fortune can mean wealth, luck, or the events that happen to someone.
fortune 可指财富、运气，或发生在某人身上的命运起伏。
important: Important describes something that has a great effect or deserves attention.
important 形容影响大、值得重视的事物。
manner: Manner means a way of doing something or behaving.
manner 指做事或表现行为的方式。
perfect: Perfect means as good, complete, or accurate as possible, without faults.
perfect 表示达到理想的完整或准确程度，没有缺陷。
usual: Usual means normal or happening in the way that is common for someone or something.
usual 表示通常会发生或符合惯例的。
charge: A charge is a fee, an accusation, or stored electricity; to charge can mean to ask a price.
charge 可指费用、指控或电荷；作动词时也可表示收费。
feeling: A feeling is an emotion, a physical sensation, or an impression about something.
feeling 指情感、身体感觉，也可指对某事的直觉印象。
quick: Quick means taking a short amount of time or moving at high speed.
quick 表示完成得快，或运动速度高。
object: An object is a thing; to object is to express disagreement or opposition.
object 作名词指物体，作动词表示反对。
past: Past means an earlier time, or beyond a particular place or point.
past 指过去的时间，也可表示经过某个位置。
press: To press is to push firmly; the press also means news organizations and journalists.
press 作动词指用力按压，作名词也可指新闻媒体。
teach: To teach is to help someone learn knowledge or a skill.
teach 指帮助别人学习知识或技能。
sometimes: Sometimes means on some occasions but not always.
sometimes 表示有时候会发生，但并非总是如此。
sort: A sort is a kind or category; to sort things is to arrange them in groups or order.
sort 指种类，作动词时表示分类或排序。
trouble: Trouble is a problem or difficulty; to trouble someone is to cause worry or inconvenience.
trouble 指麻烦或困难，作动词时可表示给人添麻烦。
count: To count is to find a number by adding items; it can also mean to matter.
count 指清点数量，也可表示某事很重要、算数。
chance: A chance is the possibility that something happens or an opportunity to do something.
chance 指某事发生的可能性，也可指做某事的机会。
immediate: Immediate means happening now, without delay, or directly connected.
immediate 表示立即发生、不拖延，或有直接联系。
plain: Plain means simple or clear, without decoration or complication.
plain 形容简单、直白，没有装饰或复杂之处。
firm: Firm describes something solid or steady, or a decision held with confidence.
firm 形容坚实稳定，也可指态度或决定坚定。
strike: To strike can mean to hit, to come suddenly to mind, or to stop work as a protest.
strike 可指击打、突然想到，也可指通过罢工表达抗议。
address: An address is the location of a place; to address a problem is to deal with it.
address 指地址，作动词时可表示处理问题。
breakdown: A breakdown is a failure of a machine or system, or a detailed division of information into parts.
breakdown 指机器或系统故障，也可指将信息分项拆解后的明细。
bottleneck: A bottleneck is a point where limited capacity slows down an entire process.
bottleneck 指容量受限、拖慢整体流程的瓶颈环节。
causal: Causal describes a relationship in which one event helps produce another.
causal 表示一个事件导致或促成另一个事件的因果关系。
caveat: A caveat is a warning or condition that limits how a statement should be understood.
caveat 指提醒读者注意某项说法适用范围或限制条件的说明。
clarification: A clarification makes something easier to understand by removing uncertainty or confusion.
clarification 指消除疑惑、使某事更加明确的解释。
confound: To confound an analysis is to make its results hard to interpret because other factors are mixed in.
confound 指其他因素混入后，使分析结果难以正确解释。
corroborate: To corroborate a claim is to support it with independent evidence or information.
corroborate 指用独立证据或资料进一步证实某项说法。
residual: A residual is the part or difference that remains after something has been accounted for.
residual 指扣除已解释或已处理部分后仍然剩余的量或差异。
reproduce: To reproduce a result is to obtain it again using the same or a described method.
reproduce 指按相同或描述过的方法再次得到某个结果。
scrutinize: To scrutinize something is to examine it very closely for important details or problems.
scrutinize 指仔细审查某事，留意关键细节或潜在问题。
