he: He is used to refer to a male person or animal who has already been mentioned or identified.
it: It is used to refer to a thing, animal, situation, or idea that is already known from the context.
pron. 它；这件事；这种情况
at: At points to a particular place, time, level, or activity.
prep. 在（某地点、时刻或水平）；参与（活动）
or: Or connects alternatives and means that one possibility, another, or both may apply depending on the context.
me: Me refers to the speaker when the speaker is the object of a verb or preposition.
us: Us refers to the speaker and one or more other people as the object of a verb or preposition.
are: Are is a present-tense form of be, used with you, we, they, and plural subjects.
v. 是；处于（be 的现在时形式，用于 you、we、they 等）
can: Can expresses ability or permission; as a noun, a can is a container made of metal.
情态动词：能够；可以。n. 金属罐
in: In means inside a place or within a period, group, or condition; as an adverb, it can mean entering or being present.
prep. 在……里面；在……期间；处于……之中。adv. 进入；在内
on: On commonly means touching a surface, associated with a day, or continuing in a state or activity.
prep. 在……上；在（某日）。adv. 继续；处于启动状态
by: By can mean near, through a method, done by an agent, or no later than a deadline.
prep. 在……旁；通过……方式；由……；不迟于
as: As can describe a role, make comparisons, or connect events happening at the same time.
prep. 作为；conj. 当……时；adv. 同样地（用于比较）
but: But connects contrasting ideas or introduces an exception to what was just said.
conj. 但是；然而；prep. 除了
say: To say something is to express it in words, aloud or in writing.
say 指用语言说出或表达某件事，可以口头说，也可以写出来。
all: All means every member or part of a group, with nothing left out.
all 指某个群体或整体中的全部成员或部分，没有遗漏。
not: Not is used to make a statement negative or to deny something.
not 用来构成否定句，表示某事不成立或不是这样。
one: One is the number 1; it can also refer to a single person or thing.
one 表示数字一，也可以指一个人或一件事物。
so: So can mean 'to that degree', 'in this way', or introduce a result.
so 可表示“如此、这么”，也可表示“因此”来引出结果。
no: No expresses refusal or disagreement, or means that none exists.
no 可表示拒绝、否定回答，也可表示“没有任何”。
two: Two is the number 2, or a group containing two people or things.
two 表示数字二，也可以指由两个成员构成的一组。
being: Being is the state of existing; it can also mean a living creature.
being 指存在或生存的状态，也可作名词表示生物或生命体。
eye: An eye is an organ used for seeing; it can also mean careful attention.
eye 指用来看的眼睛，也可比喻观察力或关注。
found: To found an organization is to establish it; found is also the past tense of find.
found 作动词可指创立组织；它也是 find（找到）的过去式和过去分词。
love: Love is a strong feeling of affection; to love someone or something is to care deeply about them.
love 指深厚的喜爱或关爱；作动词表示深爱某人或非常喜欢某物。
under: Under means below something, or subject to its control or influence.
under 表示在某物下方，也可以表示受某种控制、规则或影响。
woman: A woman is an adult female person.
young: Someone young has lived only a short time; something young is at an early stage.
young 指年纪小的，也可指事物处于发展的早期。
away: Away means at a distance from a place or moving farther from it.
away 表示离某处有一段距离，或朝远离某处的方向移动。
far: Far means at or to a great distance; it can also mean to a great degree.
far 表示距离遥远，也可表示程度很大。
three: Three is the number 3, or a set of three people or things.
three 表示数字三，也可以指三个人或三件事物组成的一组。
once: Once means one time; it can also mean at some time in the past or as soon as something happens.
once 表示一次，也可指曾经，或作连词表示“一旦”。
die: To die is to stop being alive; an idea or tradition can also die when it disappears.
die 指死亡、生命终止，也可比喻观念或传统消失。
few: Few means a small number of people or things, often fewer than expected.
few 指数量很少，通常暗示比预期少。
large: Something large is big in size, amount, or extent.
large 指体积大、数量多或范围广。
put: To put something somewhere is to move it into a particular position or place.
put 指把某物放到特定位置或地方。
why: Why is used to ask for a reason or explanation.
why 用来询问原因或理由。
here: Here means in, at, or toward the place where the speaker is.
here 表示在说话者所在的地方，或朝这个地方。
saw: Saw is the past tense of see; a saw is also a tool for cutting wood or other materials.
saw 是 see（看见）的过去式，也可作名词表示锯子。
boy: A boy is a male child or young male person.
boy 指男孩或年轻男性。
small: Something small has little size, amount, or importance.
small 指体积小、数量少，或重要性不大。
soon: Soon means after a short time, or earlier than expected.
soon 表示不久之后，或比预期更早。
war: War is prolonged armed conflict between countries or groups.
war 指国家或群体之间持续的武装冲突。
week: A week is a period of seven days.
week 指连续七天的时间。
girl: A girl is a female child or young female person.
girl 指女孩或年轻女性。
arm: An arm is a limb from shoulder to hand; it can also mean a branch or division.
arm 指从肩到手的手臂，也可比喻机构的部门或分支。
cry: To cry is to produce tears or to shout loudly; a cry is a loud call.
cry 指哭泣，也可指高声呼喊；作名词时可表示喊叫声。
law: A law is an official rule that a society or organization must follow.
law 指社会或组织制定并要求遵守的正式规则或法律。
let: To let someone do something is to allow it to happen.
let 指允许某人做某事，或让某事发生。
sit: To sit is to rest with the body's weight supported by a seat or surface.
sit 指坐着，使身体重量由座椅或其他表面支撑。
nation: A nation is a large community of people linked by shared identity or government.
nation 指具有共同身份认同或政治组织的人群，可指民族或国家。
door: A door is a movable barrier used to open or close an entrance.
door 指用于打开或关闭出入口的门。
oh: Oh is an exclamation used to show surprise, understanding, or emotion.
oh 是感叹词，用来表示惊讶、恍然大悟或其他情绪。
words: Words are units of language used to express meaning; it is the plural of word.
words 是 word 的复数，指用于表达意义的词语。
yes: Yes expresses agreement, acceptance, or a positive answer.
yes 表示同意、接受，或作肯定回答。
bad: Something bad is unpleasant, harmful, poor in quality, or not acceptable.
bad 指不好的、有害的、质量差的，或不被接受的。
beauty: Beauty is the quality of being pleasing or attractive to the senses or mind.
beauty 指能让感官或心灵感到愉悦、美好的特质。
morning: Morning is the early part of the day, usually from sunrise until noon.
morning 指一天的早段，通常从日出到中午。
art: Art is creative expression through painting, music, writing, or other forms.
art 指通过绘画、音乐、写作等形式进行的创造性表达。
happy: Someone happy feels pleasure, satisfaction, or joy.
happy 指感到快乐、满足或喜悦的。
money: Money is what people use to pay for goods and services.
money 指用于购买商品和服务的钱或货币。
month: A month is one of the twelve divisions of a calendar year.
month 指日历年中的十二个月份之一。
round: Something round is shaped like a circle or sphere; round can also mean a stage of activity.
round 指圆形的、球形的，也可指一轮活动或比赛。
wife: A wife is a married woman in relation to her spouse.
wife 指相对于配偶而言的已婚女性，即妻子。
wish: A wish is a desire or hope; to wish means to want something to happen.
wish 指愿望或希望；作动词表示希望某事发生。
air: Air is the mixture of gases around the Earth that people and animals breathe.
air 指地球周围、供人和动物呼吸的气体混合物，即空气。
family: A family is a group of people connected by kinship or close relationships.
family 指因亲属关系或紧密联系而组成的家庭成员群体。
number: A number expresses quantity or order; it can also identify something.
number 指表示数量、顺序的数字，也可用来标识某物。
felt: Felt is the past tense of feel; felt is also a soft material made from pressed fibers.
felt 是 feel（感觉）的过去式，也可作名词指毡、毛毡。
american: American describes someone or something from the United States or, in some contexts, the Americas.
American 通常指美国的人或事物；在某些语境中也可泛指美洲。
around: Around means surrounding something, moving in a circle, or approximately.
around 表示在周围、绕着移动，也可表示“大约”。
big: Something big is large in size, importance, or effect.
big 指体积大、重要性高或影响显著。
church: A church is a building for Christian worship, or the religious organization itself.
church 指基督教礼拜场所，也可指教会这一宗教组织。
marry: To marry someone is to become their spouse through marriage.
marry 指与某人结婚，成为其配偶。
night: Night is the dark part of a day between evening and morning.
night 指傍晚到早晨之间的夜间时段。
age: Age is how long someone or something has existed; an age can also be a period in history.
age 指人或事物存在了多久，也可指某个历史时期。
joy: Joy is a feeling of great happiness and delight.
joy 指强烈的快乐、喜悦。
lay: To lay something somewhere is to put it down; lay is also the past tense of lie meaning 'recline'.
lay 作动词可指把某物放下，也是 lie（躺）的过去式。
low: Something low is near the ground or below the usual level, amount, or quality.
low 指位置低，或低于通常的水平、数量或质量。
school: A school is a place or institution where people receive education.
school 指进行教育、教学的学校或教育机构。
smile: To smile is to turn up the corners of the mouth to show happiness or friendliness.
smile 指嘴角上扬以表达高兴或友好的表情，即微笑。
sea: The sea is a large body of salt water, smaller than or part of an ocean.
sea 指大片咸水水域，通常是海洋的一部分或海域。
accord: An accord is an agreement; to accord something is to give or grant it.
accord 作名词指协议、一致意见；作动词可指给予。
chief: A chief is a leader or the person with the highest position in a group.
chief 指领导者或组织中职位最高的人，也可作形容词指主要的。
cut: To cut is to divide or remove something using a sharp tool; it can also mean reduce.
cut 指用锋利工具切割、除去，也可指削减。
dead: Someone or something dead is no longer alive.
dead 指已经死亡、不再有生命的。
horse: A horse is a large animal commonly used for riding or pulling loads.
horse 指常用于骑乘或拉运物品的马。
natural: Something natural exists or happens without being made by people.
natural 指自然存在或发生的，而非人为制造的。
really: Really is used to emphasize that something is true or to a high degree.
really 用来强调某事属实，或表示“非常、确实”。
street: A street is a road in a town or city, usually with buildings along it.
street 指城镇中两侧通常有建筑物的道路、街道。
white: White is the color of snow or fresh milk.
white 指像雪或牛奶那样的白色。
english: English is the language used in England and many other places, or something related to England.
English 指英语，也可指与英格兰有关的人或事物。
father: A father is a male parent.
father 指男性家长，即父亲。
laugh: To laugh is to make sounds or facial expressions showing amusement.
laugh 指因感到好笑而发出笑声或露出笑容。
making: Making is the process of producing or creating something.
making 指生产、制作或创造某物的过程。
politics: Politics concerns government, public decisions, and struggles for power.
politics 指政府事务、公共决策及权力竞争等政治活动。
river: A river is a natural stream of water flowing toward a sea, lake, or another river.
river 指流向海洋、湖泊或其他河流的天然水流。
ship: A ship is a large vessel used to travel or transport goods on water.
ship 指用于水上运输或航行的大型船只。
silent: Someone or something silent makes little or no sound.
silent 指安静的、不发出声音的。
unite: To unite people or groups is to bring them together for a shared purpose.
unite 指使人或团体团结起来、联合起来。
land: Land is the solid surface of the Earth; to land is to arrive on the ground.
land 指陆地、土地；作动词可指着陆或登陆。
captain: A captain is the person in command of a ship, aircraft, or team.
captain 指船舶、飞机或团队的负责人，即船长、机长或队长。
later: Later means after the present time or after another event.
later 指在现在之后，或在另一件事发生之后。
soul: Soul is the spiritual part of a person; it can also mean a person's inner character.
soul 指人的灵魂，也可指内在精神或品格。
game: A game is an activity with rules played for fun or competition.
game 指按一定规则进行的娱乐或竞技活动、游戏。
master: A master is someone highly skilled or in control; to master a skill is to learn it thoroughly.
master 指技艺娴熟者或掌控者；作动词指熟练掌握。
rose: Rose is the past tense of rise; a rose is also a flowering plant.
rose 是 rise（上升）的过去式，也可指玫瑰或蔷薇。
rise: To rise is to move upward, increase, or stand up.
rise 指升起、上升、增加，也可指站起来。
fell: Fell is the past tense of fall; to fell a tree is to cut it down.
fell 是 fall（落下）的过去式；作动词还可指砍倒树木。
french: French describes the language, people, or things associated with France.
French 指法语、法国人，或与法国有关的事物。
king: A king is a male monarch who rules a kingdom.
king 指统治王国的男性君主，即国王。
lie: To lie can mean to rest horizontally, or to say something that is not true.
lie 可表示躺卧，也可表示撒谎，具体含义取决于语境。
sleep: Sleep is the natural resting state when someone is unconscious of much of their surroundings.
sleep 指睡眠，即身体休息、对周围环境感知降低的自然状态。
across: Across means from one side of something to the other.
across 指从某物的一侧到另一侧，或横跨。
island: An island is an area of land completely surrounded by water.
island 指四周被水环绕的陆地，即岛屿。
kill: To kill is to cause a person, animal, or living thing to die.
kill 指使人、动物或其他生物死亡。
member: A member is a person or thing that belongs to a group or organization.
member 指属于某个团体或组织的成员。
occasion: An occasion is a particular time, event, or reason for something.
occasion 指特定时刻、场合或事件，也可指某事发生的机会。
paper: Paper is material used for writing or printing; a paper can also be a written article.
paper 指用于书写、印刷的纸，也可指论文或文章。
possess: To possess something is to own or have it; it can also mean to have a quality or ability.
possess 指拥有某物，也可指具备某种品质或能力。
wall: A wall is a solid vertical structure separating or enclosing a space.
wall 指用于隔开或围住空间的垂直实体结构，即墙。
beautiful: Something beautiful gives pleasure because of its appearance or other qualities.
beautiful 指因外观或其他特质而令人感到美好的。
danger: Danger is the possibility that someone or something may be harmed.
danger 指人或事物可能受到伤害的危险。
distant: Something distant is far away in space, time, or relationship.
distant 指空间距离远，也可指时间久远或关系疏远。
evening: Evening is the period between late afternoon and night.
evening 指下午晚些时候到夜间之间的时段。
faith: Faith is strong trust or belief in someone, something, or a religious teaching.
faith 指对人或事物的坚定信任，也可指宗教信仰。
mere: Mere emphasizes that something is only what is stated, often less important than expected.
mere 强调“仅仅、不过是”，常暗示比想象中小或不重要。
officer: An officer is a person holding an official position in the military, police, or an organization.
officer 指军队、警察或组织中担任正式职务的人员。
peace: Peace is a state without war, violence, or serious conflict.
peace 指没有战争、暴力或严重冲突的和平状态。
remark: A remark is something said or written as a comment about a subject.
remark 指对某话题作出的评论或简短意见。
respect: Respect is admiration for someone or care for their rights and feelings.
respect 指尊重、敬重他人，也包括顾及他人的权利和感受。
road: A road is a route used by vehicles or people for travel.
road 指供车辆或人通行的道路。
success: Success is achieving an aim or getting the result you hoped for.
success 指达成目标或取得期望结果的成功。
group: A group is a collection of people or things considered together.
group 指被视为一个整体的一群人或一组事物。
ago: Ago means a length of time before the present moment.
ago 表示距离现在以前多久，常放在时间短语之后。
bank: A bank is an institution that handles money; a bank can also be land beside a river.
bank 指办理金融业务的银行，也可以指河岸。
black: Black is the darkest color, like a night without light.
black 指最深的颜色，像没有光亮的夜晚一样的黑色。
book: A book is a set of written or printed pages; to book means to reserve in advance.
book 指书籍；作动词表示提前预订。
exist: To exist is to be real or to be present in the world.
exist 指存在、真实地出现在世界上。
fellow: A fellow is another person, especially someone who belongs to the same group.
fellow 指另一个人，尤其是同一群体中的伙伴或同伴。
following: Following means coming after something or happening next; it can also mean supporters.
following 表示接下来的、随后发生的；也可作名词指追随者群体。
particular: Particular means specific rather than general; it can also mean unusually careful about choices.
particular 指特定的、具体的，也可指对选择特别挑剔的。
position: A position is a location, arrangement, opinion, or role someone holds.
position 指位置、姿态、立场，也可指职位。
sight: Sight is the ability to see; a sight can also be something visible or worth seeing.
sight 指视力，也可指所见景象或值得观看的景点。
table: A table is furniture with a flat top; it can also organize data into rows and columns.
table 指桌子，也可以指按行列组织数据的表格。
wind: Wind is moving air outside; to wind something is to turn or wrap it around.
wind 作名词指风；作动词可指缠绕、卷绕，读音不同。
enemy: An enemy is someone who is hostile or opposed to another person or group.
enemy 指敌人，即与某人或某群体敌对的人。
equal: Things are equal when they have the same amount, value, or status.
equal 指数量、价值或地位相同的，即相等、平等。
mine: Mine means belonging to me; a mine is also a place where minerals are extracted.
mine 作代词表示“我的”；作名词表示矿井。
picture: A picture is an image made by drawing, painting, or photography.
picture 指通过绘画或摄影形成的图像、图片。
practice: Practice is repeated activity to improve a skill; it can also mean a usual way of doing things.
practice 指为提高技能进行的反复练习，也可指惯常做法。
promise: A promise is a commitment to do or not do something.
promise 指承诺，即保证做或不做某事。
ride: To ride is to travel on a bicycle, horse, or in a vehicle.
ride 指骑自行车、骑马，或乘坐交通工具出行。
slow: Something slow moves or happens at a low speed.
slow 指移动或发生的速度较低、缓慢的。
spring: Spring is the season after winter; a spring can also be a coil or a source of water.
spring 指春季，也可指弹簧或泉水。
worth: Worth means having a particular value or being deserving of effort or attention.
worth 指具有某种价值，或值得付出努力或关注。
aback: If you are taken aback, something surprises or shocks you unexpectedly.
be taken aback 指因某事出乎意料而感到吃惊或震惊。
abandonment: Abandonment is leaving behind a person, place, or responsibility without continuing to care for it.
abandonment 指抛弃某人、离开某处，或不再履行原本承担的责任。
abate: When something abates, it becomes less strong, severe, or frequent.
abate 指某事的强度、严重程度或发生频率减弱。
abbey: An abbey is a religious building or community where monks or nuns live.
abbey 指僧侣或修女居住的修道院及其建筑。
abbreviate: To abbreviate a word or phrase is to make it shorter, often by leaving letters out.
abbreviate 指通过省去部分字母等方式缩短单词或短语。
abbreviation: An abbreviation is a shortened form of a word or phrase.
abbreviation 指单词或短语的缩略形式。
abdicate: To abdicate is to formally give up an important position or responsibility, especially a throne.
abdicate 指正式放弃重要职位或职责，尤其是退位。
abdomen: The abdomen is the part of the body between the chest and the pelvis.
abdomen 指胸部与骨盆之间的腹部。
aberration: An aberration is something that differs noticeably from what is normal or expected.
aberration 指明显偏离正常或预期情况的异常现象。
abet: To abet someone is to encourage or help them do something wrong or illegal.
abet 指怂恿或帮助他人做不当或违法的事。
abeyance: Something held in abeyance is temporarily stopped until a decision can be made.
in abeyance 指某事暂时搁置，等待进一步决定。
abhor: To abhor something is to hate it very strongly, usually because you find it morally wrong.
abhor 指因觉得某事不道德等原因而深恶痛绝。
abiding: An abiding feeling or quality lasts for a long time.
abiding 用来形容长久持续的情感或特质。
abjure: To abjure a belief or claim is to formally give it up or reject it.
abjure 指正式放弃或否认某种信念或主张。
ablaze: Something ablaze is burning strongly or shining brightly.
ablaze 指某物熊熊燃烧，或发出强烈的光亮。
abnormal: Something abnormal differs from what is usual, typical, or expected.
abnormal 指不同于通常、典型或预期情况的异常现象。
aboard: If you are aboard a vehicle, you are on or inside it while traveling.
aboard 指在船、飞机、火车等交通工具上。
abode: An abode is someone's home or the place where they live.
abode 是较正式或文学性的说法，指某人的住所。
abolish: To abolish a rule or system is to officially end it.
abolish 指正式废除一项规则或制度。
abolition: Abolition is the official ending of a law, institution, or practice.
abolition 指正式废除法律、制度或某种做法。
abominable: Something abominable is extremely unpleasant or morally offensive.
abominable 指极其令人厌恶，或在道德上令人反感的事物。
abort: To abort a process or plan is to stop it before it is completed.
abort 指在某个过程或计划完成之前将其终止。
abreast: If you keep abreast of developments, you stay informed about the latest changes.
keep abreast of 指持续了解某一领域的最新进展。
abridge: To abridge a text is to shorten it while keeping its most important parts.
abridge 指在保留主要内容的同时缩短文本。
abrogate: To abrogate a law or agreement is to formally cancel it.
abrogate 指正式废止法律或撤销协议。
abruptly: If something happens abruptly, it happens suddenly and often unexpectedly.
abruptly 指某事突然发生，往往令人措手不及。
absentee: An absentee is a person who is expected somewhere but is not present.
absentee 指本应到场却没有出席的人。
absolve: To absolve someone is to formally free them from blame or responsibility.
absolve 指正式免除某人的过错指责或责任。
absorbing: An absorbing activity or story is so interesting that it holds your attention.
absorbing 形容活动或故事非常吸引人，让人全神贯注。
absorption: Absorption is the process of taking something in, such as a liquid, energy, or information.
absorption 指吸收液体、能量或信息等的过程。
abstain: To abstain is to deliberately choose not to do or take part in something.
abstain 指有意识地选择不做某事或不参与某事。
abstinence: Abstinence is the practice of choosing to avoid something, especially a pleasure or habit.
abstinence 指主动克制或戒除某种享受、习惯的做法。
abstraction: An abstraction is a general idea separated from particular examples or details.
abstraction 指从具体实例或细节中抽象出来的一般概念。
abstruse: Something abstruse is difficult to understand because it is complicated or specialized.
abstruse 指因内容复杂或过于专业而难以理解。
absurdity: An absurdity is something that is clearly unreasonable or ridiculous.
absurdity 指明显不合情理或荒谬可笑的事物。
abundantly: If something is abundantly clear, it is extremely clear and leaves little doubt.
abundantly 常用于 abundantly clear，表示某事十分清楚、几乎无可置疑。
abusive: Abusive words or behavior hurt, threaten, or mistreat another person.
abusive 指伤害、威胁或虐待他人的言语或行为。
abyss: An abyss is an extremely deep hole or a seemingly endless gap.
abyss 指极深的洞穴，或仿佛深不见底的鸿沟。
academic: Academic work relates to education, research, or study rather than immediate practical tasks.
academic 形容与教育、研究或学术学习相关的事务。
accede: To accede to a request is to agree to it, often after some hesitation.
accede to 指同意某项请求，常含起初有所犹豫之意。
accelerate: To accelerate is to move faster or cause something to happen more quickly.
accelerate 指加快速度，或促使某事更快发生。
acceleration: Acceleration is the rate at which velocity changes over time.
在物理学中，acceleration 指速度随时间变化的快慢，即加速度。
accent: An accent is a way of pronouncing a language that is associated with a region or social group.
accent 指与某地区或群体相关的语言发音特点，即口音。
accentuate: To accentuate a feature is to make it more noticeable or important.
accentuate 指突出某个特点，使它更显眼或更重要。
acceptable: Something acceptable meets the standards needed to be allowed or approved.
acceptable 指达到可以接受或认可的标准。
acceptance: Acceptance means agreeing to receive or recognize something or someone.
acceptance 指愿意接受、接纳或承认某物或某人。
accessibility: Accessibility is how easily people can reach, use, or understand something.
accessibility 指人们接近、使用或理解某物的便利程度。
accessory: An accessory is an extra item used with something else, often to improve its usefulness or appearance.
accessory 指配合主要物品使用的配件或装饰物。
accidental: An accidental event happens unintentionally or by chance.
accidental 指某事并非有意安排，而是意外或偶然发生的。
accidentally: If you do something accidentally, you do it without intending to.
accidentally 指无意中、不是故意地做了某事。
acclaim: Acclaim is strong public praise for someone's work or achievements.
acclaim 指公众对某人工作或成就的高度赞扬。
accolade: An accolade is an award or expression of special praise for an achievement.
accolade 指表彰成就的奖项或特别赞誉。
accommodating: An accommodating person is willing to adjust plans to help others.
accommodating 形容愿意为方便他人而灵活调整安排的人。
accommodation: Accommodation is a place to stay, or an adjustment made to meet someone's needs.
accommodation 可以指住宿场所，也可以指为满足他人需要所作的调整。
accompany: To accompany someone is to go somewhere or do something together with them.
accompany 指陪同某人前往某处或一起做某事。
accompaniment: An accompaniment is something that goes with and supports another thing, especially music.
accompaniment 指伴随或衬托主要事物的东西，尤其是音乐伴奏。
accomplice: An accomplice is someone who helps another person commit a crime.
accomplice 指协助他人犯罪的同伙。
accomplishment: An accomplishment is something important or difficult that has been successfully completed.
accomplishment 指成功完成的一件重要或困难的事情。
accordance: If something is in accordance with a rule, it follows that rule.
in accordance with 指某事符合某项规则或规定。
accost: To accost someone is to approach and speak to them in an unwanted or aggressive way.
accost 指冒然或带有冒犯性地上前搭话。
accountability: Accountability means being responsible for actions and having to explain their results.
accountability 指对自己的行为负责，并有义务说明其结果。
accountant: An accountant is a professional who prepares or checks financial records.
accountant 指编制或核查财务记录的会计专业人员。
category: A category is a group of things that share a defining feature.
category 指按共同特征划分的一类事物。
cite: To cite a source is to mention it as evidence or give credit to its author.
cite 指引用某一资料作为证据，或注明其作者和出处。
collapse: To collapse is to fall down, fail suddenly, or lose strength.
collapse 指倒塌、突然崩溃，或体力不支而倒下。
denote: To denote something is to represent or mean it by a word, sign, or symbol.
denote 指用词语、符号或标记表示某个含义。
partial: Partial means incomplete, or showing preference for one side.
partial 可表示不完整的，也可表示偏袒某一方的。
proceed: To proceed is to continue with an action after a pause or decision.
proceed 指在停顿或作出决定后继续进行某项行动。
cohesive: A cohesive group or text has parts that fit together well.
cohesive 形容群体或文章的各部分紧密结合、协调一致。
counter: To counter an argument or action is to respond in order to oppose or weaken it.
counter 作动词时指通过回应来反驳论点或抵消某种行动。
dependency: A dependency is a situation in which something relies on another thing to work or exist.
dependency 指某事物的运行或存在依赖另一事物的关系。
notation: Notation is a system of symbols used to express information clearly.
notation 指用一套符号系统来清楚表达信息的方法。
circuit: A circuit is a complete path through which electric current can flow.
电路语境中的 circuit 指电流可以沿之流动的闭合通路。
consistency: Consistency means staying the same or following the same standard across cases.
consistency 指在不同情况中保持一致或遵循同一标准。
drift: Drift is a slow, gradual change away from a reference or original position.
drift 指相对于参考值或初始位置发生的缓慢、逐渐的偏移。
inaccuracy: An inaccuracy is a detail or measurement that is not correct or precise enough.
inaccuracy 指不正确或不够准确的细节或测量结果。
precedence: If one thing takes precedence, it has priority over another.
take precedence 指某件事比另一件事享有更高优先级。
onset: The onset of an event is the time when it first begins.
onset 指某个事件或现象刚开始发生的时刻。
cessation: Cessation is the ending or stopping of an activity or process.
cessation 指一项活动或过程的结束或停止。
assessment: An assessment is a careful judgment of a situation or someone's performance.
assessment 指对情况或个人表现进行仔细评估后作出的判断。
incidental: Something incidental is secondary or happens as a minor part of something else.
incidental 指附带的、次要的，或作为其他事情的一小部分出现的。
susceptibility: Susceptibility is how easily someone or something can be affected by an influence.
susceptibility 指人或事物受到某种影响的容易程度。
converse: The converse of a statement reverses the direction of its claim.
在逻辑语境中，converse 指将某一命题的条件与结论交换后得到的逆命题。
optimum: The optimum level is the best possible level for a particular purpose.
optimum 指针对某一目的最合适或最理想的水平。
intricate: Something intricate has many small, complicated parts or details.
intricate 形容具有许多细小、复杂部分或细节的事物。
meticulous: A meticulous person pays close attention to every small detail.
meticulous 形容对每一个细节都十分仔细、严谨的人。
speculate: To speculate is to suggest an explanation without enough evidence to know it is true.
speculate 指证据还不充分时推测某种解释或可能性。
extrapolate: To extrapolate is to use known results to estimate what may happen outside the observed range.
extrapolate 指根据已知结果推算观测范围以外可能发生的情况。
steady: Steady describes something that continues at a fairly constant rate or remains firm and controlled.
steady 表示稳定、持续而没有明显波动，也可形容人镇定或物体牢固。
somewhat: Somewhat means to a limited degree, but not completely or extremely.
somewhat 表示有些、稍微，程度有限，并非非常或完全如此。
mostly: Mostly means for the most part, though not necessarily entirely.
mostly 表示大部分情况下或主要是这样，但并不一定全部如此。
largely: Largely means mainly or to a great extent, with some possible exceptions.
largely 表示在很大程度上或主要如此，可能仍有例外。
mainly: Mainly points to the most important part, cause, or group in a situation.
mainly 用于指出某事最主要的部分、原因或对象。
neither: Neither means not one and not the other of two people or things.
neither 表示两者中的任何一个都不，可作限定词、代词或副词。
supposedly: Supposedly means that something is said or believed to be true, but has not been confirmed.
supposedly 表示据说某事属实，但说话人未必已经核实。
essentially: Essentially describes what is true at the most basic or important level.
essentially 指从最核心、最根本的意义上说，或实质上如此。
nominally: Nominally means in name or by official description, even if the reality differs.
nominally 表示名义上或按正式称谓如此，实际情况可能不同。
previously: Previously means at a time before the present or before another event.
previously 表示在此之前、先前的某个时候。
frequently: Frequently means often, or on many separate occasions.
frequently 表示频繁地、经常在不同场合发生。
occasionally: Occasionally means sometimes, but not regularly or very often.
occasionally 表示偶尔发生，但不经常或没有固定规律。
rarely: rarely 表示很少、难得发生。
seldom: Seldom means rarely; it is slightly more formal than rarely in many contexts.
seldom 表示很少、难得，在不少语境下比 rarely 稍正式。
usually: Usually means in most ordinary cases, but not without exceptions.
usually 表示通常情况下如此，但允许存在例外。
literally: Literally means in the exact, non-figurative sense; in informal speech it can also add emphasis.
literally 通常表示按字面意义、并非比喻；口语中也可用于加强语气。
simultaneously: Simultaneously means happening or being done at the same time.
simultaneously 表示两个或多个事件同时发生或进行。
respectively: Respectively connects items in two lists in the order in which they were mentioned.
respectively 表示两组项目按前后顺序一一对应，即“分别”。
regardless: Regardless means without being affected by a particular condition or consideration.
regardless 表示不受某个条件或因素影响，常用 regardless of。
notably: Notably introduces a particularly important or noticeable example or feature.
notably 用于指出特别值得注意的例子或特点。
sufficiently: Sufficiently means to a degree that is enough for a particular purpose.
sufficiently 表示程度足够，足以满足某个具体目的。
adequately: Adequately means well enough to meet a need or an acceptable standard.
adequately 表示足够好，能够满足要求或达到可接受的标准。
scarcely: Scarcely means almost not, or only just; it can emphasize how small an amount is.
scarcely 表示几乎不、仅仅勉强，突出数量或程度非常有限。
solely: Solely means only or exclusively, with no other factor or purpose involved.
solely 表示仅仅、完全只限于某一因素或目的。
similarly: Similarly shows that another situation has something important in common with the first.
similarly 表示另一种情况在重要方面与前述情况相似。
differently: Differently means in a way that is not the same as another way or situation.
differently 表示以不同的方式，或与另一种情况不一样地。
consistently: Consistently means in the same way over time or across repeated cases.
consistently 表示在不同时间或多次情况下保持一致。
accurately: Accurately means in a way that is correct or close to the true value.
accurately 表示准确地，或与事实、真值相符地。
completely: Completely means in every part or to the full possible extent.
completely 表示完全地、彻底地，没有留下未完成的部分。
partially: Partially means only in part, not wholly.
partially 表示部分地，而不是全部。
somehow: Somehow means in a way that is not known, explained, or specified.
somehow 表示以某种尚不清楚或未具体说明的方式。
somewhere: Somewhere refers to an unspecified or unknown place.
somewhere 指某个不确定或未指明的地方。
anywhere: Anywhere refers to any place at all, often in questions or negatives.
anywhere 表示任何地方，在疑问句和否定句中尤其常见。
elsewhere: Elsewhere means in another place or in other places.
elsewhere 表示在别处、在其他地方。
abroad: Abroad means in or to a foreign country.
abroad 表示在国外或前往国外。
overseas: Overseas means in or to a country across the sea or outside one's own country.
overseas 表示在海外或前往外国；具体用法不一定要求跨海旅行。
moderately: Moderately means to a limited or reasonable degree rather than excessively.
moderately 表示适度地，程度不过分。
rare: Rare describes something that is uncommon or not frequently found.
rare 形容少见、不常出现的事物，也可用于牛排的熟度。
plentiful: Plentiful describes something that exists or is available in a large amount.
plentiful 形容数量丰富、供应充足。
apparent: Apparent means easy to notice, or seeming to be true although that may be misleading.
apparent 可表示明显的，也可表示表面上看似如此、未必确定。
ambivalent: Ambivalent means having mixed or conflicting feelings about something.
ambivalent 表示对某事怀有矛盾或复杂的感情，既赞成又犹豫。
indifferent: Indifferent means not interested or concerned about something.
indifferent 表示对某事不太在意、不关心，态度冷淡。
eager: Eager means very interested in doing or getting something.
eager 表示热切想要做某事或得到某物。
willing: Willing means ready to do something without strong objection.
willing 表示愿意、乐于做某事。
capable: Capable means having the ability or qualities needed to do something.
capable 表示有能力、有条件完成某事。
proficient: Proficient means skilled and able to do something well.
proficient 表示熟练掌握某项技能、能够做得很好。
fluent: Fluent describes speech or language use that flows smoothly and easily.
fluent 形容语言表达流利、顺畅；并不自动等于完全没有错误。
verbose: Verbose describes speech or writing that uses more words than needed.
verbose 形容语言或文字冗长、啰嗦。
biased: Biased describes judgment or information that unfairly favors one side.
biased 形容判断或信息存在偏向，未能公平对待各方。
comparable: Comparable means similar enough in important ways to be meaningfully compared.
comparable 表示在重要方面足够相似，因此可以进行有意义的比较。
identical: Identical means exactly the same in the relevant respects.
identical 表示在有关方面完全相同。
distinctive: Distinctive describes a feature that makes something easy to recognize.
distinctive 形容独特而容易辨认的特征。
preceding: Preceding means coming immediately or generally before something else.
preceding 表示在某事之前出现或发生的。
intermittent: Intermittent means stopping and starting again at intervals rather than continuing steadily.
intermittent 表示间歇性的，时断时续。
continuous: Continuous means continuing without a break.
continuous 表示连续不断、没有中断。
continual: Continual means happening repeatedly over time, sometimes with pauses between occurrences.
continual 表示反复不断发生，中间可能有间隔。
conclusive: Conclusive evidence is strong enough to settle a question or remove reasonable doubt.
conclusive 形容证据或论证足以得出明确结论。
inconclusive: Inconclusive means not giving enough evidence for a clear decision.
inconclusive 表示证据或结果不足以得出明确结论。
volatile: Volatile describes something that changes quickly and unpredictably.
volatile 形容变化迅速且难以预测；在化学中也指易挥发的。
unstable: Unstable means likely to change, collapse, or behave unpredictably.
unstable 表示不稳定、容易变化或出现难以预测的行为。
maximum: Maximum means the greatest amount or level allowed or possible.
maximum 表示允许或可能达到的最大数量或水平。
minimum: Minimum means the least amount or level required or possible.
minimum 表示所需或可能达到的最小数量或水平。
inefficient: Inefficient means wasting more time, effort, or resources than necessary.
inefficient 表示效率不高，花费了不必要的时间、精力或资源。
ineffective: Ineffective means not producing the intended result.
ineffective 表示未达到预期目的、没有起到应有效果。
costly: Costly means expensive or causing a serious loss of resources.
costly 表示代价高昂，不一定只指金钱。
affordable: Affordable means not too expensive for a person or group to pay for.
affordable 表示价格在某人或某群体能够承担的范围内。
expensive: Expensive means costing a lot of money relative to what is normal or expected.
expensive 表示价格较高、花钱较多。
cheap: Cheap means costing little money; it can also imply low quality.
cheap 表示便宜，某些语境也可能暗示质量差。
valuable: Valuable means useful, important, or worth a considerable amount.
valuable 表示有价值、重要或值得珍视，也可指价格昂贵。
worthless: Worthless means having little or no value or usefulness.
worthless 表示几乎没有价值或用处。
trustworthy: Trustworthy describes a person or source that deserves trust.
trustworthy 表示值得信赖的、可靠的。
dubious: Dubious means doubtful, questionable, or not clearly trustworthy.
dubious 表示令人怀疑的、不确定的或不太可信的。
contentious: Contentious describes a subject or person that is likely to cause arguments.
contentious 形容易引发争论的议题，或好争辩的人。
convincing: Convincing describes an explanation or argument that makes people likely to believe it.
convincing 形容论证或解释有说服力，容易让人相信。
persuasive: Persuasive describes speech or reasoning that can change someone's opinion.
persuasive 表示能够说服他人、影响其观点的。
misleading: Misleading means causing someone to form an incorrect impression.
misleading 表示容易使人产生错误印象、具有误导性。
representative: Representative describes someone or something that fairly reflects a larger group.
representative 表示能够较好反映更大群体特征的，也可指代表。
exceptional: Exceptional means unusually good or different from what is typical.
exceptional 表示特别出色，或不同于一般情况的。
typical: Typical means having the features usually associated with a group or situation.
typical 表示具有某类事物通常具有的特征。
ordinary: Ordinary means normal or not particularly unusual or special.
ordinary 表示普通、平常，没有特别之处。
extraordinary: Extraordinary means very unusual, remarkable, or beyond what is normal.
extraordinary 表示非同寻常、格外突出的。
accustomed: Accustomed means familiar with something because you have experienced or done it often.
accustomed 表示由于经常经历或做某事而已经习惯、熟悉。
actual: Actual describes what is real or true, rather than expected, imagined, or officially stated.
actual 表示实际的、真实发生的，与预期、设想或名义上的情况相对。
amount: An amount is the quantity of something, especially something measured rather than counted individually.
amount 指某事物的数量或总量，尤其常用于不可数事物。
classic: Classic describes something recognized as an outstanding or typical example of its kind.
classic 表示经典的、具有代表性的，或公认的优秀范例。
classical: Classical relates to ancient Greek or Roman traditions, or to recognized traditions of art and music.
classical 表示与古希腊、古罗马传统有关，或与古典艺术、音乐传统有关。
compliment: A compliment is a remark that expresses praise or admiration; to compliment is to give such praise.
compliment 指赞美的话；作动词表示称赞、夸奖。
economic: Economic describes matters relating to an economy, money, production, or trade.
economic 表示与经济、生产、贸易或货币有关的。
economical: Economical describes something that uses money, energy, or other resources without waste.
economical 表示节约资源、经济实惠，强调不浪费。
eventual: Eventual describes what happens or becomes true at the end of a process.
eventual 表示经过一段过程后最终发生或形成的。
fewer: Fewer means a smaller number of people or countable things.
fewer 表示可数的人或事物数量更少。
further: Further can mean at a greater distance, or additional and more advanced in degree or development.
further 可以表示距离更远，也常表示进一步的、更多的。
historic: Historic describes an event or place that is important in history or likely to be remembered.
historic 表示具有历史意义、值得载入史册的。
historical: Historical describes something connected with history or events in the past.
historical 表示与历史或过去事件有关的。
insure: To insure something is to protect it financially through an insurance agreement.
insure 指通过保险合同为某事物提供经济保障。
invent: To invent something is to create a new device, method, or idea for the first time.
invent 指首次创造出某种新装置、新方法或新想法。
nominal: Nominal describes something existing in name or officially stated, rather than necessarily in practice.
nominal 表示名义上的、正式标定的，实际情况未必完全相同。
possibility: A possibility is something that could happen or be true.
possibility 指可能发生或可能属实的事情。
principal: Principal means main or most important; as a noun, it can also refer to a school head or an original amount of money.
principal 作形容词表示主要的；作名词还可指校长或本金。
sensible: Sensible describes a person or decision that shows good judgment and practical thinking.
sensible 形容人或决定明智、务实，判断合理。
sensitive: Sensitive describes someone or something that reacts easily or strongly to changes or influences.
sensitive 形容对变化或外界影响反应敏锐、容易受到影响。
gentleman: A gentleman is a man, especially one considered polite or respectful.
gentleman 指男子，尤其指举止礼貌、待人尊重的男士。
religion: A religion is a system of beliefs and practices concerning the sacred or divine.
religion 指与神圣事物或神灵有关的一套信仰和实践。
united: When people or groups are united, they are joined together by a shared goal or purpose.
united 表示人们或群体因共同目标而团结在一起。
blood: Blood is the red liquid that flows through the body and carries oxygen and nutrients.
blood 指在人体内流动、输送氧气和养分的红色液体。
bed: A bed is a piece of furniture used for sleeping or resting.
bed 指供人睡觉或休息的家具。
cold: Something cold has a low temperature; a cold person may also seem unfriendly.
cold 指温度低，也可以形容人态度冷淡。
daughter: A daughter is someone's female child.
duty: A duty is something you are expected or required to do.
duty 指按职责、规定或道义应该做的事。
music: Music is sound arranged in a way that expresses rhythm, melody, or feeling.
music 指通过节奏、旋律等组织起来、表达感受的声音。
quiet: A quiet place or person makes little noise.
quiet 指地方或人发出的声音很小，十分安静。
strange: Something strange is unusual, unexpected, or difficult to explain.
strange 指不寻常、出人意料或难以解释的事物。
suddenly: If something happens suddenly, it happens quickly and unexpectedly.
suddenly 表示某事迅速而出人意料地发生。
taking: Taking can refer to the act of receiving, removing, or carrying something.
taking 可以指拿取、收取或带走某物的行为。
top: The top is the highest or uppermost part of something.
top 指某物最高或最上面的部分。
touch: To touch something is to make physical contact with it.
touch 指与某物发生身体接触，常指用手触碰。
attack: To attack is to act violently against someone or something, or to criticize fiercely.
attack 指对人或物发起攻击，也可指猛烈抨击。
buy: To buy something is to pay money to obtain it.
eat: To eat is to put food into your mouth, chew it, and swallow it.
eat 指把食物放入口中咀嚼并吞咽。
forward: Forward means toward the front or toward a later stage of progress.
forward 表示向前方，也可表示朝着下一阶段推进。
heavy: Something heavy weighs a lot; a heavy workload is unusually demanding.
heavy 指重量大，也可以形容工作负担沉重。
husband: A husband is a man who is married to someone.
husband 指已婚的男性配偶，即丈夫。
news: News is information about recent events or developments.
news 指有关近期事件或新进展的消息。
pray: To pray is to speak or think words directed to a god or other divine being.
pray 指向神或其他神圣存在祈祷。
race: A race is a competition to see who is fastest; to race can mean to move quickly.
race 指比谁最快的竞赛；作动词时也可指快速移动。
satisfy: To satisfy a need or requirement is to meet it adequately.
satisfy 指充分满足某种需要或要求。
send: To send something is to arrange for it to go or be delivered somewhere.
send 指让某物被送往或送达某地。
service: A service is work done to help people or meet a need.
service 指为帮助他人或满足需求而提供的服务。
surprise: A surprise is something unexpected; to surprise someone is to make them feel that way.
surprise 指出乎意料的事，也可作动词表示让某人感到意外。
train: To train someone is to teach them the skills needed for a task.
train 指训练某人掌握完成任务所需的技能。
drop: To drop something is to let it fall, or to decrease to a lower level.
drop 指让某物落下，也可以指数量或水平下降。
declare: To declare something is to announce it clearly or officially.
declare 指清楚地或正式地宣布某事。
dress: To dress is to put on clothes; a dress is also a one-piece garment.
dress 作动词指穿衣，作名词也指连衣裙。
entire: Entire means including every part of something, with nothing left out.
entire 表示包含某物的全部部分，没有遗漏。
front: The front is the part of something that faces forward or is seen first.
front 指某物面朝前方或最先被看到的部分。
none: None means not one person or thing, or not any amount.
none 表示一个也没有，或一点也没有。
patient: A patient person can wait or face difficulties without becoming easily annoyed.
patient 作形容词指有耐心的，能等待或面对困难而不轻易烦躁。
personal: Something personal relates to a particular person or their private life.
personal 指与某个人或其私人生活有关的。
prince: A prince is a male member of a royal family, often the son of a king or queen.
prince 指王室男性成员，通常是国王或女王的儿子。
saying: A saying is a familiar short expression that communicates an idea or lesson.
saying 指表达观点或道理的常见简短说法。
son: A son is someone's male child.
tear: To tear something is to pull it apart or make a hole in it.
tear 作动词时可以指撕开某物或把某物撕出破洞。
travel: To travel is to go from one place to another, often over some distance.
travel 指从一处前往另一处，通常涉及一定距离。
field: A field is an area of land or a particular subject or area of activity.
field 指田地、空地，也可以指某个学科或活动领域。
death: Death is the end of a person's or an organism's life.
death 指人或其他生物生命的终结。
dream: A dream is an experience during sleep or a strong hope for the future.
dream 指睡梦中的经历，也可指对未来的强烈愿望。
living: Something living is alive; living can also refer to the way someone earns money.
living 可指活着的，也可指一个人谋生的方式。
mountain: A mountain is a very high natural area of land with steep sides.
mountain 指海拔很高、坡面通常较陡的自然地形。
piece: A piece is a part separated from or belonging to something larger.
piece 指较大整体中的一部分或一块。
term: A term is a word or phrase with a particular meaning, or a period of time.
term 指具有特定含义的词语，也可以指一段期限。
class: A class is a group of students or a course in which people learn a subject.
class 指一班学生，也可以指教授某一学科的课程。
board: A board can be a flat piece of material or a group of people who oversee an organization.
board 可指平板，也可指负责管理或监督组织的董事会等机构。
boat: A boat is a small or medium-sized vessel used for traveling on water.
boat 指供人在水上航行的船只。
certainly: Certainly means without doubt, or is used to express strong agreement.
certainly 表示毫无疑问，也用于明确表示同意。
comfort: Comfort is a state of ease, or the relief given to someone who is upset.
comfort 指舒适的状态，也指给难过的人带来的安慰。
fly: To fly is to move through the air, usually using wings or an aircraft.
fly 指借助翅膀或飞机等在空中飞行。
political: Political means related to government, public power, or public affairs.
political 指与政府、公共权力或公共事务有关的。
rich: Someone rich has a lot of money; a rich experience can also be full of variety.
rich 指有钱的，也可形容体验丰富多样。
seat: A seat is a place designed for someone to sit.
seat 指供人坐下的位置或座位。
sing: To sing is to make musical sounds with your voice.
sing 指用嗓音发出带有旋律的声音，即唱歌。
soldier: A soldier is a person who serves in an army.
soldier 指在军队服役的军人。
society: Society is a community of people living together under shared systems and institutions.
society 指在共同制度和社会关系下生活的人群与社会。
hang: To hang something is to attach or place it so that it is supported from above.
hang 指把某物悬挂起来，使其从上方受到支撑。
poet: A poet is a person who writes poetry.
poet 指写诗的人，即诗人。
season: A season is one of the main divisions of the year, such as spring or winter.
season 指一年中春、夏、秋、冬等季节。
third: A third is one of three equal parts of a whole.
third 作名词时指整体均分成三份中的一份。
wide: Something wide has a large distance from one side to the other.
wide 指从一侧到另一侧的距离很大，即宽的。
wild: Wild animals or plants live or grow naturally rather than being domesticated.
wild 指动物或植物自然生长、未被驯养或栽培的。
window: A window is an opening in a building, usually fitted with glass, that lets in light or air.
window 指建筑物上通常装有玻璃、供采光或通风的窗户。
bound: If something is bound to happen, it is very likely or certain to happen.
bound 在 be bound to 中表示某事很可能或必然发生。
center: The center is the middle point or main area of something.
center 指某物的中心点或主要区域。
civil: Civil can mean polite, or related to ordinary citizens rather than the military.
civil 可以表示有礼貌的，也可以表示与普通公民而非军队有关的。
health: Health is the condition of a person's body and mind.
health 指一个人的身体和心理健康状况。
imagine: To imagine is to form a picture or idea in your mind.
imagine 指在脑海中形成画面或想法，即想象。
minister: A minister is a government official responsible for an area of policy, or a religious leader.
minister 可以指负责某方面政策的政府部长，也可以指宗教神职人员。
pain: Pain is an unpleasant physical sensation or emotional suffering.
pain 指身体上的痛楚或精神上的痛苦。
private: Something private is intended for one person or a limited group rather than everyone.
private 指只供个人或少数人使用、不向公众开放的。
scene: A scene is the place where something happens or a particular part of a story.
scene 指事件发生的现场，也可以指故事中的某个场景。
secret: A secret is information kept from other people.
secret 指不让他人知道的信息或秘密。
soft: Something soft is easy to press or bend and is not hard to the touch.
soft 指触感柔软、容易按压或弯曲的。
town: A town is a settled community, usually smaller than a city.
town 指通常规模比城市小的城镇。
wood: Wood is the hard material that forms the trunks and branches of trees.
wood 指构成树干和树枝的木质材料。
divide: To divide something is to separate it into parts or groups.
divide 指把某物分成若干部分或组。
plant: A plant is a living organism that usually grows in soil and makes food using light.
plant 指通常生长在土壤中、利用光合作用制造养分的植物。
destroy: To destroy something is to damage it so severely that it no longer exists or works.
destroy 指严重破坏某物，使其不复存在或无法再使用。
dine: To dine is to eat a meal, often in a formal or pleasant setting.
dine 指吃一顿饭，常用于较正式或讲究的场合。
due: If something is due, it is expected or required at a particular time.
due 指某事在特定时间预定发生或应当完成。
future: The future is the time that has not yet happened.
future 指尚未到来的时间，即未来。
glad: Glad means happy or pleased about something.
glad 指因为某事而感到高兴或欣慰。
gold: Gold is a valuable yellow metal used in jewelry and many other products.
gold 指一种贵重的黄色金属，常用于珠宝等制品。
hair: Hair is the thin strands that grow on a person's or animal's skin.
hair 指长在人或动物皮肤上的细丝状毛发。
lady: Lady is a polite or sometimes old-fashioned word for a woman.
lady 是对女性的礼貌称呼，在某些语境中也带有传统色彩。
leader: A leader is a person who guides or directs a group.
leader 指引导或带领某个群体的人。
minutes: Minutes are the written record of what was discussed or decided at a meeting.
minutes 指会议上讨论或决定事项的书面记录。
prison: A prison is a secure institution where people are held as punishment for crimes.
prison 指关押被判刑人员的监狱。
animal: An animal is a living creature that can usually move and respond to its surroundings.
animal 指通常能够移动并对环境作出反应的动物。
pleasure: Pleasure is a feeling of enjoyment or satisfaction.
pleasure 指愉悦、享受或满足的感受。
sail: A sail is a piece of fabric that catches the wind to move a boat.
sail 作名词时指借助风力推动船只的帆。
special: Something special is different from the ordinary in a meaningful or valued way.
special 指有特别之处、因而不同于寻常事物的。
author: An author is a person who writes a book or other written work.
author 指书籍或其他文字作品的作者。
beat: To beat someone in a competition is to win against them; beat can also mean strike repeatedly.
beat 指在比赛中击败某人，也可指反复敲击。
blue: Blue is a color like a clear sky; feeling blue can also mean feeling sad.
blue 指像晴朗天空一样的蓝色；feel blue 也可指心情低落。
building: A building is a structure with walls and a roof, used as a home or for other activities.
building 指有墙壁和屋顶、供居住或其他活动使用的建筑物。
delight: Delight is great pleasure; to delight someone is to give them that pleasure.
delight 指极大的快乐，作动词时指使某人非常高兴。
dog: A dog is an animal commonly kept as a pet or trained to help people.
dog 指常被当作宠物饲养或训练来协助人类的狗。
drink: To drink is to take liquid into your mouth and swallow it.
drink 指把液体送入口中并吞下，即喝。
excite: To excite someone is to make them feel enthusiastic, eager, or emotionally stirred.
excite 指使某人感到兴奋、期待或情绪激动。
industry: An industry is a group of businesses that make similar products or offer similar services.
industry 指生产相似产品或提供相似服务的企业所构成的行业。
red: Red is the color of blood or ripe strawberries.
red 指像鲜血或成熟草莓那样的红色。
repeat: To repeat something is to say, do, or happen again.
repeat 指再次说出、做出或发生某事。
wrong: Something wrong is incorrect, unsuitable, or morally unacceptable.
wrong 指错误、不合适，或在道德上不可接受的。
connect: To connect things is to join them or establish a link between them.
connect 指把事物连接起来，或在它们之间建立联系。
bright: Something bright gives a lot of light; a bright person is also quick to understand.
bright 指光线明亮，也可形容人理解力强、聪明。
camp: To camp is to stay outdoors in a temporary shelter, often a tent.
camp 指在户外临时住所（通常是帐篷）里住宿。
cost: The cost of something is the money needed to buy or obtain it.
cost 指购买或获得某物所需要的钱。
crowd: A crowd is a large number of people gathered in one place.
crowd 指聚集在同一地点的大量人群。
foreign: Foreign means related to another country rather than your own.
foreign 指与本国以外的国家有关的。
garden: A garden is an area where plants, flowers, or vegetables are grown.
garden 指种植植物、花卉或蔬菜的园地。
mark: A mark is a sign, symbol, or trace left on a surface.
mark 指留在表面上的记号、符号或痕迹。
military: Military means related to armed forces or their activities.
military 指与军队或其活动有关的。
paint: Paint is a colored liquid used to cover or decorate a surface.
paint 作名词时指涂在表面、用于着色或装饰的涂料。
print: To print is to produce words or pictures on paper or another surface.
print 作动词时指把文字或图像印在纸张等表面上。
single: Single means one, or not joined with others; it can also mean unmarried.
single 指单个的、未与其他事物结合的，也可以指未婚的。
star: A star is a large glowing ball of gas in space, seen as a point of light in the sky.
star 指宇宙中发光的巨大气体球，在夜空中看起来像光点。
vote: A vote is an expression of a person's choice in an election or decision.
vote 指在选举或集体决策中表达的选择或投票。
warm: Something warm has a comfortably high temperature without being very hot.
warm 指温度较高、令人舒适，但并不十分烫的。
finish: To finish something is to complete it or bring it to an end.
finish 指完成某事，或让某事结束。
affair: An affair is an event, matter, or situation; it can also mean a secret romantic relationship.
affair 可以指事件或事务，也可以指秘密的恋爱关系。
grace: Grace is smooth, attractive movement or a quality of kindness and dignity.
grace 指优美流畅的动作，也可以指仁慈、庄重的气质。
meeting: A meeting is a planned gathering of people to discuss or decide something.
meeting 指人们为讨论或决定事情而事先安排的聚会。
relation: A relation is a connection or association between people, facts, or things.
relation 指人、事实或事物之间的联系或关系。
tone: Tone is the quality of a sound or the attitude conveyed by someone's words.
tone 指声音的音色，也可指言语传达出的态度或语气。
utter: Utter is an adjective meaning complete or absolute, often before negative nouns.
utter 作形容词时表示完全的、彻底的，常修饰负面名词。
bird: A bird is an animal with feathers, two legs, and usually wings for flying.
bird 指长有羽毛、两条腿，通常有翅膀的鸟类。
cross: To cross something is to move from one side of it to the other.
cross 作动词时指从某物的一侧穿越到另一侧。
ear: An ear is the organ used for hearing and helping maintain balance.
ear 指用于听觉、也有助于保持平衡的耳朵。
fast: Fast means moving, happening, or working at high speed.
fast 表示移动、发生或运转速度快。
glory: Glory is great honor, praise, or impressive beauty.
glory 指极大的荣耀、赞誉，或令人赞叹的壮美。
lip: A lip is one of the two soft edges of the mouth.
lip 指嘴巴上下两片柔软的唇之一。
outside: Outside means beyond the limits or outer surface of a place or thing.
outside 指在某个地方或事物的边界、外表面之外。
queen: A queen is a female monarch or the wife of a king.
queen 指女性君主，或国王的妻子。
serious: Something serious is important, worrying, or not intended as a joke.
serious 指重要、令人担忧，或并非开玩笑的。
shot: A shot can be a single attempt, an act of firing, or a photograph.
shot 可以指一次尝试、一次射击，也可以指一张照片。
weak: Something weak lacks strength, power, or effectiveness.
weak 指缺乏力量、权势或效力的。
whatever: Whatever can mean anything at all, or it can emphasize that the choice does not matter.
whatever 可以表示无论什么，也可强调选择什么都无所谓。
youth: Youth is the period of life between childhood and adulthood, or young people as a group.
youth 指从童年到成年的年轻时期，也可以指年轻人群体。
anger: Anger is a strong feeling of displeasure or hostility.
anger 指强烈的不满或愤怒情绪。
beginning: The beginning is the first part of an event, process, or period.
beginning 指事件、过程或一段时期的开端。
below: Below means at a lower level or position than something else.
below 表示处于另一事物之下或更低的位置。
bit: A bit is a small amount or part of something.
bit 指某物的一小部分或少量。
lower: To lower something is to move it down or reduce its level.
lower 指把某物向下移动，或降低其程度。
mouth: The mouth is the part of the face used for eating, speaking, and breathing.
mouth 指面部用于吃东西、说话和呼吸的嘴。
safe: Someone or something safe is protected from danger or harm.
safe 指某人或某物受到保护、没有危险。
shoulder: A shoulder is the part of the body between the neck and the upper arm.
shoulder 指颈部与上臂之间的肩膀。
silence: Silence is the absence of sound, or a period when no one speaks.
silence 指没有声音，或无人说话的一段时间。
summer: Summer is the warmest season of the year in many regions.
summer 指许多地区一年中最暖和的季节。
wound: A wound is an injury that damages the skin or other tissue.
wound 指使皮肤或其他组织受损的伤口。
admire: To admire someone or something is to respect or appreciate them greatly.
admire 指非常尊重或欣赏某人、某事物。
blow: To blow is to make air move, or to send something away by moving air.
blow 指吹动空气，或用气流把某物吹走。
brother: A brother is someone's male sibling.
conscious: A conscious person is awake and aware of what is happening.
conscious 指神志清醒、能感知周围发生事情的。
critic: A critic is a person who judges and comments on art, ideas, or other work.
critic 指评价和评论艺术、观点或其他作品的人。
exact: Something exact is accurate in every detail.
exact 指在各个细节上都准确无误的。
glance: To glance at something is to look at it quickly.
glance 指快速地看某物一眼。
immediately: Immediately means at once, without waiting.
immediately 指立即、马上，不作等待。
moral: A moral is a lesson about right and wrong; moral can also mean related to ethics.
moral 作名词指关于是非对错的教训，作形容词指与道德有关的。
recent: Something recent happened or appeared not long ago.
recent 指不久前发生或出现的。
science: Science is the systematic study of the natural world using observation and evidence.
science 指通过观察和证据系统研究自然世界的科学。
supply: To supply something is to provide it where it is needed.
supply 指在需要的地方提供某物。
sweet: Something sweet has a taste like sugar; sweet can also describe kindness.
sweet 指有糖一样的甜味，也可以形容人亲切温柔。
various: Various means several different kinds or examples of something.
various 表示某物有若干不同种类或实例。
tree: A tree is a tall plant with a woody trunk and branches.
tree 指具有木质树干和树枝的高大植物。
active: Someone or something active is doing things, moving, or working.
active 指正在活动、运动或发挥作用的。
broken: Something broken is damaged or divided into pieces and no longer intact.
broken 指某物受损或裂成几块、不再完整。
careful: A careful person pays attention to avoid mistakes or danger.
careful 指做事留心，以避免错误或危险。
guard: To guard someone or something is to protect them from harm or danger.
guard 作动词时指保护某人或某物免受伤害、危险。
impress: To impress someone is to make them feel admiration or respect.
impress 指使某人产生赞赏或敬佩之情。
individual: An individual is a single person or separate thing.
individual 指单个的人或独立的事物。
instant: An instant is a very short period of time.
instant 指极短的一段时间，即瞬间。
quarter: A quarter is one of four equal parts of a whole.
quarter 指整体均分成四份中的一份。
south: South is the direction opposite north.
south 指与北方相反的方向，即南方。
spot: A spot is a particular small place or mark; to spot something is to notice it.
spot 指某个小地点或斑点；作动词时指发现某物。
leaf: A leaf is the usually flat green part of a plant that grows from a stem or branch.
leaf 指长在茎或枝上的叶片，通常扁平且呈绿色。
appearance: Appearance is how someone or something looks.
appearance 指某人或某物的外观、样子。
circle: A circle is a round shape whose points are all the same distance from its center.
circle 指圆周上所有点到圆心距离相等的圆形。
confident: Someone confident believes in their abilities or is sure of something.
confident 指对自己能力有信心，或对某事有把握。
consequent: Something consequent happens as a result of something else.
consequent 指某事由另一件事引起、随之发生的。
crime: A crime is an act that breaks the law and can be punished.
crime 指违反法律且可能受到惩罚的行为。
grave: A grave is a place where a dead person is buried; grave can also mean very serious.
grave 作名词指坟墓，作形容词还可指十分严重的。
speech: Speech is spoken language, or a formal talk given to an audience.
speech 指口头语言，也可指面向听众发表的演讲。
title: A title is the name of a book or work, or a word that identifies a person's role.
title 指书籍或作品的名称，也可以指说明某人身份的头衔。
abandon: To abandon something is to leave it behind or stop supporting it completely.
abandon 指彻底抛弃某物，或完全停止支持某项计划或想法。
correlate: Two quantities correlate when they tend to change together in a related way.
correlate 指两个量在变化上呈现关联趋势，但不必然互为因果。
deduce: To deduce something is to reach a conclusion by reasoning from known facts.
deduce 指根据已知事实，通过推理得出结论。
indian: Indian describes a person or thing from India; it can also be a noun for someone from India.
Indian 指来自印度的人或事物，作名词时也可指印度人。
british: British describes people or things connected with the United Kingdom.
British 指与英国或英国人有关的。
german: German describes people, language, or things associated with Germany.
German 指与德国、德国人或德语有关的。
bill: A bill is a statement of money owed, a proposed law, or a banknote in American English.
bill 可以指账单、法案草案，在美式英语里也可以指纸币。
century: A century is a period of one hundred years.
century 指一百年的时间，即一个世纪。
elect: To elect someone is to choose them by voting; it can also mean to choose a course of action.
elect 指通过投票选出某人，也可以表示选择某种做法。
escape: To escape is to get away from danger, confinement, or an unpleasant situation.
escape 指从危险、束缚或不愉快的处境中脱离。
food: Food is what people or animals eat to obtain energy and nutrients.
food 指人或动物为获取能量和营养而吃的食物。
official: Official means approved by an authority; an official is a person with an official position.
official 作形容词指得到正式认可的，作名词指担任公职或职务的人。
social: Social relates to people and their relationships or activities together.
social 指与人际关系、社会生活或共同活动有关的。
battle: A battle is a fight between opposing forces; it can also mean a difficult struggle.
battle 指交战，也可以比喻艰难的斗争。
courage: Courage is the ability to face fear, danger, or difficulty without giving up.
courage 指面对恐惧、危险或困难时仍能坚持的勇气。
length: Length is the distance from one end to the other, or how long something lasts.
length 指物体两端之间的长度，也可以指某事持续的时间。
market: A market is a place or system for buying and selling goods and services.
market 指买卖商品或服务的场所，也可以指市场体系。
noble: Noble means morally admirable or associated with a high hereditary social rank.
noble 指品格高尚的，也可以指与世袭贵族身份有关的。
seven: Seven is the number that comes after six and before eight.
seven 指六之后、八之前的数字七。
slave: A slave is someone held in slavery and denied personal freedom.
slave 指被奴役、失去人身自由的人。
exclaim: To exclaim is to say something suddenly and strongly because of emotion.
exclaim 指因强烈情绪而突然大声说出某句话。
slight: Something slight is small or not very serious; to slight a person is to treat them as unimportant.
slight 作形容词指轻微的，作动词指轻视或怠慢某人。
standing: Standing can mean a person's reputation or position within a group.
standing 可以指某人在群体中的地位或声望。
servant: A servant is someone employed to do domestic tasks for another person.
servant 指受雇为别人做家务等事务的人。
article: An article is a written piece in a publication; in grammar, a and the are articles.
article 可以指刊物中的文章；在语法中也指冠词。
compose: To compose is to create music or writing, or to form a whole from parts.
compose 指创作音乐、文字，也可以指由各部分组成整体。
dance: To dance is to move rhythmically to music; a dance is also such an activity.
dance 指随音乐有节奏地移动身体，也可以指舞蹈活动。
dare: To dare is to have the courage to do something risky or challenging.
dare 指敢于做有风险或有挑战性的事。
degree: A degree is an amount or level, a unit of temperature or angle, or an academic qualification.
degree 指程度、温度或角度的单位，也可以指学位。
fresh: Fresh describes something new, recently produced, or not stale.
fresh 指新鲜的、新做出来的或未变质的。
honor: Honor is respect or recognition; to honor someone is to show that respect.
honor 指尊重或荣誉，作动词时指向某人表达敬意。
impossible: Something impossible cannot be done or cannot be true.
impossible 指不可能完成或不可能属实的。
main: Main describes the most important or central part of something.
main 指某事物最主要或最核心的部分。
native: Native can describe someone born in a place or something naturally occurring there.
native 可以指某地土生土长的人或自然生长于当地的事物。
pleasant: Something pleasant is enjoyable or gives a good feeling.
pleasant 指令人愉快、感觉舒适的。
problem: A problem is a difficulty that needs attention or a question that needs solving.
problem 指需要处理的困难，或需要解决的问题。
slowly: Slowly means at a low speed or taking a long time.
slowly 表示速度缓慢，或花费较长时间。
troop: A troop is a group of soldiers or, in some contexts, another organized group.
troop 指一队士兵，在某些语境下也可以指其他有组织的群体。
burn: To burn is to be on fire or be damaged by heat; it can also mean to use fuel.
burn 指燃烧、被热灼伤，也可以表示消耗燃料。
chapter: A chapter is a numbered or named section of a book.
earth: Earth is the planet we live on; earth can also mean soil or ground.
Earth 指我们居住的地球，小写时 earth 也可以指泥土或地面。
finally: Finally means at the end, after some time or after other events.
finally 表示经过一段时间或其他事情之后，终于、最后发生。
frequent: Something frequent happens often or at short intervals.
frequent 指某事经常发生，或两次发生之间的间隔很短。
gentle: A gentle person or action is kind, mild, and not rough.
gentle 指人或动作温柔、轻缓，不粗暴。
inquire: To inquire is to ask for information or investigate something.
inquire 指询问信息，或对某事展开调查。
lot: A lot can be a piece of land, a group of things, or an informal expression meaning many.
lot 可以指一块地、一批物品，也常出现在表示大量的 a lot of 中。
memory: Memory is the ability to remember things or something remembered from the past.
memory 指记忆能力，也可以指过去留下的某段回忆。
pure: Something pure is not mixed with other substances, or is free from contamination.
pure 指不掺杂其他物质的，或没有受到污染的。
roll: To roll is to turn over repeatedly or move on wheels; a roll is also a small round piece of bread.
roll 指滚动或靠轮子移动，也可以指小圆面包。
sharp: Something sharp has a cutting edge or point; it can also describe a sudden or strong change.
sharp 指锋利、尖锐的，也可以形容突然或剧烈的变化。
wise: Someone wise makes good judgments based on knowledge and experience.
wise 指能够凭知识和经验作出明智判断的。
chair: A chair is a seat, usually with a back; a chair can also be the person leading a meeting.
chair 指椅子，也可以指主持会议的人。
color: Color is the appearance of light reflected by things; the British spelling is colour.
color 指物体呈现的颜色；英式英语通常拼作 colour。
edit: To edit writing or media is to revise and prepare it for use or publication.
edit 指修改文字或媒体内容，使之适合使用或发表。
extreme: Something extreme is very great in degree or far from what is usual.
extreme 指程度非常高，或远远超出通常范围的。
ill: Someone ill is unwell or suffering from disease.
ill 指身体不适或患病。
presence: Presence is the state of being somewhere, or the noticeable effect of someone's being there.
presence 指在场的状态，也可以指某人在场时产生的明显影响。
space: Space is an empty area or room; it can also mean the vast region beyond Earth.
space 指空地或空间，也可以指地球以外的宇宙空间。
winter: Winter is the cold season between autumn and spring.
winter 指秋季与春季之间寒冷的冬季。
afraid: Someone afraid feels fear about something.
afraid 指对某事感到害怕或恐惧。
companion: A companion is someone who travels, spends time, or shares activities with another person.
companion 指与某人同行、相处或共同活动的伙伴。
dinner: Dinner is a main meal, usually eaten in the evening in many cultures.
dinner 指一天中的一顿正餐，在许多地区通常是晚餐。
dry: Something dry has little or no moisture; to dry is to remove moisture.
dry 指缺少水分、干燥的，作动词时指使其变干。
hot: Something hot has a high temperature; it can also describe something fashionable or intense.
hot 指温度高，也可以形容流行或激烈的事物。
rapid: Something rapid happens or moves very quickly.
rapid 指发生或移动速度很快的。
suit: A suit is a matching set of formal clothes; to suit means to be appropriate for someone.
suit 指成套的正式服装，作动词时指适合某人。
total: A total is the complete amount; total can also mean complete or entire.
total 作名词指总量，作形容词指全部的、完全的。
ancient: Something ancient belongs to a very distant past.
ancient 指属于遥远过去的、古老的。
car: A car is a road vehicle, usually with four wheels, used to carry people.
car 指通常有四个轮子的道路机动车，主要用来载人。
middle: The middle is the part equally distant from the ends or edges.
middle 指与两端或边缘距离大致相等的中间部分。
similar: Things are similar when they share important features but are not exactly the same.
similar 指事物在重要特征上相似，但不完全相同。
stock: Stock can mean goods kept for sale, shares in a company, or an available supply.
stock 可以指存货、公司股票，或可供使用的储备。
straight: Something straight has no bend; it can also mean direct or honest.
straight 指没有弯曲的，也可以表示直接的或坦率的。
cast: To cast can mean to choose actors, throw something, or form an object in a mould.
cast 可指选角、投掷，或用模具铸造物品。
corner: A corner is where two edges or sides meet.
corner 指两条边或两个侧面相接的角落。
noise: Noise is unwanted sound or interference that can make a useful signal harder to detect.
noise 指干扰听觉或测量的无用声音或杂讯，会使有效信号更难辨认。
decisive: A decisive action settles an issue, or strongly determines what happens next.
decisive 指能解决问题或对后续结果起决定作用的。
blunt: Something blunt has no sharp edge; a blunt remark is unusually direct.
blunt 可指物体不锋利，也可以指话语过于直率、不加修饰。
rough: A rough surface is uneven; a rough estimate is only approximate.
rough 可以指表面粗糙、不平整，也可以指估计粗略、并不精确。
steep: A steep slope rises or falls sharply; a steep increase is unusually large.
steep 指坡度很陡，也可以形容价格或数量急剧上升。
persistent: Something persistent continues despite obstacles or lasts longer than expected.
persistent 指某种行为坚持不懈，或某种状态持续存在、难以消除。
transient: Something transient lasts only a short time and then disappears.
transient 指短暂存在、很快消失的，而不是长期持续的。
local: Something local belongs to or affects a particular nearby area rather than a wider region.
local 指属于、发生于或影响某个具体地区，而非更大范围的。
global: Something global involves the whole world or an entire system rather than one part.
global 指涉及全世界或整个系统，而不仅是某个局部。
remote: Something remote is far away, or can be operated without being physically present.
remote 指距离遥远的，也可以指无需身处现场就能操作的。
broad: Something broad is wide or covers many topics, people, or possibilities.
broad 指物理上宽阔，也可以表示涵盖范围广泛。
narrow: Something narrow is not wide, or is limited to a small range or specific issue.
narrow 指宽度小、狭窄，也可以指范围或关注点有限。
fierce: Something fierce is very strong, intense, or aggressive.
fierce 指强烈、激烈或凶猛的。
mild: Something mild is gentle or not strong, severe, or extreme.
mild 指温和、不强烈或程度不严重的。
fare: A fare is the price paid for a trip on public transport.
fare 指乘坐公共交通工具所支付的票价。
enrich: To enrich something is to make it better, more meaningful, or more varied.
enrich 指使内容、体验或环境更加丰富、有价值。
postulate: To postulate something is to put it forward as an assumption for reasoning or study.
postulate 指提出一个假定，作为推理或研究的出发点。
posit: To posit an idea is to propose it as something to consider or reason from.
posit 指提出某个观点或假设，供讨论或推理。
sympathetic: Someone sympathetic understands another person's difficulties and shows concern.
sympathetic 指理解他人的困难，并表现出关切与同情。
efficacy: Efficacy is how well a treatment, method, or intervention produces its intended effect.
efficacy 指治疗、方法或干预达到预期效果的能力或有效性。
competence: Competence is the ability and knowledge needed to perform a task satisfactorily.
competence 指胜任某项任务所需的能力和知识。
retrospective: A retrospective view looks back at events that have already happened.
retrospective 指回顾过去事件、根据已发生情况进行的。
oversight: An oversight can be an accidental failure to notice something; it can also mean supervision.
oversight 可指疏忽、遗漏，也可指监督或监管。
outlet: An outlet is a place to sell goods, a way to express feelings, or a point for electricity or flow.
outlet 可以指销售网点、情感宣泄渠道，也可以指电源插座或出口。
income: Income is money received from work, business, investments, or other sources.
income 指来自工作、经营、投资等来源的收入。
precedent: A precedent is an earlier example or decision used as a guide for a later one.
precedent 指可供后来类似情况参照的先例或既有裁决。
preclude: To preclude something is to prevent it from being possible or happening.
preclude 指使某事无法发生，或排除某种可能性。
procure: To procure something is to obtain it, often through an organized or formal process.
procure 指通过采购或正式程序获得某物。
purchase: To purchase something is to buy it; a purchase is something bought.
purchase 作动词指购买，作名词指购买行为或购得的物品。
sanction: A sanction can be an official penalty, or an official approval of an action.
sanction 既可以指官方制裁或处罚，也可以指正式批准。
cede: To cede territory or control is to formally give it to another person or authority.
cede 指正式将领土、控制权或权利让渡给他人。
owing: Owing to something means because of it; owing can also mean money still unpaid.
owing to 表示由于某种原因；owing 也可以指尚未偿还的款项。
alongside: Alongside means next to someone or something, or working together with them.
alongside 表示在某人某物旁边，也可以指与其并肩合作。
afterward: Afterward means at a later time, following an event already mentioned.
afterward 表示在先前提及的事件之后、后来。
onward: Onward means moving or continuing forward in space, time, or progress.
onward 指向前行进，或继续向前发展。
onwards: Onwards means forward or continuing from a particular point onward.
onwards 表示向前、继续发展，常见于英式英语。
anyway: Anyway can mean despite that, or can be used to return to the main topic.
anyway 可以表示尽管如此，也可以用于把谈话拉回正题。
anyhow: Anyhow can mean anyway or in whatever manner something can be done.
anyhow 可以表示无论如何，也可以指以任何可行的方式。
nowhere: Nowhere means in no place, or not at any possible location.
nowhere 表示没有任何地方、无处。
everywhere: Everywhere means in all places or in many different places.
everywhere 表示到处、各个地方。
who: Who asks which person is involved, or introduces information about a person.
who 用来询问涉及的是谁，也可以引导补充说明某人的从句。
fairly: Fairly can mean reasonably or moderately, and sometimes in a just or impartial way.
fairly 可以表示相当、还算，也可以表示公平公正地。
regularly: Something happens regularly when it occurs repeatedly, often at predictable intervals.
regularly 指某事有规律地反复发生，通常间隔可预期。
periodically: Something happens periodically when it takes place from time to time at recurring intervals.
periodically 指某件事以一定间隔周期性地发生。
tenable: A tenable argument or position can be defended with reasonable evidence or logic.
tenable 指某种观点或立场有合理依据，可以站得住脚。
definite: Something definite is clear, certain, and not vague or undecided.
definite 指明确、确定，而非含糊或尚未决定的。
categorize: To categorize things is to arrange them into groups according to shared features.
categorize 指按照共同特征将事物分门别类。
summary: A summary is a short account of the main ideas without all the details.
summary 指只概括要点、不包含全部细节的简短总结。
elucidate: To elucidate something is to explain it in a way that makes it clearer.
elucidate 指通过解释把复杂或模糊的事情讲清楚。
exemplify: To exemplify something is to illustrate it with a clear example.
exemplify 指用具体例子说明某种特点或道理。
attest: To attest to something is to state or provide evidence that it is true.
attest 指作证或提供证据，证明某事属实。
substantiate: To substantiate a claim is to support it with facts or evidence.
substantiate 指用事实或证据支持某项主张。
falsify: To falsify information is to change or invent it dishonestly; in science, a claim is falsified if evidence shows it false.
falsify 可以指伪造或篡改资料；在科学讨论中也可指以证据证伪主张。
refute: To refute a claim is to show with reasons or evidence that it is wrong.
refute 指通过论据或证据驳倒某种主张。
rebut: To rebut an argument is to respond with reasons or evidence against it.
rebut 指用理由或证据回应并反驳某项论点。
dispute: To dispute something is to disagree with or challenge its truth or validity.
dispute 指对某事提出异议，质疑其真实性或有效性。
contest: To contest a decision or claim is to challenge it formally or publicly.
contest 指正式或公开地质疑某项决定、权利或主张。
allege: To allege something is to claim it happened without necessarily proving it.
allege 指声称某件事发生了，但并不表示已得到证实。
contend: To contend that something is true is to argue for it, often against other opinions.
contend 指在存在不同意见时坚持主张某事成立。
register: To register is to enter information officially, or to show a measurable reaction or value.
register 指正式登记，也可以表示记录到某种反应或数值。
allude: To allude to something is to refer to it indirectly without stating it explicitly.
allude to 指不直接说出，而是间接提及某事。
signify: To signify something is to mean it, represent it, or show that it exists.
signify 指意味着、象征着，或表明某事存在。
symbolize: To symbolize something is to stand for or represent an idea or quality.
symbolize 指象征、代表某种观念或性质。
importance: Importance is the quality of mattering or having significant effects.
importance 指某件事的重要程度或影响力。
implication: An implication is a possible result of something, or a meaning that is suggested indirectly.
implication 指某件事可能带来的影响，也可指隐含的意思。
ramification: A ramification is a further consequence of an action, often complex or unexpected.
ramification 指某项行动进一步引发的复杂或意外后果。
repercussion: A repercussion is an indirect effect or consequence, especially an unwelcome one.
repercussion 指间接后果，尤其是不利的连锁影响。
hazard: A hazard is something that can cause harm or danger.
hazard 指可能造成损害或危险的事物或因素。
threat: A threat is a possible source of harm, or a statement of intention to cause harm.
threat 指可能造成伤害的威胁，也可指扬言加害的行为。
peril: Peril is serious or immediate danger.
peril 指严重或迫在眉睫的危险。
prevention: Prevention means taking action to stop something harmful from happening.
prevention 指采取措施，防止有害事件发生。
axiom: An axiom is a principle accepted as a starting point for reasoning in a system.
axiom 指在某个推理体系中作为起点被接受的公理。
conjecture: A conjecture is an idea or statement believed possible but not yet proved.
conjecture 指有待证明的猜想或推测。
proposition: A proposition is a statement or idea that can be considered, debated, or proved.
proposition 指可供考虑、讨论或证明的命题或主张。
allegation: An allegation is a claim about wrongdoing that has not necessarily been proved.
allegation 指对不当行为的指控，但不意味着指控已经证实。
accusation: An accusation is a statement that someone has done something wrong.
accusation 指指责或控告某人做了错事。
notification: A notification is a message informing someone that something has happened or requires attention.
notification 指告知某事发生或需要关注的通知消息。
announcement: An announcement is a public or formal statement giving information.
announcement 指向公众或有关人员发布信息的公告或宣布。
declaration: A declaration is a formal statement that makes a position or fact known.
declaration 指正式宣布某种立场或事实的声明。
communication: Communication is the exchange or sharing of information, ideas, or feelings.
communication 指交流、传递信息、观点或感受的过程。
metaphor: A metaphor describes something in terms of something else to suggest a shared quality.
metaphor 指借用另一事物来描述某物，以突出二者的共同特点，即隐喻。
idiom: An idiom is a fixed expression whose meaning is not always clear from its individual words.
idiom 指整体含义未必能从每个字面词义推得的习惯用语。
utterance: An utterance is a particular act or piece of spoken language.
utterance 指一次说话行为，或说出的某段话。
clause: A clause is a group of words containing a subject and a verb, often forming part of a sentence.
clause 指含有主语和谓语的词组，常作为句子的一个分句。
grammar: Grammar is the system of rules describing how words combine into meaningful sentences.
grammar 指单词组合成有意义句子的语法规则体系。
conceptual: Something conceptual concerns ideas or concepts rather than practical details.
conceptual 指涉及概念和思想，而非具体操作细节的。
discernment: Discernment is the ability to judge or notice subtle differences accurately.
discernment 指准确判断事物或察觉细微差别的能力。
awareness: Awareness is knowing that something exists or understanding what is happening.
awareness 指意识到某事存在，或了解当前情况。
cognition: Cognition is the mental process of acquiring knowledge, thinking, and understanding.
cognition 指获取知识、思考和理解的认知过程。
recognition: Recognition is identifying something known, or acknowledging its value or status.
recognition 指认出熟悉的事物，也可以指承认其价值或地位。
comprehension: Comprehension is the ability or process of understanding something.
comprehension 指理解某种内容的能力或过程。
criticism: Criticism is the expression of disapproval or the careful evaluation of a work or idea.
criticism 指批评指责，也可以指对作品或观点的细致评价。
norm: A norm is a typical standard of behavior or an accepted expectation in a group.
norm 指一个群体通常接受的行为准则或惯例。
yardstick: A yardstick is a standard used to measure or judge the quality or success of something.
yardstick 指衡量质量或成效的标准或尺度。
coefficient: A coefficient is a number that multiplies a variable or describes a relationship in a formula.
coefficient 指公式中乘在变量前或表示某种关系的系数。
approximation: An approximation is a value or description that is close but not exact.
approximation 指接近准确值、却并非完全精确的近似值或描述。
correctness: Correctness is the quality of being accurate or following the right rules.
correctness 指结果正确，或符合适当规则的性质。
stability: Stability is the ability to remain steady without unexpected change.
stability 指保持稳定、不发生意外变化的能力。
pace: Pace is the speed at which something happens or progresses.
pace 指事情发生或进展的速度与节奏。
tempo: Tempo is the speed or rhythm of music or another activity.
tempo 指音乐或某种活动的速度与节奏。
breadth: Breadth is the distance across something, or the range of its scope.
breadth 指物体的宽度，也可以指涉及范围的广度。
depth: Depth is how deep something is, or the complexity of knowledge or analysis.
depth 指物体的深度，也可以指理解或分析的深入程度。
density: Density is the amount of mass or other quantity within a given volume or area.
density 指单位体积或面积内所含的质量或其他数量。
voltage: Voltage is the electrical potential difference between two points.
voltage 指电路中两点之间的电势差，即电压。
skew: Skew is a lack of balance or symmetry, or a bias in how data are distributed.
skew 指不对称或偏斜，也可以表示数据分布偏态。
displacement: Displacement is a change in position from a reference point.
displacement 指物体相对于参考位置发生的位置变化或位移。
instability: Instability is a tendency to change unpredictably or to lose a steady state.
instability 指状态不稳定、容易发生不可预期变化。
lag: A lag is a delay between one event or change and another.
lag 指一个事件或变化相对于另一个发生的延迟。
alignment: Alignment is the arrangement of things so that they match a common line, position, or goal.
alignment 指事物在位置、方向或目标上保持一致、对齐的状态。
interference: Interference is an unwanted effect that disrupts a signal, activity, or process.
interference 指干扰信号、活动或过程正常进行的不利影响。
suppression: Suppression is the act of stopping, reducing, or holding something back.
suppression 指压制、抑制或减少某种活动或现象。
setback: A setback is a problem or event that delays progress.
setback 指使进展受阻或延后的挫折。
shortcoming: A shortcoming is a weakness or deficiency in a person, plan, or system.
shortcoming 指人、计划或系统存在的不足或缺点。
omission: An omission is something left out, especially by accident.
omission 指被遗漏的内容，尤其是无意中漏掉的部分。
transparency: Transparency is the quality of being open and easy to inspect or understand.
transparency 指过程或信息公开透明、便于检查和理解的性质。
opacity: Opacity is the quality of not allowing light through, or of being hard to understand.
opacity 指不透光，也可以比喻信息不透明、难以理解。
subtlety: Subtlety is a fine distinction or quality that is not immediately obvious.
subtlety 指不容易立即察觉的细微差别或精妙之处。
intricacy: Intricacy is the quality of having many small, complicated, connected details.
intricacy 指由许多相互关联的细节构成的复杂精细程度。
practicality: Practicality is how suitable or useful something is in real situations.
practicality 指某种方案在实际情境中的实用性或可操作性。
viability: Viability is the ability of an idea, business, or organism to work or survive.
viability 指方案、企业或生物体能够运作或生存的可行性。
proficiency: Proficiency is the ability to do something skillfully and competently.
proficiency 指熟练而胜任地完成某项任务的能力。
expertise: Expertise is detailed knowledge or skill gained through training and experience.
expertise 指通过训练和经验获得的专业知识或技能。
diligence: Diligence is careful and persistent effort in doing a task.
diligence 指完成任务时认真、细致而持续付出的努力。
perseverance: Perseverance is continuing to work toward a goal despite obstacles.
perseverance 指即使遇到困难，也持续朝目标努力的毅力。
forbearance: Forbearance is patient self-control when facing difficulty or irritation.
forbearance 指面对困难或冒犯时克制自己、耐心忍让。
brittle: Something brittle is hard but breaks easily rather than bending.
brittle 指坚硬但容易断裂，而不容易弯曲的。
sturdy: Something sturdy is strongly built and unlikely to break or fall.
sturdy 指结构结实、不容易损坏或倒塌的。
prolonged: Something prolonged continues for longer than usual or expected.
prolonged 指持续时间超过通常情况或预期的。
recurrent: Something recurrent happens repeatedly, often after intervals.
recurrent 指某种问题或事件间隔一段时间后反复发生。
recurring: Something recurring happens again and again, sometimes regularly.
recurring 指某件事反复出现，有时具有规律性。
superfluous: Something superfluous is unnecessary because there is more than is needed.
superfluous 指超过需要、多余而无必要的。
negligible: Something negligible is too small or unimportant to matter in a particular context.
negligible 指在特定情境中小到可以忽略不计的。
interdependence: Interdependence is a situation in which two or more things depend on each other.
interdependence 指两个或更多事物相互依赖的关系。
subordinate: Someone or something subordinate has a lower rank or is less important than another.
subordinate 指地位较低或次要的，也可作名词指下属。
anterior: Anterior means nearer the front, especially in anatomy.
anterior 指更靠近前部的位置，尤其用于解剖学。
posterior: Posterior means nearer the back, especially in anatomy, or coming later.
