posterior 指更靠近后部的，尤其用于解剖学，也可指时间上在后的。
sequential: Sequential events follow one another in a particular order.
sequential 指事件按照特定顺序一个接一个发生。
serial: Serial means arranged in a series or occurring one after another.
serial 指按系列排列或依次发生的。
successive: Successive events or people follow one another in order, often without interruption.
successive 指依次接续出现的事件或人，常强调连续。
consolidated: Something consolidated has been combined into a single, stronger or simpler whole.
consolidated 指多个部分整合成一个更统一、更牢固的整体。
integrated: Something integrated has parts that work together as one system.
integrated 指不同部分协调配合、作为一个整体运行的。
inclusive: Something inclusive is designed to include a wide range of people or possibilities.
inclusive 指尽量涵盖不同人群或各种情况的。
exclusive: Something exclusive is limited to certain people, or does not include something else.
exclusive 指专属于特定人群或排除其他事物的。
isolated: Something isolated is separated from others or not connected with them.
isolated 指与其他事物分离、缺少联系的。
hereby: Hereby is used in formal writing to announce that something is done by the statement itself.
hereby 用于正式文件，表示某项行为通过当前声明即告完成，常译为“特此”。
atop: Atop means on the top of something.
atop 表示在某物的顶部，语气比 on top of 略带书面色彩。
anew: To do something anew is to do it again, often with a fresh approach or beginning.
anew 指重新开始或以新的方式再做一次，而不只是机械重复。
apart: When things are apart, they are separated by space, distance, or disagreement.
apart 指在空间上分开、彼此相隔，也可以表示关系疏离。
thoroughly: To do something thoroughly is to do it completely and carefully.
thoroughly 指全面、仔细地完成某事，不遗漏重要细节。
steadily: Something happens steadily when it continues at a fairly constant pace.
steadily 指以相对稳定的速度或节奏持续进行。
gradually: Something changes gradually when it changes in small steps over time.
gradually 指逐渐发生变化，而非一次性突然改变。
broadly: Broadly means in a general way, without focusing on fine details.
broadly 指从整体或大致层面而言，不拘泥于细节。
narrowly: Narrowly means by a small margin, or in a limited way.
narrowly 可以表示仅以微小差距达成，也可以指范围狭窄地。
frankly: To speak frankly is to express an opinion honestly and directly.
frankly 指坦率、直接地表达看法，不刻意回避问题。
indirectly: Something happens indirectly when it occurs through another cause or route.
indirectly 指间接地发生或产生作用，并非通过直接途径。
effectively: Effectively can mean successfully, or practically the same as a stated situation.
effectively 可以指有效地，也可以表示实际上或实质上等同于某种情况。
ideally: Ideally means in the best possible situation, although reality may differ.
ideally 指在理想情况下，暗示现实未必完全符合。
unexpectedly: Something happens unexpectedly when it was not anticipated.
unexpectedly 指事情出乎预料地发生。
deliberately: To act deliberately is to act on purpose rather than by accident.
deliberately 指有意、故意地采取行动，而非无意之举。
intentionally: Something is done intentionally when it is done with a conscious purpose.
intentionally 指出于明确意图而做某事。
practically: Practically can mean almost, or in a sensible way that works in real life.
practically 可以表示几乎、差不多，也可以指切合实际地。
theoretically: Theoretically means according to an idea or theory, rather than necessarily in practice.
theoretically 指按照理论而言，不保证实际情况也如此。
ostensibly: Ostensibly describes an apparent reason or situation that may conceal a different reality.
ostensibly 表示表面上或据称如此，暗示背后可能另有实际原因。
critically: Critically can mean with careful judgment, or in a way that is crucial to success.
critically 可以表示批判性地审视，也可以指对结果至关重要地。
arguably: Arguably introduces a claim that can reasonably be supported by argument.
arguably 表示某种评价有理由成立，但并非不容争辩的定论。
henceforth: Henceforth means from this point in time onward.
henceforth 表示从此以后，常用于正式声明。
daily: Daily means happening or being done every day.
daily 指每天发生或进行的。
weekly: Weekly means happening once a week or relating to each week.
weekly 指每周发生一次或与每周有关的。
monthly: Monthly means occurring or being prepared once every month.
monthly 指每月发生或编制一次的。
yearly: Yearly means happening once a year or each year.
yearly 指每年一次或每年都会发生的。
annually: Something happens annually when it happens once every year.
annually 指每年一次，常见于报告、财务和正式表达。
formerly: Formerly means in the past, before a change of name, role, or condition.
formerly 表示从前、以前，常暗示如今已经改变。
lately: Lately means in the recent past, especially over a continuing period.
lately 表示最近一段时间，常用于谈论近期持续的变化。
recently: Recently means not long ago or during the recent past.
recently 指不久之前或最近一段时间内。
shortly: Shortly can mean soon, or briefly and with few words.
shortly 可以表示很快、不久，也可以指简短地。
promptly: To respond promptly is to respond without unnecessary delay.
promptly 指及时、迅速地行动，不作无谓拖延。
temporarily: Something exists temporarily when it lasts for a limited time.
temporarily 指暂时存在或持续，而非永久如此。
permanently: A change is permanent when it is intended to last indefinitely.
permanently 指永久地或长期固定地，不只是暂时。
indefinitely: Indefinitely means without a fixed end date or clear limit.
indefinitely 指没有明确截止时间，并不一定意味着永远。
initially: Initially means at the beginning, before a situation develops or changes.
initially 表示最初、起先，之后情况可能改变。
noticeably: A change is noticeable when it is clear enough to be observed.
noticeably 指明显到能够察觉的程度。
sharply: Something changes sharply when it changes suddenly or by a large amount.
sharply 指突然或大幅度地变化，也可以表示语气尖锐。
simply: Simply can mean in an uncomplicated way, or just and nothing more.
simply 指简单地，也可以表示仅仅、不过是。
predominantly: Predominantly means mainly or for the most part.
predominantly 表示主要地、占绝大部分地。
appropriately: To act appropriately is to act in a way that suits the situation.
appropriately 指以符合场合、目的或规范的方式行事。
duly: Duly means at the proper time or in the proper manner, often following a formal process.
duly 表示按规定、适当地或如期完成，常见于正式语境。
suitably: Suitably means in a way that fits a particular purpose or occasion.
suitably 指适合特定目的或场合地。
uniformly: Uniformly means in the same way or to the same extent throughout.
uniformly 指各处一致地、均匀地。
strictly: Strictly means according to a rule without exception, or with exact precision.
strictly 指严格按照规则，也可以表示从严格意义上而言。
directly: Directly means without an intermediate step, or can mean immediately.
directly 表示直接地、不经中间环节；在某些语境中也表示立即。
formally: Formally means according to official rules or conventional procedures.
formally 指依照正式规则或程序地。
cautiously: To proceed cautiously is to act carefully because there may be risks.
cautiously 指考虑到风险而谨慎地行事。
collectively: Collectively means considered or acting as a group rather than separately.
collectively 指作为整体或群体共同地。
individually: Individually means one by one, or separately for each person or item.
individually 指逐个地、分别地，而非作为整体。
namely: Namely introduces the specific name or details of what was just mentioned.
namely 用来明确指出前文提到的对象，常译为“即、也就是”。
mutually: Mutually means shared or done by two or more parties toward one another.
mutually 指双方或多方相互地、共同地。
independently: Independently means without relying on or being controlled by another person or factor.
independently 指独立地，不依赖另一人或因素。
separately: Separately means as distinct items or events, rather than together.
separately 指分别、单独地处理，而非合在一起。
jointly: Jointly means together with another person or organization.
jointly 指双方或多方联合、共同地。
closely: Closely means at a short distance, or with careful attention or a strong connection.
closely 指紧密地、仔细地或密切相关地。
systematically: To work systematically is to follow an organized method or plan.
systematically 指按照有组织、有步骤的方法开展工作。
easily: Easily means without much difficulty or effort.
easily 指轻易、毫不费力地。
surely: Surely expresses strong confidence, or asks for agreement with what seems obvious.
surely 表达确信，也可用于反问以寻求认同。
inevitably: Something happens inevitably when it cannot reasonably be avoided.
inevitably 指不可避免地、必然地发生。
decidedly: Decidedly means clearly and definitely, with little doubt.
decidedly 表示明显地、毫无疑问地。
openly: To speak openly is to do so without hiding one's views or actions.
openly 指公开、坦诚地表达，不加掩饰。
undoubtedly: undoubtedly 表示毫无疑问地，强调说话者高度确信。
maybe: Maybe means perhaps; it expresses possibility rather than certainty.
maybe 表示也许、可能，而非确定。
superficial: Something superficial concerns only the surface or lacks depth.
superficial 指表面的、肤浅的，未深入本质。
terse: A terse reply is very brief and may sound abrupt.
terse 指答复或表达非常简短，有时显得生硬。
succinct: Something succinct expresses the key points clearly in few words.
succinct 指言简意赅，既简洁又抓住要点。
lucid: A lucid explanation is clear and easy to understand.
lucid 指解释或思路清晰明白、易于理解。
contradictory: Two statements are contradictory when they cannot both be true in the same sense.
contradictory 指两项陈述相互矛盾，在同一意义下不能同时成立。
conflicting: Conflicting interests or statements are incompatible or opposed.
conflicting 指利益、证据或说法彼此冲突、不一致。
elusive: Something elusive is difficult to find, achieve, describe, or fully understand.
elusive 指难以捉摸、发现、实现或清楚界定的。
illusory: Something illusory seems real or achievable but actually is not.
illusory 指看似真实或可实现、实则虚幻的。
imminent: Something imminent is expected to happen very soon.
imminent 指即将发生、迫在眉睫的。
eminent: An eminent person is highly respected or distinguished in a field.
eminent 指某人在某个领域声望很高、卓有成就。
immanent: Immanent describes something existing or operating within a thing rather than coming from outside it.
immanent 指内在于某事物或体系之中的，而非来自外部。
averse: Someone averse to something strongly dislikes or wishes to avoid it.
averse 指反感或不愿接触某事，常用 be averse to。
elude: To elude someone is to escape their grasp, understanding, or efforts to find you.
elude 指逃脱追捕，或使人难以理解、记起或找到。
disdain: To disdain something is to regard it as unworthy of respect or attention.
disdain 指轻蔑、不屑，认为某事物不值得尊重。
disinterested: A disinterested judge is impartial and has no personal stake in the outcome.
disinterested 在严谨用法中指公正无私、没有利害关系，而非单纯不感兴趣。
latest: The latest item or news is the most recent one available.
latest 指最新的、最近出现的，不等同于最后一个。
lastly: Lastly introduces the final item in a sequence or list.
lastly 用来引出顺序中的最后一点，常用于列举。
confidently: To act confidently is to do so with a strong belief in one's ability or judgment.
confidently 指有信心地做某事，不代表必然正确。
stipulate: To stipulate a condition is to state that it must be met as part of an agreement.
stipulate 指在协议或规则中明确规定必须满足的条件。
herein: Herein means in this document or within the matter being discussed.
herein 在正式书面语中表示在本文件中或在此所讨论的事项内。
thereof: Thereof means of the thing just mentioned, especially in legal or formal language.
thereof 在法律或正式文字中表示“其中的、它的”，指代前面提到的事物。
whence: Whence asks or states the place or source from which something comes.
whence 表示从何处、由何而来，较古旧或书面。
whatsoever: Whatsoever adds emphasis to a negative statement, meaning at all.
whatsoever 常用于否定句中加强语气，表示丝毫、任何。
beforehand: Beforehand means before a particular event or time.
barring: Barring something means except if that event or condition occurs.
barring 表示除非发生某件事，或除了某项阻碍之外。
spoke: Spoke is the past tense of speak; it also names a rod connecting the center of a wheel to its rim.
spoke 是 speak 的过去式；作名词时还指连接轮毂与轮圈的辐条。
thinking: Thinking is the process of using your mind to form ideas, judgments, or plans.
thinking 指运用头脑形成想法、判断或计划的思考过程。
works: Works can mean creations, such as books or art, or the parts and mechanisms of a machine.
works 可指著作、艺术作品，也可指机器内部的零件或机构。
honour: Honour is respect or high esteem; it is the usual British spelling of honor.
honour 指荣誉、尊重；这是英式拼写，美式通常写作 honor。
trying: Something trying is difficult or exhausting to deal with.
trying 作形容词时表示难以应付、令人疲惫或心烦的。
clothe: To clothe someone is to provide them with clothes or cover them.
clothe 指为某人提供衣服，或用衣物覆盖某人。
fool: A fool is a person who acts without good judgment; to fool someone is to trick them.
fool 作名词指做事缺乏判断力的人；作动词指欺骗、愚弄。
expression: An expression is a way of showing an idea or feeling through words, a face, or an action.
expression 指通过话语、面部表情或行为表达想法或情感的方式。
opportune: An opportune moment is a particularly suitable or convenient time for an action.
opportune 指时机恰到好处、特别适合采取行动的。
ring: A ring is a circular band, or a clear sound made by a bell or phone; to ring is to make that sound.
ring 指环形物，也可指铃声；作动词时指发出铃声。
learned: Learned can mean having gained knowledge, or highly educated and scholarly.
learned 既可表示已经学会，也可作形容词表示学识渊博的。
fame: Fame is the state of being widely known, usually for an achievement or activity.
fame 指因某种成就或活动而广为人知的名声。
finance: Finance concerns the management of money, investments, and funding.
finance 指资金、投资和融资等方面的财务管理。
forth: Forth means forward or outward from a place, often in literary expressions.
forth 表示向前、向外，常用于书面或固定搭配中。
regular: Something regular happens repeatedly at usual intervals, or follows an established pattern.
regular 指按通常间隔重复发生的，或遵循固定规律的。
relieve: To relieve pain or pressure is to make it less severe; to relieve someone can also mean to replace them on duty.
relieve 指缓解疼痛或压力，也可指接替某人的工作岗位。
running: Running is the action of moving quickly on foot; it can also describe something currently operating.
running 指跑步，也可表示正在运行或持续进行的。
shadow: A shadow is a dark shape formed when an object blocks light.
shadow 指物体挡住光线时形成的阴影。
working: Something working is functioning or in operation; working conditions concern the environment of a job.
working 可表示正在运行的；working conditions 指工作条件。
agent: An agent acts on behalf of another person or organization; in science, it may be a substance that causes an effect.
agent 指代理人或代表；在科学语境中也指能产生特定作用的物质。
farm: A farm is land used to grow crops or raise animals for food or other products.
farm 指种植作物或饲养动物的农场。
fortunate: Someone fortunate has experienced good luck or favorable circumstances.
fortunate 指幸运的、境遇有利的。
hurry: To hurry is to move or act quickly, often because time is limited.
hurry 指匆忙地移动或行动，通常因为时间紧迫。
list: A list is an ordered collection of names or items, usually written one after another.
list 指依次列出的名称或事项清单。
shore: A shore is the land along the edge of a sea, lake, or river.
shore 指海、湖或河流边缘的岸边。
rock: Rock is hard natural material from the earth; to rock something is to move it back and forth.
rock 指岩石，也可作动词表示使某物前后摇晃。
base: A base is the bottom or main support of something; to base a claim on evidence is to ground it in evidence.
base 指底部或基础；base a claim on evidence 指让主张以证据为依据。
bow: To bow is to bend your head or body as a sign of respect; a bow can also be a curved weapon or ribbon.
bow 作动词指鞠躬；作名词还可指弓或蝴蝶结，读音随词义变化。
fancy: Fancy can mean elaborate or decorative; as a verb it can mean to want or like something.
fancy 可表示精美、花哨的；作动词时也可表示想要或喜欢。
lift: To lift something is to raise it; a lift is also a British English word for an elevator.
lift 指举起或抬高；作名词时在英式英语中还可指电梯。
literary: Literary means related to literature or characteristic of written artistic works.
literary 指与文学有关的，或具有文学作品风格的。
popular: Something popular is liked or supported by many people.
popular 指受到许多人喜爱或支持的。
taste: Taste is the flavor of food or drink, or someone's personal preference.
taste 指食物或饮料的味道，也可指个人品味、喜好。
violent: Something violent involves physical force intended to hurt or cause damage.
violent 指具有暴力性质、可能造成伤害或破坏的。
cloud: A cloud is a visible mass of tiny water droplets or ice crystals in the sky.
cloud 指天空中由微小水滴或冰晶组成的云。
stage: A stage is a phase of a process, or a raised platform used for performance.
stage 指过程中的阶段，也可指演出使用的舞台。
court: A court is a place where legal cases are judged; it may also mean an area used for certain sports.
court 指审理案件的法庭，也可指网球、篮球等运动的场地。
dependent: Someone or something dependent relies on another person, thing, or condition.
dependent 指依赖他人、其他事物或特定条件的。
situation: A situation is the set of circumstances existing at a particular time.
situation 指某一时刻所处的情况或局面。
stream: A stream is a small flowing body of water; it can also mean a continuous flow of data or events.
stream 指小溪，也可指连续的数据流或事件流。
wave: A wave is a moving disturbance, such as on water or in a signal; to wave is to move a hand in greeting.
wave 指水面或信号中的波动；作动词还可指挥手示意。
hit: To hit something is to strike or make contact with it, often forcefully.
hit 指击中、碰到某物，通常伴随一定力度。
passage: A passage is a section of written text, a route through somewhere, or the act of passing.
passage 指文章片段、通道，也可指经过或通过的过程。
vain: Something done in vain produces no useful result; a vain person is overly proud of their appearance or abilities.
in vain 指徒劳无功；vain 作形容词还可指自负、爱慕虚荣的。
aid: Aid is help or support given to someone; to aid is to assist.
aid 指提供的帮助、援助，作动词指协助。
conversation: A conversation is an informal exchange of ideas or information between people.
conversation 指人与人之间非正式地交谈、交流。
mount: To mount is to climb or get onto something, or to increase gradually.
mount 可指登上、骑上，也可指数量或压力逐渐增加。
oil: Oil is a thick liquid used as fuel, lubricant, or food ingredient.
oil 指可用作燃料、润滑剂或食物原料的油。
price: A price is the amount of money asked or paid for something.
price 指购买某物需要支付的金额。
rush: To rush is to move or act very quickly, often without much time to plan.
rush 指迅速、匆忙地行动，往往没有充裕时间作准备。
whisper: To whisper is to speak very quietly, usually so that only nearby people can hear.
whisper 指低声耳语，通常只有近处的人听得见。
considerable: A considerable amount is large enough to be important or noticeable.
considerable 指数量或程度相当大，足以引起注意或产生重要影响。
speed: Speed is how fast something moves or an activity progresses.
speed 指物体移动或事情进展的速度。
coast: A coast is the land along the edge of a sea or ocean.
coast 指临海的陆地边缘、海岸。
journey: A journey is the act of traveling from one place to another, often over a significant distance.
journey 指从一地前往另一地的旅程，通常着重整个行程。
liberty: Liberty is the freedom to act, think, or live without unjust restrictions.
liberty 指不受不合理限制地行动、思考或生活的自由。
mystery: A mystery is something whose cause or meaning is unknown or difficult to explain.
mystery 指原因或含义不明、难以解释的谜团。
shout: To shout is to speak or call out in a very loud voice.
shout 指大声喊叫或呼喊。
vessel: A vessel is a ship or a container, and in anatomy it can carry blood or fluid.
vessel 指船只、容器；在解剖学中还可指运输血液或体液的管道。
addition: An addition is something added, or the act of combining numbers by adding.
addition 指增加的事物，也可指数学中的加法。
charm: Charm is an attractive quality that makes someone or something pleasant or appealing.
charm 指使人或事物讨人喜欢的魅力。
cheer: To cheer is to shout encouragement or show happiness and support.
cheer 指欢呼、喝彩或表达鼓励和支持。
commission: A commission may be a group appointed to perform a task, a payment for sales, or an instruction to create work.
commission 可指受委任的委员会、销售佣金，或委托创作的任务。
date: A date is a calendar day; it can also be a planned meeting, often romantic.
date 指日期，也可指事先约定的见面，尤其是约会。
excel: To excel at something is to perform exceptionally well at it.
excel at 指在某方面表现出色、特别擅长。
fashion: Fashion is a style of clothing or behavior popular at a particular time.
fashion 指某一时期流行的服装或行为风格。
philosophy: Philosophy is the study of fundamental questions about knowledge, reality, values, and reasoning.
philosophy 指研究知识、存在、价值和推理等根本问题的哲学。
project: A project is a planned piece of work with a specific aim; as a verb, project can mean to estimate a future amount.
project 指有明确目标的计划或项目；作动词时可指预测未来数值。
style: Style is a distinctive way of doing, writing, or designing something.
style 指做事、写作或设计的独特方式和风格。
absolute: Something absolute is complete or not limited by conditions; in measurement it can mean referenced to a fixed standard.
absolute 指绝对的、不受条件限制的；在测量中可指相对于固定基准的。
depart: To depart is to leave a place, especially to start a journey.
depart 指离开某地，尤其是启程前往另一处。
gaze: To gaze is to look steadily at something for a relatively long time.
gaze 指长时间凝视某物。
seize: To seize something is to take hold of it suddenly or by force.
seize 指突然或强行抓住、夺取某物。
credit: Credit can mean recognition for an achievement, borrowed money, or the ability to pay later.
credit 指功劳或认可，也可指信贷及赊购资格。
dispose: To dispose of something is to get rid of it; to dispose someone toward something is to incline them to it.
dispose of 指处理、丢弃某物；dispose someone toward 指使某人倾向于某事。
election: An election is a process in which people vote to choose representatives or leaders.
election 指通过投票选举代表或领导者的程序。
shine: To shine is to give off or reflect light brightly.
shine 指发光或明亮地反射光线。
tender: Tender can mean gentle or soft; it also refers to a formal offer to provide goods or services.
tender 可指温柔、柔软的，也可指提供货物或服务的正式投标。
region: A region is a particular area distinguished by location, features, or administration.
region 指因位置、特征或行政区划而划定的地区。
arise: To arise is to happen or come into existence, often referring to a problem or situation.
arise 指情况或问题出现、产生。
calm: Someone calm is not anxious or upset; to calm someone is to make them less agitated.
calm 指平静、不焦躁的；作动词表示使人平静下来。
rank: A rank is a position within an order or hierarchy, or a person's official status.
rank 指等级、名次或职务级别。
sympathy: Sympathy is concern or compassion for another person's suffering or difficulty.
sympathy 指对他人的痛苦或困难表示同情与关切。
confidence: Confidence is belief in one's ability, judgment, or the reliability of a result.
confidence 指对自己能力、判断或结果可靠性的信心。
series: A series is a sequence of related events, items, or measurements.
series 指一连串相关的事件、事物或测量值。
storm: A storm is a period of severe weather with strong wind, rain, snow, or thunder.
storm 指伴有强风、雨雪或雷电的恶劣天气。
committee: A committee is a group appointed to discuss, decide, or act on particular matters.
committee 指被指定讨论、决定或处理特定事务的委员会。
profit: Profit is the money remaining after the costs of an activity or business are subtracted from its income.
profit 指收入扣除经营成本后剩余的利润。
copy: A copy is a reproduction of an original; to copy is to reproduce or imitate it.
copy 指原件的复制品；作动词指复制或模仿。
department: A department is a division of an organization or institution responsible for certain work.
department 指组织或机构中承担某类工作的部门。
operation: An operation is an organized activity, a medical procedure, or the functioning of a system.
operation 指有组织的行动、外科手术，或系统的运行。
statement: A statement is something expressed clearly in speech or writing, especially an official declaration.
statement 指口头或书面明确表达的陈述，尤其是正式声明。
area: An area is a particular space or region; in geometry, it is the size of a surface.
area 指特定区域；在几何中指表面的面积。
assertion: An assertion is a statement made confidently, often without presenting all its supporting evidence.
assertion 指明确而肯定的主张或断言，未必同时给出充分证据。
catalyst: A catalyst speeds up a chemical reaction without being consumed overall; figuratively, it triggers change.
catalyst 指在反应中总体不被消耗的催化剂；比喻义为促成变化的因素。
counterpart: A counterpart is a person or thing in another group that has a similar role or function.
counterpart 指另一组织或情境中承担类似职能的对应人物或事物。
detrimental: Something detrimental causes harm or has a damaging effect.
detrimental 指有害的、造成不良影响的。
doctrine: A doctrine is a system of principles or beliefs taught or accepted by a group.
doctrine 指某个群体教导或接受的一套原则、教义或学说。
endow: To endow an institution is to provide it with money or assets; to be endowed with a quality is to possess it.
endow 指向机构捐赠资金或资产；be endowed with 指天生或本身具有某种特质。
essence: The essence of something is its most important or defining quality.
essence 指事物最根本、最具决定性的特征或本质。
inclination: An inclination is a tendency or preference to do something; it can also mean a slope.
inclination 指做某事的倾向或意愿，也可指倾角、斜度。
initiative: Initiative is the ability to act without being told, or a new plan intended to solve a problem.
initiative 指主动采取行动的能力，也可指解决问题的新计划、倡议。
interim: Interim describes a temporary period or arrangement until a more permanent one exists.
interim 指过渡时期的、临时的安排，直到更稳定的方案建立。
provision: A provision is a condition in an agreement or law; provisions can also be supplies prepared for future needs.
provision 指法律或合同中的条款；复数 provisions 还可指储备物资。
salient: A salient feature is the most noticeable or important feature in a situation.
salient 指某种情况中最显著、最重要的特征。
speculative: Something speculative is based on uncertain ideas or assumptions rather than firm evidence.
speculative 指主要基于推测或不确定假设、缺乏坚实证据的。
substantive: A substantive issue concerns the main content or essential facts rather than mere procedure or form.
substantive 指涉及实质内容、核心事实的，而非仅关乎程序或形式。
virtue: A virtue is a morally good quality; by virtue of means because of or through something.
virtue 指美德、优点；by virtue of 表示由于或凭借某事。
volatility: Volatility is the degree to which a value or situation changes rapidly or unpredictably.
volatility 指数值或局势快速且难以预测地波动的程度。
withhold: To withhold something is to deliberately refuse to give, share, or reveal it.
withhold 指有意扣留、不提供或不披露某物。
juxtapose: To juxtapose two things is to place them side by side to highlight their relationship or differences.
juxtapose 指将两个事物并置，以凸显它们的联系或差异。
emanate: To emanate from something is to come out or spread from that source.
emanate 指从某一源头发出、散发或产生。
illicit: Something illicit is forbidden by law or accepted rules.
illicit 指法律或规范所禁止的、非法的。
elicit: To elicit a response is to draw it out through a question, action, or stimulus.
elicit 指通过提问、行动或刺激引出反应或信息。
illusion: An illusion is a false impression of reality or something that seems real but is not.
illusion 指对现实的错觉，或看似真实却并非如此的表象。
allusion: An allusion is an indirect reference to something without naming it directly.
allusion 指不直接点明对象的暗示或间接提及。
random: Something random is selected or occurs without a predictable pattern; statistical randomness has a defined probability model.
random 指随机选取或发生的；统计学中的随机性需要由概率模型加以刻画。
stratify: To stratify a population is to divide it into layers or groups based on defined characteristics.
stratify 指根据明确特征将总体分层、分组。
traceable: Something traceable can be tracked back to its source or reconstructed through a recorded chain.
traceable 指可以追溯到来源，或通过记录链条重新核查的。
contemporaneous: Contemporaneous events happen or exist during the same period.
contemporaneous 指同时代的、在同一时期发生或存在的。
pervasive: Something pervasive spreads widely through an area, group, or situation and is hard to avoid.
pervasive 指某种影响或现象广泛存在、渗透各处，因而难以避开。
ubiquitous: Something ubiquitous seems to be present or found almost everywhere.
ubiquitous 指某事物几乎随处可见、无处不在。
sporadic: Something sporadic happens occasionally and irregularly, with gaps between occurrences.
sporadic 指事情偶尔、不规则地发生，中间有间隔。
episodic: Something episodic happens in separate periods or episodes rather than continuously.
episodic 指事情分阶段、间歇性地发生，而非持续不断。
perpetual: Something perpetual continues indefinitely or happens so often that it seems never-ending.
perpetual 指持续不断，或频繁到仿佛永无止境。
emerging: Something emerging is beginning to appear, develop, or become important.
emerging 指某事物正开始出现、发展，或逐渐受到重视。
emergent: Something emergent is newly appearing or arises from interactions within a larger system.
emergent 指新近出现的事物；在系统论中也指由整体相互作用产生的性质。
nascent: Something nascent is at a very early stage of development.
nascent 指事物刚开始形成或发展，尚处于萌芽阶段。
paramount: Something paramount is more important than all competing considerations.
paramount 指比其他相关因素都更重要、具有最高优先级。
ancillary: Something ancillary provides additional support to a main activity or purpose.
ancillary 指为主要活动或目的提供辅助、配套作用。
extrinsic: Something extrinsic comes from outside the thing or situation being considered.
extrinsic 指某种因素来自所讨论事物或情境的外部。
consequential: Something consequential has important effects or results.
consequential 指会产生重要影响或后果。
inconsequential: Something inconsequential has little importance or effect on the outcome.
inconsequential 指不重要，或对结果影响很小。
appreciable: An appreciable difference or amount is large enough to be noticed or measured.
appreciable 指差异或数量足够明显，可以觉察或测量。
conspicuous: Something conspicuous is easy to notice because it stands out.
conspicuous 指由于十分突出而容易被注意到。
conspicuously: Conspicuously means in a way that is especially noticeable or stands out.
conspicuously 指以格外显眼、引人注意的方式。
discernible: Something discernible can be recognized or noticed, although it may not be obvious.
discernible 指某事物虽不一定明显，但仍能辨认或察觉。
imperceptible: A change that is imperceptible is too small or subtle to be noticed.
imperceptible 指变化过于微小或细微，以至于无法察觉。
dissonance: Dissonance is a lack of agreement or harmony between ideas, sounds, or feelings.
dissonance 指观念、声音或感受之间的不协调、不一致。
reconciliation: Reconciliation is restoring a relationship or making apparently conflicting facts or records consistent.
reconciliation 指修复关系，或使表面冲突的事实、记录重新一致。
recant: To recant is to formally withdraw a statement or belief that you previously asserted.
recant 指正式撤回先前公开坚持的陈述或信念。
rescind: To rescind a decision, agreement, or rule is to officially cancel it.
rescind 指正式撤销一项决定、协议或规定。
repeal: To repeal a law is to officially end its legal force.
repeal 指正式废除法律，使其不再具有法律效力。
revoke: To revoke a permission or right is to officially withdraw it.
revoke 指正式撤销已经授予的许可或权利。
renounce: To renounce a claim, belief, or right is to formally give it up.
renounce 指正式放弃某项主张、信念或权利。
relinquish: To relinquish something is to give up control, possession, or responsibility for it.
relinquish 指放弃对某物的控制、占有，或不再承担某项责任。
retract: To retract a statement is to withdraw it; to retract a part is to pull it back.
retract 可指撤回言论，也可指将某个部分缩回。
recede: To recede is to move farther away, or gradually become less strong or noticeable.
recede 指向远处退去，或逐渐减弱、不再显眼。
subside: To subside is to become less intense or gradually return to a lower level.
subside 指强度逐渐减弱，或慢慢回到较低水平。
rebound: To rebound is to recover after a fall or setback, or to bounce back after contact.
rebound 指下跌或受挫后反弹、恢复，也可指撞击后的弹回。
surge: A surge is a sudden large increase; to surge is to rise or move quickly and powerfully.
surge 指突然大幅增加；作动词也指迅猛上涨或涌动。
oscillate: To oscillate is to move or vary repeatedly between two positions or values.
oscillate 指在两个位置或数值之间反复往复变化。
plateau: A plateau is a period or level at which growth or change stops after earlier progress.
plateau 指此前的增长或变化进入停滞、保持稳定的阶段。
outset: The outset of an activity or period is its beginning.
outset 指某项活动或某一时期的起始阶段。
saturation: Saturation is the state of being fully filled or having reached the maximum useful capacity.
saturation 指达到饱和、充满，或达到有效容量上限的状态。
granular: Granular information is divided into small, detailed parts rather than broad categories.
granular 指信息划分得很细，具有较高的细节粒度。
proxy: A proxy is something or someone that stands in for another, sometimes as an indirect measure.
proxy 指代替他者的代理人、替代物，或用作间接衡量的指标。
surrogate: A surrogate is a substitute that takes the place of another thing or person.
surrogate 指用于替代另一事物或他人的替代者、替代物。
mediator: A mediator helps parties reach an agreement, or is a factor through which one variable affects another.
mediator 指协助双方达成协议的调解者；在研究中也指传递变量影响的中介因素。
supposition: A supposition is an idea accepted provisionally without enough proof.
supposition 指证据尚不充分时暂且接受的一种设想或假定。
disparage: To disparage someone or something is to speak about them as though they have little value.
disparage 指贬低某人或某物，仿佛其没有多少价值。
denigrate: To denigrate someone is to unfairly criticize or belittle their worth or reputation.
denigrate 指贬损某人的价值或名誉，通常带有不公正的贬低意味。
disregard: To disregard something is to pay no attention to it or deliberately ignore it.
disregard 指不予理会某事，或有意忽视它。
supervise: To supervise people or work is to oversee and direct their activities.
supervise 指监督并指导人员或工作的进行。
misinterpret: To misinterpret something is to understand its meaning incorrectly.
misinterpret 指错误理解某件事的意义。
misconceive: To misconceive something is to form a fundamentally mistaken idea about it.
misconceive 指从根本上错误地理解或设想某事。
misrepresent: To misrepresent something is to describe it inaccurately or misleadingly.
misrepresent 指不准确或具有误导性地陈述某件事。
mislead: To mislead someone is to cause them to believe something false or inaccurate.
mislead 指使某人相信错误或不准确的事情。
contravene: To contravene a rule or law is to act in a way that breaks it.
contravene 指采取违反法规或规则的行动。
counteract: To counteract an effect is to reduce or neutralize it by an opposing action.
counteract 指通过反向作用减弱或抵消某种影响。
counterbalance: To counterbalance one force or influence is to offset it with another.
counterbalance 指用另一种力量或影响来平衡、抵消原有作用。
circumvent: To circumvent an obstacle or rule is to find a way around it instead of confronting it directly.
circumvent 指绕开障碍或规则，而不是直接面对或遵循它。
refrain: To refrain from doing something is to deliberately avoid doing it.
refrain from 指有意识地克制自己，不去做某事。
forgo: To forgo something is to decide not to have or do it.
forgo 指主动选择放弃某种利益、机会或做法。
forego: To forego something can mean to go before it, though it is also often used as a variant of forgo.
forego 原义是“先于……发生”；现代使用中也常作为 forgo“放弃”的变体。
forbear: To forbear is to patiently hold back from doing something.
forbear 指耐心克制自己，避免采取某种行动。
suspend: To suspend an activity is to stop it temporarily, with the possibility of resuming it.
suspend 指暂时中止活动，之后可能恢复。
postpone: To postpone something is to move it to a later time or date.
postpone 指把原定事件推迟到较晚的时间。
annul: To annul an agreement or marriage is to declare it legally invalid.
annul 指依法宣布协议或婚姻无效。
void: Something void has no legal force or effect; a void can also be an empty space.
void 作形容词指不具有法律效力；作名词也可指空隙或真空。
invalidate: To invalidate a claim or result is to show it is not valid or make it no longer acceptable.
invalidate 指证明主张或结果无效，或使它不再被认可。
indeterminate: Something indeterminate cannot be established exactly from the information available.
indeterminate 指凭现有信息无法准确确定的事物。
anecdotal: Anecdotal evidence comes from individual experiences rather than systematic research.
anecdotal evidence 指来自个人经历而非系统性研究的轶事性证据。
attributable: Something attributable to a cause can reasonably be explained as resulting from it.
attributable to 指某种结果可合理地归因于某个原因。
putative: Something putative is commonly believed or claimed to be a certain thing, without full confirmation.
putative 指人们普遍认为或声称属于某类，但尚未完全确认。
alleged: Something alleged is claimed to have happened or to be true, but has not been established as fact.
alleged 指有人声称其发生或属实，但尚未证实。
lenient: A lenient person or rule is less strict in punishment or enforcement.
lenient 指处理、惩罚或执行规则时比较宽容、不严格。
lax: Someone lax is not careful or strict enough about rules or standards.
lax 指对规则或标准把关不严、过于松懈。
haphazard: Something haphazard is done without a clear plan or consistent method.
haphazard 指做事缺少清晰计划或一致的方法，杂乱无章。
methodical: Someone methodical works carefully according to an orderly plan.
methodical 指做事遵循有条理的计划，细致而系统。
colloquial: Colloquial language is ordinary conversational speech rather than formal writing.
colloquial 指日常口语式的表达，而非正式书面语言。
ironically: Ironically introduces a situation that is unexpectedly opposite to what one would expect.
ironically 用于指出情况与通常预期意外地相反。
sarcastically: Someone speaking sarcastically uses irony to mock or criticize.
sarcastically 指用讽刺、挖苦的语气说话。
bluntly: To speak bluntly is to express an opinion directly without softening it.
bluntly 指直截了当地表达意见，不作委婉缓和。
prolix: Prolix writing or speech is unnecessarily long and wordy.
prolix 指文字或讲话不必要地冗长、啰嗦。
gratuitous: Something gratuitous is unnecessary or uncalled for; in some contexts it means free of charge.
gratuitous 可指多余、无缘无故；在某些语境中也指免费的。
repetitive: Something repetitive repeats the same action or idea many times, often tediously.
repetitive 指同一动作或观点一再重复，常带有单调意味。
ephemeral: Something ephemeral lasts only a very short time.
ephemeral 指持续时间非常短、转瞬即逝。
enduring: Something enduring continues for a long time despite change or difficulty.
enduring 指即使经历变化或困难，仍长期持续。
incessant: Something incessant continues without stopping, especially in an annoying way.
incessant 指接连不断、几乎不停止，常带有令人厌烦的意味。
periodic: Something periodic happens at regular or recurring intervals.
periodic 指按固定或反复出现的时间间隔发生。
customary: Something customary is usual because of an established practice or tradition.
customary 指由于惯例或传统而通常采用的做法。
habitual: Something habitual is done regularly as a habit.
habitual 指已经形成习惯、经常反复进行的行为。
orthodox: An orthodox view or method follows established or generally accepted beliefs and practices.
orthodox 指遵循既定、普遍认可的观点或做法。
unorthodox: Something unorthodox departs from conventional or accepted methods or beliefs.
unorthodox 指不遵循传统或公认的方法、观念。
mainstream: Mainstream ideas or activities are accepted or practiced by most people in a group.
mainstream 指某群体中多数人接受或采用的主流观点、做法。
fringe: Fringe ideas or groups lie outside the mainstream; a fringe is also an edge or border.
fringe 可指主流之外的边缘观点或群体，也可以指物体的边缘。
inadvertent: Something inadvertent happens unintentionally, often through inattention.
inadvertent 指无意中发生，常因疏忽造成。
unintentional: Something unintentional is not done on purpose.
unintentional 指并非有意实施或造成。
negligent: Someone negligent fails to take reasonable care or meet an expected duty.
negligent 指未尽到合理注意或应有责任，具有疏忽失职意味。
recklessly: To act recklessly is to disregard the possible risks or consequences.
recklessly 指不顾潜在风险或后果地行事。
reluctantly: To do something reluctantly is to do it despite not wanting to.
reluctantly 指虽然不愿意，仍勉强去做某事。
conceivably: Conceivably means that something is possible to imagine, even if it is unlikely.
conceivably 表示某种情况可以设想、存在可能，即使未必很有希望。
hitherto: Hitherto means until now or until a particular time in the past, especially in formal writing.
hitherto 是较正式的“迄今为止”或“截至当时”。
cohesion: Cohesion is the quality of parts of a group or text holding together as a unified whole.
cohesion 指群体各部分凝聚成整体，或文章各部分衔接紧密。
credibility: Credibility is the quality of being believable or worthy of trust.
credibility 指说法、证据或人物令人信服、值得信任的程度。
credence: Credence is belief or acceptance given to a claim, especially when there is supporting evidence.
credence 指对某种说法给予相信或认可，常建立在证据支持上。
rectify: To rectify a mistake or problem is to correct it or put it right.
rectify 指纠正错误或解决问题，使事情恢复正确状态。
divergent: Divergent ideas, paths, or results move in different directions or become increasingly different.
divergent 指观点、路径或结果朝不同方向发展，或差异逐渐增大。
deduction: Deduction is reasoning from a general rule to a conclusion; it can also mean an amount subtracted.
deduction 指从一般原则推导结论；也可指从总额中扣除的款项。
induction: Induction can mean reasoning from observations toward a general rule, or the act of introducing someone into a role.
induction 可指从具体观察归纳一般规律，也可指入职、就任或入会程序。
deductive: Deductive reasoning applies general premises to reach a particular conclusion.
deductive 指依据一般前提推导出具体结论的演绎式推理。
rigor: Rigor is the strictness and care used in reasoning, research, or carrying out a process.
rigor 指推理、研究或工作过程中严谨、严格和细致的程度。
rigidity: Rigidity is the inability or unwillingness to bend, change, or adapt.
rigidity 指物体缺乏柔韧性，或做法、观点僵化而难以调整。
intangible: Something intangible has no physical form, even though its effects or value may be real.
intangible 指无形、无法触摸，但可能具有实际价值或影响的事物。
discretion: Discretion is careful judgment about what to do or say; it can also be freedom to decide within limits.
discretion 指处事或言语的审慎，也指在一定权限内自行决定的裁量权。
discretionary: Discretionary decisions or spending are optional or left to someone’s judgment rather than required.
discretionary 指由个人判断决定、并非强制要求的事项或支出。
indiscriminate: Indiscriminate actions affect things or people without making careful distinctions.
indiscriminate 指不加区分、不作审慎选择的行为。
equivocal: An equivocal statement is deliberately or inherently open to more than one interpretation.
equivocal 指表述含糊、模棱两可，可能有不止一种解释。
equivocation: Equivocation is the use of ambiguous language to avoid a clear commitment or answer.
equivocation 指利用含糊说法回避明确表态或直接回答。
frank: Someone frank expresses what they really think openly, even when it may be uncomfortable.
frank 指坦率、直接表达真实想法，即使可能令人不快。
candid: Someone candid is honest and open in what they say, without hiding important facts.
candid 指坦诚直言、不隐瞒重要事实或看法。
forthright: A forthright person speaks or acts directly and without unnecessary hesitation.
forthright 指说话或行事直截了当、不拐弯抹角。
tacit: Tacit agreement or knowledge is understood without being explicitly said.
tacit 指虽未明说，却被默认、默许或心照不宣的约定或知识。
tacitly: Tacitly means without saying something directly, but in a way that implies consent or understanding.
tacitly 指虽没有明确说出，却以行动或态度表示默许、默认。
overt: Overt actions or attitudes are open and easily observed rather than hidden.
overt 指公开、明显可见，而不是暗中进行的行为或态度。
covert: Covert actions are deliberately concealed or kept secret.
covert 指有意隐藏、不让人察觉的行动或活动。
unbiased: An unbiased assessment is not unfairly influenced by personal preferences or prejudice.
unbiased 指评价或判断不受个人偏好、成见的不当影响。
corollary: A corollary is a result or conclusion that follows naturally from something already established.
corollary 指从已有事实、原理或结论自然推导出的推论。
verified: Verified information has been checked and shown to be accurate or genuine.
verified 指信息已经查验，确认准确或真实。
propagation: Propagation is the process by which a signal, wave, effect, or idea spreads through a system or space.
propagation 指信号、波、影响或观念在系统或空间中的传播过程。
synchronous: Synchronous events occur in step with one another or are coordinated by a shared timing reference.
synchronous 指事件同步发生，或在共同时间基准下协调运行。
amplitude: Amplitude is the size of a wave or oscillation measured from its central level to a peak.
amplitude 指波形或振荡相对于中心位置到峰值的幅度。
requisite: Something requisite is necessary for a particular purpose or result.
requisite 指达到某一目的或结果所必需的条件或事物。
vicinity: The vicinity is the area close to a particular place.
vicinity 指某地点附近的区域。
scrupulous: Someone scrupulous takes great care to act correctly, honestly, and with attention to detail.
scrupulous 指做事一丝不苟，注重细节并严格遵守原则。
cursory: A cursory look or examination is quick and pays little attention to detail.
cursory 指查看或检查匆匆进行，未深入关注细节。
laconic: A laconic person uses very few words, sometimes appearing unusually brief or reserved.
laconic 指言辞极为简短、惜字如金，有时显得冷淡。
long-winded: A long-winded explanation is unnecessarily lengthy and uses more words than needed.
long-winded 指说明或讲话冗长啰嗦，超过实际需要。
redundancy: Redundancy is unnecessary repetition; in engineering it can also mean backup capacity that improves reliability.
redundancy 指不必要的重复；在工程中也可指用于提高可靠性的冗余备份。
forthcoming: Forthcoming events or publications are expected soon; a forthcoming person is open with information.
forthcoming 可指即将到来的活动或出版物，也可形容人愿意坦诚提供信息。
impending: An impending event is likely to happen very soon, often with a sense of urgency or concern.
impending 指某事迫在眉睫，常带有紧迫或令人担忧的意味。
foresight: Foresight is the ability to anticipate future needs or consequences and prepare for them.
foresight 指预见未来需要或后果，并提前做好安排的能力。
construe: To construe a statement or action is to interpret it in a particular way.
construe 指以某种特定方式理解或解释话语、行为。
transmission: Transmission is the act or process of sending something, such as data, energy, or a disease, from one place to another.
transmission 指数据、能量或疾病等从一处传递到另一处的过程。
analogous: Two things are analogous when they are similar in a relevant way, even though they are not identical.
analogous 指两件事物在某个相关方面具有可类比的相似性，但并不完全相同。
chiefly: Chiefly means mainly or for the most part.
chiefly 表示主要地、大部分地。
commensurate: Something commensurate with a responsibility or achievement is appropriate in size or degree to it.
commensurate with 指某种程度或规模与责任、成果等相称。
comparative: Comparative describes something considered by comparing it with another thing.
comparative 指通过与其他事物比较来考察或描述的。
comprehensible: Something comprehensible can be understood clearly.
comprehensible 指能够被清楚理解、易于领会的。
contiguous: Contiguous places or objects touch one another or share a boundary.
contiguous 指地点或物体彼此相接、共用边界。
continuum: A continuum is a range in which neighboring states blend gradually into one another.
continuum 指相邻状态逐渐过渡、没有明确断点的连续范围。
curative: A curative treatment is intended to cure a condition rather than merely ease its symptoms.
curative 指以治愈疾病为目的，而不只是缓解症状的治疗。
deference: Deference is respectful willingness to accept another person’s judgment or authority.
deference 指出于尊重而愿意听从他人的判断或权威。
deferential: Someone deferential shows respect by giving weight to another person’s wishes or authority.
deferential 指对他人的意愿或权威表现出恭敬、尊重的态度。
descriptive: A descriptive account states how something is, without necessarily saying how it ought to be.
descriptive 指描述事实或现状，而不一定判断其应当如何。
discrimination: Discrimination can mean unfair differential treatment; in technical contexts, it can also mean distinguishing between categories.
discrimination 常指不公正的区别对待；在技术语境中也可指辨别、区分不同类别的能力。
disproportionate: Something disproportionate is too large or too small relative to what it is being compared with.
disproportionate 指相对于比较对象而言过大或过小、不成比例的。
egalitarian: An egalitarian approach supports equal rights, opportunities, or standing for people.
egalitarian 指主张人们享有平等权利、机会或地位的。
equality: Equality is the state of being equal in status, rights, value, or quantity.
equality 指在地位、权利、价值或数量等方面相等的状态。
equitable: An equitable arrangement is fair, taking account of relevant differences in circumstances.
equitable 指考虑具体处境差异后，仍能做到公平合理的。
equity: Equity means fairness in how people are treated or resources are allocated; in finance, it can mean ownership interest.
equity 可指待遇或资源分配上的公平；金融语境中也指所有者权益。
exclusion: Exclusion is the act or condition of leaving someone or something out.
exclusion 指将某人或某物排除在外的行为或状态。
exemption: An exemption is official permission not to follow a rule that normally applies.
exemption 指正式获准不适用通常必须遵守的规则。
fragility: Fragility is the tendency to break, fail, or be harmed under stress.
fragility 指在受压或受冲击时容易损坏、失效或受到伤害的性质。
fundamentally: Fundamentally means at the most basic or important level.
fundamentally 指从最根本、最基本的层面来看。
hypothesize: To hypothesize is to propose a possible explanation that can be examined or tested.
hypothesize 指提出一种可以进一步检验的可能解释或假说。
implicate: To implicate someone is to suggest involvement in wrongdoing; to implicate a factor is to connect it with an effect.
implicate 常指暗示某人牵涉不当行为；也可指表明某因素与某结果有关。
insignificant: Something insignificant is too small or unimportant to matter in context; in statistics it may mean lacking sufficient evidence against a null hypothesis.
insignificant 指在特定情境下影响很小、不重要；统计学中可指缺乏足够证据拒绝原假设。
intelligible: Speech or writing is intelligible when its meaning can be understood.
intelligible 指话语或文字的意思能够被理解。
intersection: An intersection is a place or set where two roads, areas, or groups meet or overlap.
intersection 指道路交叉处，或两个区域、集合相交重叠的部分。
intolerance: Intolerance is unwillingness to accept differing views or people; it can also mean inability to tolerate a substance.
intolerance 指不能容忍不同观点或群体；也可指身体无法耐受某种物质。
inversely: Two quantities vary inversely when one increases as the other decreases according to a specified relationship.
inversely 指两个量按某种反向关系变化，一个增大时另一个减小。
legible: Writing or print is legible when its letters can be recognized and read.
legible 指字迹或印刷文字清晰可辨、能够看清。
perpetually: Perpetually means continuously or so repeatedly that something seems never to stop.
perpetually 指持续不断，或反复得仿佛永不停歇。
prevalence: Prevalence is how widespread a condition or characteristic is in a population at a given time or period.
prevalence 指某种状况或特征在特定时间或时期内于群体中的普遍程度。
preventive: A preventive measure is taken to stop a problem or disease from occurring.
preventive 指为防止问题或疾病发生而提前采取的预防性措施。
propensity: A propensity is a natural tendency or inclination to behave in a particular way.
propensity 指倾向于采取某种行为的习性或趋势。
proportional: Two quantities are proportional when they maintain a constant ratio as they vary.
proportional 指两个量在变化时保持固定比值，成比例。
proportionate: Something proportionate is appropriate in scale or degree relative to the situation.
proportionate 指规模或程度与具体情况相称、不过度的。
restriction: A restriction is a rule or condition that limits what can be done.
restriction 指限制行为或范围的规则、条件。
spurious: A spurious claim, relationship, or result appears valid but is actually misleading or lacks a sound basis.
spurious 指表面看似成立，但实际上具有误导性或缺乏可靠依据的主张、关系或结果。
stipulation: A stipulation is a condition explicitly required as part of an agreement.
stipulation 指协议中明确提出、必须满足的条件。
tentatively: Tentatively means in a cautious or provisional way, without treating the result as final.
tentatively 指谨慎地、暂定地作出判断，而不将其视为最终结论。
tenure: Tenure is the period of holding a position or property; in academia, it can mean a secure continuing appointment.
tenure 指任职或持有财产的期限；在学术界还可指长期、稳定的聘任资格。
tolerable: Something tolerable is unpleasant or imperfect but can still be endured or accepted.
tolerable 指虽不理想或令人不适，但尚可忍受或接受。
tolerance: Tolerance is willingness to accept differences, or the permissible degree of variation from a target.
tolerance 可指对差异的包容；技术领域中也指允许偏离目标值的范围。
tolerant: Someone tolerant accepts differences; a system tolerant of faults can continue to function despite them.
tolerant 指能够包容差异；形容系统时可指即使出现故障仍能继续工作的。
transit: Transit is the act of passing through a place or traveling from one point to another.
transit 指通过某地，或从一处到另一处的运输、通行。
transitional: A transitional stage connects one established state or period to another.
transitional 指连接两个阶段或状态的过渡性的。
transitory: Something transitory lasts only for a short period and is not permanent.
transitory 指只持续短暂时间、并非永久的。
unequivocal: An unequivocal statement is clear and leaves no doubt about the intended meaning.
unequivocal 指陈述明确、毫不含糊，不会对其本意产生疑问。
variability: Variability is the degree to which observations or values differ across cases or over time.
variability 指不同样本之间或随时间变化时，观测值存在差异的程度。
qualification: A qualification can be a required skill or condition; in an argument, it limits how broadly a claim applies.
qualification 可指资格或必要条件；在论证中还指对结论适用范围的限定。
connotation: A connotation is an extra feeling or association a word suggests beyond its literal meaning.
connotation 指词语在字面意义之外引发的情感色彩或联想。
germane: Something germane is closely connected to the topic and useful to the discussion.
germane 指与当前主题密切相关、对讨论有帮助的。
digress: To digress is to move away from the main subject temporarily when speaking or writing.
digress 指说话或写作时暂时偏离主要话题。
digression: A digression is a passage or remark that departs from the main line of discussion.
digression 指偏离主要论述方向的一段话或插叙。
vindicate: To vindicate someone or something is to show that they were right or not to blame.
vindicate 指证明某人正确或无辜，或证明某种观点有道理。
inadvertently: Inadvertently means accidentally, without intending or realizing what happened.
inadvertently 指无意中、不知不觉地做了某事。
negligence: Negligence is failure to exercise the care that a situation reasonably requires.
negligence 指未尽到特定情境下合理应有的注意义务。
commitment: A commitment is a promise or firm decision to devote effort, time, or resources to something.
commitment 指承诺，或坚定地投入时间、精力与资源的决定。
standardize: To standardize is to make methods or products follow a consistent set of rules.
standardize 指使方法、产品等符合统一标准。
fraction: A fraction is part of a whole or a number expressed as one quantity divided by another.
fraction 指整体中的一部分，或用一数除以另一数表示的分数。
brain: The brain controls thought, sensation, and many bodily functions; it can also mean intelligence.
brain 指控制思维、感觉和许多身体活动的大脑，也可借指智力。
cell: A cell is the smallest basic unit of life; it can also be a small room or a unit in a table.
cell 指生物体的基本细胞，也可指小房间或表格中的单元格。
gas: Gas is a state of matter that spreads to fill its container; in American English, gas can also mean gasoline.
gas 指会扩散并充满容器的气态物质；美式英语中还可指汽油。
heat: Heat is thermal energy transferred because of a temperature difference; more generally it means warmth.
heat 指因温差传递的热量，日常也泛指热或温暖。
loss: Loss is the act or experience of losing something, or a reduction in value, amount, or ability.
loss 指失去某物，也可指数量、价值或能力的减少。
mass: Mass is the quantity of matter in an object; it can also mean a large amount or group.
mass 指物体的质量，也可指大量事物或人群。
metal: Metal is a material that usually conducts heat and electricity and can often be shaped.
metal 指通常能够导热、导电且可以加工成形的金属材料。
pile: A pile is a heap of things placed together; to pile things is to stack them up.
pile 指堆在一起的一堆东西；作动词时指把东西堆叠起来。
root: A root anchors a plant and absorbs resources; figuratively it is the origin or basic cause of something.
root 指植物的根；引申为事物的起源、根本原因。
seed: A seed is the part of a plant that can grow into a new plant; it can also mean the beginning of an idea.
seed 指能长成新植物的种子，也可比喻想法的萌芽。
shape: Shape is the outline or form of something; to shape is to influence how it develops.
shape 指外形或形状；作动词时可指塑造、影响事物的发展。
site: A site is a particular place where something happens, is built, or is located; it can also be a website.
site 指某项活动或建筑所在的地点，也可指网站。
size: Size describes how large or small something is, such as its dimensions or amount.
size 指事物的大小、尺寸或规模。
soil: Soil is the upper layer of earth in which plants grow; to soil something is to make it dirty.
soil 指植物生长的土壤；作动词时指弄脏。
solid: A solid has a definite shape and volume; solid can also describe something firm or reliable.
solid 指具有固定形状和体积的固体，也可形容坚固、可靠。
abuse: Abuse is the harmful or improper treatment or use of a person, thing, or power.
abuse 指对人、物或权力的伤害性、不当使用或对待。
ahead: Ahead means in front, further forward, or at an earlier point in the future.
ahead 指在前方、向前，或在未来某个时间之前。
alarm: An alarm is a warning signal, or a feeling of sudden fear or concern.
alarm 指警报、提醒信号，也可指突然的恐惧或担忧。
alive: Someone or something alive is living, not dead; the word can also suggest energy or activity.
alive 指仍有生命、活着，也可形容充满活力。
ally: An ally is a person, group, or country that cooperates with and supports another.
ally 指与另一方合作、给予支持的盟友或伙伴。
amaze: To amaze someone is to surprise them greatly, often in a positive way.
amaze 指使人极为惊讶，常带有赞叹意味。
amuse: To amuse someone is to entertain them or make them laugh.
amuse 指使人感到有趣、开心或发笑。
awake: Someone awake is not sleeping; to awake can mean to stop sleeping or become conscious of something.
awake 指醒着、没有睡觉；也可表示醒来或开始意识到某事。
awful: Awful usually means very bad or unpleasant; it can also intensify a description informally.
awful 通常指非常糟糕、令人不快，也可在非正式表达中加强语气。
band: A band is a group of musicians, or a strip that holds or marks something.
band 指乐队，也可指用于固定或标记的带子、条带。
bar: A bar is a long narrow piece, a place serving drinks, or a rule that prevents something.
bar 可指长条形物体、酒吧，也可指阻止某事的障碍或禁令。
bare: Bare means uncovered, without decoration, or only the minimum necessary.
bare 指未覆盖、没有装饰，或仅有最基本的部分。
bay: A bay is an inlet of the sea; it can also be a marked space in a building or parking area.
bay 指海湾，也可指建筑或停车场中划分出来的区域。
bid: A bid is an offer of money or an attempt to win something; to bid is to make such an offer.
bid 指出价、投标，或争取某物的尝试；作动词时指提出报价。
block: A block is a solid piece or section; to block something is to prevent movement or access.
block 指块状物或区段；作动词时指阻挡、妨碍通行。
bore: To bore someone is to make them lose interest; to bore a hole is to drill into something.
bore 可指使人厌烦，也可指钻孔。
born: Born describes someone coming into life; it is used with be to talk about birth.
born 指出生，通常与 be 连用表示某人在何时何地出生。
burst: To burst is to break open suddenly, or to begin doing something suddenly and forcefully.
burst 指突然爆裂，也可指突然猛烈地开始某个动作。
cap: A cap is a small covering or hat; it can also mean an upper limit on an amount.
cap 指帽子或盖子，也可指数量或金额的上限。
card: A card is a small flat piece used for information, payment, playing games, or identification.
card 指用于记录信息、支付、游戏或身份识别的卡片。
chain: A chain is a series of connected links or events; to chain things is to connect them together.
chain 指链条或相互关联的一连串事物；作动词时指把事物连接起来。
clean: Something clean has no dirt; to clean is to remove dirt or unwanted material.
clean 指干净、无污物；作动词时指清洁、清除污物。
coach: A coach trains people in a skill or sport; a coach can also be a type of bus.
coach 指指导训练的教练，也可指长途客车。
cool: Cool describes a fairly low temperature; informally it can mean impressive or calm.
cool 指凉爽，也可在口语中表示很棒或镇定。
crack: A crack is a narrow break or opening; to crack something is to make it split.
crack 指狭窄的裂缝；作动词时指使其开裂。
crop: A crop is a plant grown for food or other use; it can also be the amount harvested.
crop 指种植供食用或其他用途的作物，也可指收成。
cure: To cure a disease is to end it; a cure is a treatment that makes a disease go away.
cure 指治愈疾病，也可指能使疾病消除的治疗方法。
dash: To dash is to move quickly; a dash is also a short punctuation mark or a small amount.
dash 指猛冲、疾奔；作为名词还可指破折号或少量某物。
deem: To deem something a certain way is to consider or judge it to be so, often formally.
deem 指认为、判定某事具有某种性质，通常用于较正式的表达。
dim: Dim light is not bright; dim can also describe something faint or unclear.
dim 指光线昏暗，也可指微弱、不清晰。
dozen: A dozen is a group of twelve; dozens of something means many of them.
dozen 指十二个；dozens of 在口语中表示几十个或许多。
drag: To drag is to pull something with effort; it can also mean moving slowly or reluctantly.
drag 指费力地拖拉，也可指缓慢、勉强地移动。
ease: Ease is freedom from difficulty or discomfort; to ease something is to make it less severe.
ease 指轻松或舒适；作动词时指减轻困难、疼痛或负担。
edge: An edge is the outer boundary of something; to edge forward is to move slowly and gradually.
edge 指边缘；作动词时也可指缓慢地向前移动。
faint: Something faint is difficult to see, hear, or feel; to faint is to lose consciousness briefly.
faint 指微弱、难以察觉；作动词时指短暂昏厥。
false: Something false is untrue or incorrect; a false impression is a misleading belief.
false 指不真实、不正确；false impression 指错误、误导性的印象。
fan: A fan moves air, and a fan of someone or something is an enthusiastic supporter.
fan 可指风扇，也可指某人或某事物的热心支持者。
fate: Fate is what happens to someone, especially when it seems beyond their control.
fate 指命运，尤其指仿佛超出个人控制的遭遇。
fault: A fault is a mistake or defect; in geology it is a fracture along which rocks have moved.
fault 指过错或缺陷；在地质学中指发生相对位移的断层。
feed: To feed someone is to give them food; to feed data into a system is to supply it as input.
feed 指给人或动物食物，也可指向系统输入数据。
file: A file is a collection of stored information or documents; to file something is to store or formally submit it.
file 指档案或计算机文件；作动词时指归档或正式提交。
fixed: Fixed means firmly attached, not changing, or already arranged in advance.
fixed 指固定的、不变的，或事先确定的。
flag: A flag is a piece of cloth used as a symbol; to flag something is to mark it for attention.
flag 指旗帜；作动词时也指标记需要注意的事项。
flat: Flat means level, smooth, or without much variation; as a noun it can mean an apartment.
flat 指平坦、平整或变化不大；作为名词在英式英语中也指公寓。
float: To float is to remain on the surface of a liquid or move gently in air.
float 指漂浮在液面上，也可指在空中轻轻飘动。
flow: Flow is smooth, continuous movement, especially of a liquid, gas, or information.
flow 指液体、气体或信息等连续、顺畅的流动。
fold: To fold something is to bend it over itself; a fold is the bend created this way.
fold 指把东西折叠起来，或由折叠形成的褶皱。
fond: To be fond of someone or something is to feel affection or liking toward them.
fond of 指喜欢、喜爱某人或某事物。
frame: A frame is a supporting structure or boundary; to frame an idea is to present it in a particular way.
frame 指框架或边框；作动词时也指以某种方式表述、界定一个观点。
fund: A fund is a sum of money set aside for a purpose; to fund something is to provide its money.
fund 指为特定目的准备的资金；作动词时指提供经费。
grade: A grade is a level or mark of achievement or quality; to grade is to assign such a level.
grade 指等级或成绩；作动词时指评分或分级。
admonish: To admonish someone is to warn or criticize them firmly about their behavior.
admonish 指郑重告诫或批评某人的行为，通常希望对方改正。
acquiesce: To acquiesce is to accept something without open protest, even if you do not fully agree.
acquiesce 指虽然不完全赞同，却没有公开反对而默许或接受。
acquiescence: Acquiescence is acceptance without objection, sometimes despite private reservations.
acquiescence 指没有提出异议的默许，有时内心仍有所保留。
acrid: An acrid smell or taste is sharp, bitter, and often unpleasant.
acrid 形容气味或味道刺鼻、辛辣或苦涩，通常令人不适。
accredit: To accredit an institution is to officially recognize that it meets certain standards.
accredit 指正式认可某机构符合特定标准，授予认证资格。
accrue: When benefits or costs accrue, they build up gradually over time.
accrue 指收益、成本或权利随时间逐渐累积。
acquittal: An acquittal is a legal decision that a person has not been proved guilty of a charge.
acquittal 指法院作出的无罪判决，即控方未能依法证明被告有罪。
adduce: To adduce evidence is to present it in support of an argument.
adduce 指举出证据或理由来支持某项论证。
adjourn: To adjourn a meeting is to stop it, usually with the intention of meeting again later.
adjourn 指暂时休会或延期会议，通常计划日后继续。
adjunct: An adjunct is something added to support or supplement a main part.
adjunct 指附加在主体之外、起辅助或补充作用的事物。
admissible: Admissible evidence or information is allowed to be considered under the applicable rules.
admissible 指依照适用规则允许采纳或考虑的证据、信息。
admittedly: Admittedly introduces a fact that is accepted as true, often before a contrasting point.
admittedly 用于承认某个事实，后面常接转折或限制。
admonition: An admonition is a serious warning or expression of disapproval.
admonition 指严肃的警告、劝诫或批评。
adroit: Someone adroit handles difficult situations skillfully and with good judgment.
adroit 指处理复杂事情灵巧、熟练而且判断得当。
affiliation: An affiliation is a formal connection with an organization or institution.
affiliation 指与组织或机构之间的正式隶属、合作或关联关系。
affidavit: An affidavit is a written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation for legal use.
affidavit 指以宣誓或正式确认方式保证真实性、用于法律程序的书面陈述。
affirmation: An affirmation is a statement that something is true or a firm expression of support.
affirmation 指对某事属实的正式确认，或明确表达的支持。
aggregation: Aggregation is the process of combining separate items or measurements into a larger whole.
aggregation 指把独立项目或测量结果汇总为整体的过程。
allegiance: Allegiance is loyalty to a person, country, or cause.
allegiance 指对个人、国家或事业的忠诚与效忠。
allay: To allay a fear or concern is to reduce its intensity.
allay 指缓和恐惧、担忧或疑虑的程度。
allotment: An allotment is a portion of something assigned to a person or purpose.
allotment 指分配给某人或某种用途的一份资源或配额。
aloof: Someone aloof seems emotionally distant or unwilling to become involved.
aloof 指显得冷淡、疏离或不愿参与的人。
altruism: Altruism is concern for other people’s welfare without expecting a personal reward.
altruism 指关心他人福祉、不以个人回报为目的的利他主义。
amalgamate: To amalgamate is to combine different groups or things into one.
amalgamate 指把不同组织或事物合并为一个整体。
amenable: Someone amenable is willing to listen, cooperate, or accept a proposed change.
amenable 指愿意听取意见、配合或接受建议。
ameliorate: To ameliorate a difficult condition is to make it better.
ameliorate 指改善困难或不良状况，但不一定彻底解决。
anachronism: An anachronism is something placed in a historical period where it does not belong.
anachronism 指与所在历史时期不符的人物、观念或物品，属于时代错置。
anathema: Something that is anathema to a person is deeply hated or completely unacceptable to them.
anathema 指对某人极其厌恶或完全不能接受的事物。
antipathy: Antipathy is a strong feeling of dislike or hostility.
antipathy 指强烈的反感、厌恶或敌意。
apathy: Apathy is a lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern.
apathy 指缺乏兴趣、热情或关切的冷漠状态。
aperture: An aperture is an opening through which light or something else can pass.
aperture 指光线或其他东西可以通过的开口；摄影中常指光圈开口。
aphorism: An aphorism is a short, memorable statement expressing a general truth or observation.
aphorism 指简短、精练、容易记住的格言式说法。
apocryphal: An apocryphal story is widely repeated but of doubtful authenticity.
apocryphal 指广为流传、却真实性存疑的故事或说法。
appease: To appease someone is to calm their anger by meeting some of their demands.
appease 指通过满足部分要求来平息某人的愤怒或不满。
append: To append something is to add it at the end of a document or sequence.
append 指把内容附加在文档或序列末尾。
appraise: To appraise something is to assess its value, quality, or importance.
appraise 指评估某物的价值、质量或重要性。
apprehensive: Someone apprehensive feels uneasy because they expect something unpleasant might happen.
apprehensive 指因担心不好的事情可能发生而感到不安。
apprise: To apprise someone of something is to inform them of it, usually formally.
apprise 指通常以较正式的方式把某事告知某人。
arbitrate: To arbitrate a dispute is to make a decision about it as an independent third party.
arbitrate 指作为独立第三方对争议进行仲裁。
arbitration: Arbitration is a way of settling a dispute through a decision by a neutral third party.
arbitration 指通过中立第三方裁决解决争议的仲裁程序。
archaic: An archaic word or custom belongs to an earlier time and is no longer commonly used.
archaic 指属于早期时代、如今已不常使用的词语或习俗。
artless: Someone artless is natural and without pretense, sometimes to the point of being naive.
artless 指自然、不做作，有时也带有天真、不谙世故的含义。
ascribe: To ascribe a quality or cause to something is to regard it as belonging to or resulting from it.
ascribe 指把某种特征、原因或结果归属于某人某事。
assent: Assent is agreement or approval, especially given after a proposal is made.
assent 指对建议或决定表示同意或认可。
assiduous: An assiduous person works carefully and persistently over a long period.
assiduous 指做事勤勉、细致，并能长期坚持。
assimilate: To assimilate information is to understand it and integrate it into what you know.
assimilate 指理解新信息，并把它纳入已有知识；也可指文化同化。
assuage: To assuage a feeling is to make it less painful or intense.
assuage 指缓解悲伤、愧疚、恐惧等情绪的强烈程度。
astute: Someone astute notices important details and makes shrewd judgments.
astute 指观察敏锐、善于判断，能够抓住关键细节。
attainable: An attainable goal is one that can realistically be achieved.
attainable 指有现实可能性实现的目标。
attenuate: To attenuate a signal or effect is to reduce its strength.
attenuate 指削弱信号、影响或其他作用的强度。
aversion: An aversion is a strong dislike of something or a wish to avoid it.
aversion 指对某物强烈反感、希望回避的态度。
avid: Someone avid is extremely eager or enthusiastic about an activity or interest.
avid 指对某种活动或兴趣非常热衷、渴望投入。
avow: To avow something is to state it openly and firmly.
avow 指公开、坚定地声明某种信念、立场或事实。
awry: When a plan goes awry, it develops in an unexpected and troublesome way.
awry 常用于 go awry，表示计划出岔子或事情偏离预期。
baffle: To baffle someone is to confuse them so much that they cannot understand or explain something.
baffle 指使人困惑到难以理解或解释的程度。
banal: Something banal is so ordinary or overused that it feels dull and unoriginal.
banal 指内容过于平庸、陈词滥调，缺少新意。
beguile: To beguile someone is to charm or distract them, sometimes in a deceptive way.
beguile 指使人着迷或分心，有时带有诱骗意味。
belie: To belie an appearance or claim is to show that it is misleading or untrue.
belie 指事实与外表或说法不一致，从而说明其具有误导性。
beleaguer: To beleaguer someone is to trouble or overwhelm them with persistent problems or demands.
beleaguer 指长期不断的问题或要求使某人疲于应付。
benefactor: A benefactor is someone who gives money or help to support another person or organization.
benefactor 指为个人或组织提供资金或帮助的捐助者、恩人。
benevolent: Someone benevolent is kind and wishes good things for others.
benevolent 指心怀善意、愿意帮助他人的仁慈态度。
bequeath: To bequeath something is to leave it to someone in a will.
bequeath 指通过遗嘱把财产或物品留给某人。
bereft: Someone bereft has lost a person or thing they deeply valued.
bereft 指失去珍视的人或事物后感到被剥夺或悲痛。
blatant: Something blatant is very obvious, especially in a way that is offensive or unacceptable.
blatant 指问题或行为明目张胆、十分明显，通常带有负面评价。
blunder: A blunder is a careless or serious mistake, often one that could have been avoided.
blunder 指因粗心或判断不当而犯下的严重错误。
bluff: To bluff is to pretend to have more knowledge, power, or confidence than you actually have.
bluff 指虚张声势，假装比实际更有把握、实力或信息。
backbone: A backbone is the spine; figuratively it can mean the main support of a system.
backbone 本指脊柱；比喻用法指系统或组织的主要支撑。
ballot: A ballot is a vote, a voting paper, or the process of voting.
ballot 指投票、选票或投票程序。
bankruptcy: Bankruptcy is a legal status or process for a person or business unable to pay debts.
bankruptcy 指个人或企业无法偿还债务时适用的破产法律状态或程序。
balancing: Balancing involves keeping opposing demands or forces in a workable relationship.
balancing 指协调相互竞争的要求或作用，使其保持适当平衡。
allot: To allot something is to give a specified share or amount to someone or something.
allot 指把一定份额或数量分配给某人或某项用途。
allowance: An allowance is an amount of money or resources regularly provided, or a permitted amount.
allowance 指定期提供的津贴、额度，也可指允许的数量。
aptly: Aptly means in a way that is particularly appropriate or fitting.
aptly 指表达或做法十分恰当、切中要点。
affable: Someone affable is friendly and easy to talk to.
affable 指态度和蔼、友善，容易交谈。
appliance: An appliance is a device used to perform a particular task, especially in a home.
appliance 指用于完成特定任务的器具，尤其是家用电器。
acoustic: Acoustic relates to sound, especially how it is produced or transmitted.
acoustic 指与声音的产生、传播或声学特性有关的。
actuate: To actuate a mechanism is to cause it to move or start operating.
actuate 指驱动机械装置，使其开始运动或工作。
adjustment: An adjustment is a small change made to improve accuracy, fit, or suitability.
adjustment 指为改善准确度、匹配程度或适用性而进行的调整。
anomalous: An anomalous result differs noticeably from what is usual or expected.
anomalous 形容结果明显偏离常态或预期，并不自动意味着它是错误的。
articulation: Articulation is the clear expression of an idea, or the physical formation of speech sounds.
articulation 指清晰表达思想，也可指语音发音动作。
asymmetric: Asymmetric describes something whose sides, parts, or effects are not balanced or identical.
asymmetric 指两侧、部分或作用不对称、不完全相同。
attested: Attested means supported by recorded evidence or formally confirmed.
attested 指有文献证据支持或经过正式证实的。
clock: A clock measures time; in digital electronics, a clock is a periodic signal used to coordinate operations.
clock 指计时装置；在数字电子学中也指协调操作的周期性时钟信号。
compulsory: Compulsory describes something required by a rule or authority rather than freely chosen.
compulsory 指根据规定或权威要求必须完成的，而非自愿选择的。
confounded: A result is confounded when another factor makes it difficult to isolate the effect of interest.
confounded 指受到其他因素混杂影响，难以单独识别所关注的作用。
correction: A correction is a change that fixes an error or compensates for a known effect.
correction 指纠正错误的修改，也可指对已知偏差进行补偿的修正。
creditable: Creditable describes work or behavior worthy of praise or respect.
creditable 形容表现或工作值得称赞、值得认可，而不等于“可信的”。
credulous: A credulous person is too ready to believe claims without enough evidence.
credulous 指轻信的、对未经充分证实的说法过于容易相信的。
derived: Something derived is obtained from another source, quantity, or idea.
derived 指由其他来源、数值或概念推导、衍生而来的。
disparate: Disparate things are so different that they may be hard to compare or combine.
disparate 形容事物差异显著，难以直接比较或归为一类。
divergence: Divergence is the process or degree of moving apart in direction, opinion, or value.
divergence 指方向、观点或数值逐渐分离的过程或程度。
fidelity: Fidelity is faithfulness to an original or accuracy in reproducing a signal or source.
fidelity 指对原作的忠实程度；技术语境指信号或信息还原的保真度。
impulse: An impulse is a sudden urge or brief force; in signal analysis, it is a short input used to study a system.
impulse 指突然的冲动或短暂的力；信号分析中指用于研究系统的短时输入。
inconsistency: An inconsistency is a lack of agreement between statements, results, or behaviors.
inconsistency 指陈述、结果或行为之间不一致、彼此矛盾之处。
inconspicuous: Something inconspicuous does not attract attention or is difficult to notice.
inconspicuous 指不显眼、不易被注意到的。
incredulous: Someone incredulous finds a claim hard to believe, often expressing disbelief.
incredulous 指因某种说法难以置信而表现出怀疑或不相信。
independence: Independence is freedom from control or influence; in statistics it has a specific probability meaning.
independence 指不受他人控制或影响；统计学中的“独立”还有严格的概率含义。
independent: Independent means not controlled by another; statistical independence requires a specific relationship between probabilities.
independent 指不受他方控制；统计独立还需满足相应的概率关系。
innate: An innate characteristic exists naturally from birth rather than being learned later.
innate 指与生俱来的特性，而不是后天习得的。
latent: Latent describes something that exists but is not yet visible, active, or directly observable.
latent 指已经存在、但尚未显现或不能直接观察到的潜在状态。
leftover: A leftover is something that remains after the main part has been used or taken.
leftover 指主要部分使用或取走后剩下的东西。
lucidity: Lucidity is clarity of expression or thought.
lucidity 指表达或思维清楚、易于理解的程度。
mode: A mode is a way of operating or behaving; in statistics, it is the most frequent observed value.
mode 指运行模式或方式；统计学中指众数，即出现次数最多的值。
nuisance: A nuisance is a source of annoyance; in analysis, a nuisance parameter affects observations but is not the target of interest.
nuisance 指造成困扰的事物；分析中的 nuisance parameter 是影响观测却并非研究目标的参数。
oblique: Oblique means slanting rather than straight, or expressed indirectly.
oblique 指倾斜的，也可形容间接、不直说的表达。
odds: Odds describe the ratio of the probability of an event to the probability that it does not occur.
odds 在概率中指事件发生的概率与不发生的概率之比，不等于概率本身。
opaque: Opaque means not allowing light through, or difficult to understand.
opaque 指不透明；也可形容解释、制度等难以理解。
ostensible: Ostensible describes the reason or purpose presented publicly, which may differ from the real one.
ostensible 指对外宣称或表面上的理由、目的，可能与真实情况不同。
peripheral: Peripheral means located at the edge or less central to the main issue.
peripheral 指处于边缘位置，或不是问题的核心部分。
permissible: Permissible means allowed under the relevant rules or conditions.
permissible 指在有关规定或条件下允许的。
permissive: Permissive describes a person, policy, or environment that allows considerable freedom.
permissive 指宽松的、给予较多自由与许可的态度或制度。
practicable: Practicable describes a plan or action that can actually be carried out.
practicable 形容计划或行动在现实条件下可以实施；不等同于 practical 的“实用”。
predictability: Predictability is the extent to which future behavior or outcomes can be anticipated.
predictability 指未来行为或结果可以被预先判断的程度。
prediction: A prediction is a statement about what is likely to happen, often based on evidence or a model.
prediction 指根据证据、规律或模型对未来结果作出的预测。
presumption: A presumption is something accepted as true until it is challenged or disproved.
presumption 指在遭到反驳或证伪前暂时作为真的推定。
recurrence: Recurrence is the return or repeated occurrence of an event or condition.
recurrence 指事件或状态再次出现、反复发生。
remainder: A remainder is the part left after something has been divided, used, or removed.
remainder 指分配、使用或取走某部分后剩余的部分。
sceptical: Sceptical is a British spelling of skeptical, meaning inclined to question a claim until there is evidence.
sceptical 是 skeptical 的一种英式拼写，意为对未经证实的说法持怀疑态度。
statistical: Statistical means relating to the collection, analysis, or interpretation of numerical data.
statistical 指与数据收集、统计分析或结果解释有关的。
stratum: A stratum is a layer or a distinct subgroup within a larger population.
stratum 指地层、层次；统计抽样中也指总体的一个分层。
surreptitious: Surreptitious describes an action performed secretly to avoid being noticed.
surreptitious 形容偷偷进行、刻意避免被人发现的行为。
suspicion: Suspicion is a belief that something may be wrong or untrue without conclusive proof.
suspicion 指没有确凿证据时产生的怀疑或猜测。
symmetrical: Symmetrical means having matching or balanced parts on opposite sides or around a center.
symmetrical 指相对两侧或围绕中心的部分对应、对称。
tenuous: Tenuous describes a connection, claim, or argument supported by weak evidence.
tenuous 形容联系、说法或论证薄弱，证据不足。
alias: An alias is an alternative name used by a person, file, command, or object.
alias 指别名，可用于人名、文件名、命令或程序对象。
chronological: Chronological describes events arranged in the order in which they happened.
chronological 指按实际发生的先后时间顺序排列的。
chronology: Chronology is the order of events in time or a record arranged in that order.
chronology 指事件的时间先后关系，或依时间顺序编排的记录。
constrained: Constrained means limited by a rule, resource, condition, or other restriction.
constrained 指受到规则、资源或其他条件约束、限制的。
contested: Contested describes a claim or decision that is disputed rather than generally accepted.
contested 指存在争议、尚未获得普遍认可的主张或决定。
demonstration: A demonstration is a practical showing of how something works, or evidence that a claim holds.
demonstration 指展示某物如何运行，也可指通过推演或实验说明主张成立。
discrepant: Discrepant results differ in a way that requires attention or explanation.
discrepant 形容结果存在不一致之处，需要进一步解释。
durability: Durability is the ability to withstand wear, damage, or deterioration over time.
durability 指长期承受磨损、损坏或老化的耐久性。
exactness: Exactness is the quality of being precise and free from approximation in the relevant sense.
exactness 指在有关意义上精确、严格、不含近似的性质。
factual: Factual describes information based on facts rather than opinion or speculation.
factual 指基于事实而非个人意见或猜测的信息。
gradient: A gradient is the rate of change of a quantity with position; informally, it can mean a slope.
gradient 指某个量随空间位置变化的速率；也可泛指坡度。
intercept: An intercept is where a line crosses an axis; to intercept is to stop or capture something along its route.
intercept 指直线与坐标轴的交点或截距；作动词还可指中途拦截。
justified: Justified means supported by good reasons or evidence.
justified 指有充分理由或证据支持、可以合理说明的。
negative: Negative can mean expressing refusal, below zero, or indicating the absence of a tested feature.
negative 可表示否定、小于零，或检测结果未发现所测试的特征。
overestimate: To overestimate is to estimate a quantity, ability, or likelihood as greater than it really is.
overestimate 指把数量、能力或可能性估计得高于实际。
peer: A peer is someone of similar age, rank, or status, often used in academic and professional contexts.
peer 指年龄、地位或职位相近的同辈、同行。
positive: Positive can mean favorable, above zero, or indicating that a tested feature is present.
positive 可表示积极的、大于零，或检测发现了被检验的特征。
precaution: A precaution is an action taken in advance to reduce the risk of harm or failure.
precaution 指事先采取的预防措施，用于降低损害或故障风险。
predictable: Predictable describes an event or behavior that can be anticipated with reasonable confidence.
predictable 指有规律、可以较有把握地预见的。
predictive: Predictive describes information or a model that helps anticipate future outcomes.
predictive 形容能帮助预测未来结果的信息或模型。
probation: Probation is a trial period or a legal arrangement allowing supervision instead of imprisonment.
probation 指试用、考察期；法律上也可指受监督的缓刑安排。
pronounced: Pronounced means very noticeable or strongly marked; it can also be the past participle of pronounce.
pronounced 形容明显、显著的；也可用作 pronounce 的过去分词。
qualified: Qualified means having the necessary credentials, or limited by conditions or exceptions.
qualified 指具有资格；也可指附有限定条件、并非毫无保留的。
reasonable: Reasonable means fair, sensible, or supported by appropriate grounds.
reasonable 指合理、公正，或有适当理由支持。
reasoning: Reasoning is the process of drawing conclusions from information, premises, or evidence.
reasoning 指根据事实、前提或证据进行推理的过程。
slope: A slope is a surface inclination or the rate at which one quantity changes with another.
slope 指斜坡；在图表中也指一个变量随另一变量变化的斜率。
succession: Succession is a series of things following one another, or the process of inheriting a position.
succession 指接连发生的一系列事物，也可指继承职位或权力的过程。
temporal: Temporal means relating to time rather than space, or to ordinary worldly life.
temporal 指与时间有关；也可表示世俗的、非宗教的。
testimonial: A testimonial is a statement expressing support, satisfaction, or personal experience.
testimonial 指表达支持、满意或个人经历的推荐性证言。
timely: Timely describes something happening at a suitable or useful time.
timely 指发生在恰当或有帮助的时机，而非仅仅“准时”。
timing: Timing is the choice or measurement of when an event occurs in relation to other events.
timing 指事件发生时机的安排，或它相对于其他事件的时间测量。
underestimate: To underestimate is to judge a quantity, ability, or risk as smaller than it really is.
underestimate 指把数量、能力或风险估计得低于实际。
unpredictable: Unpredictable describes behavior or events that are difficult to foresee.
unpredictable 指难以预见其发生或变化规律的。
adherence: Adherence is the act of following a rule, plan, or set of instructions.
adherence 指遵守规定、计划或指示的行为。
advisory: An advisory provides guidance or warnings rather than binding orders.
advisory 指提供建议或警示的通知，通常不等于强制命令。
antecedent: An antecedent is something that happened earlier, or a word referred back to by a pronoun.
antecedent 指先前发生的事物；语法中指代词所指回的先行词。
decay: Decay is the gradual reduction, deterioration, or breakdown of something.
decay 指某物逐渐衰减、腐坏或分解的过程。
delineate: To delineate something is to describe its boundaries or details clearly.
delineate 指清楚地描绘事物的边界或详细特征。
demarcation: Demarcation is the act of marking or defining a boundary.
demarcation 指标定或明确划分界限的行为。
derivative: A derivative is something obtained from another source; in calculus, it measures a rate of change.
derivative 指由其他事物衍生的东西；微积分中指表示变化率的导数。
diagnostic: Diagnostic information is used to identify the nature or cause of a problem.
diagnostic 指用于识别问题性质或原因的诊断性信息。
equilibrium: Equilibrium is a state in which opposing effects are balanced.
equilibrium 指相互作用达到平衡、整体状态相对稳定的情况。
foreseeable: Foreseeable means reasonably possible to predict in advance.
foreseeable 指事先可以合理预见的。
generalize: To generalize is to form a broad conclusion from particular examples or apply beyond them.
generalize 指由具体例子归纳出一般结论，或把结论推广到更广范围。
heterogeneous: Heterogeneous describes a mixture of elements that differ in kind or properties.
heterogeneous 指由种类或性质不同的成分组成的异质体系。
homogeneous: Homogeneous describes something whose parts are similar in kind or properties.
homogeneous 指各部分在种类或性质上相似、较为均一的。
operational: Operational means connected with actual operation or ready to function.
operational 指与实际运行有关的，也可指已具备运行条件的。
specification: A specification is a detailed statement of technical or functional requirements.
specification 指对技术或功能要求的详细规定、规范。
ache: An ache is a continuous, often dull pain in part of the body.
ache 指身体某部位持续的、通常较隐隐的疼痛。
acid: An acid is a substance with particular chemical properties, often reacting with bases.
acid 指具有特定化学性质、通常能与碱反应的酸性物质。
acre: An acre is a unit of land area, equal to 4,840 square yards.
acre 指面积单位“英亩”，等于 4,840 平方码。
additional: Additional means extra or added to what already exists.
additional 指在已有数量或内容之外额外增加的。
adore: To adore someone or something is to love them very much.
adore 指非常喜爱、深爱某人或某物。
adorn: To adorn something is to make it more attractive by adding decorations.
adorn 指通过添加装饰使某物更美观。
adult: An adult is a fully grown person; as an adjective, it describes maturity.
adult 指成年人；作形容词时表示成年的、成熟的。
agreement: An agreement is a shared decision or understanding reached by two or more parties.
agreement 指双方或多方达成的协议或一致意见。
album: An album is a collection of music recordings, photographs, or similar items.
album 指音乐专辑、相册或类似物品的合集。
alert: To be alert is to notice things quickly; an alert is also a warning.
alert 形容警觉、反应敏捷；作名词还可指警报或提醒。
alien: Alien means foreign or unfamiliar; in science fiction, an alien is a being from another world.
alien 指外来的、陌生的；科幻作品中也指外星生物。
ample: Ample means enough or more than enough for a particular purpose.
ample 指对某种用途而言充足、绰绰有余的。
angle: An angle is the space between two lines meeting at a point, measured in degrees or radians.
angle 指两条相交线之间的夹角，通常用度或弧度衡量。
apartment: An apartment is a separate home within a larger building.
apartment 指一栋建筑中的独立住宅单元，即公寓套房。
