tough: Tough may describe something difficult, someone resilient, or a material that is hard to break or chew.
tough 可表示“困难的、坚韧的、结实的、难嚼的”，具体含义依语境而定。
skin: Skin is the outer protective covering of a person or animal; it can also mean a surface layer of something.
skin 指人或动物的“皮肤”，也可指其他物体表面的“外层、表皮”。
generation: A generation is a group born in a similar period or the act of producing something.
generation 指年龄相近的“一代人”，也可表示“产生、生成”。
commercial: Commercial relates to business and selling goods; as a noun it can mean an advertisement on television or radio.
commercial 作形容词是“商业的、商用的”；作名词可指电视或广播“广告”。
item: An item is one thing on a list or in a group, such as a product, task, or piece of information.
item 指清单或集合中的“一项、一件”，如商品、任务或信息条目。
reality: Reality means what actually exists or happens, rather than what is imagined or desired.
reality 指实际存在或发生的“现实、真实情况”，与想象或愿望相对。
investment: An investment is money or effort committed now in the hope of a future return or benefit.
investment 指为获得未来回报而投入的“资金、资源或精力”。
discussion: A discussion is a conversation in which people exchange views or examine a subject.
discussion 指交换观点或探讨某个问题的“讨论、商议”。
budget: A budget is a plan for income and spending; it can also mean the amount available for a purpose.
budget 指收入与支出的“预算计划”，也可指可用的“预算金额”。
scientist: A scientist conducts systematic research to increase understanding of the natural or social world.
scientist 指通过系统研究增进对自然或社会世界认识的“科学家”。
victim: A victim is a person harmed by a crime, accident, or other damaging event.
victim 指在犯罪、事故或其他有害事件中遭受伤害的“受害者、受难者”。
attorney: An attorney is a lawyer, especially in American English; attorney can also have a wider legal meaning of an authorized agent.
attorney 在美式英语中通常指“律师”，在法律用语中也可指获授权的代理人。
audience: An audience is the group watching or listening to a performance or presentation; it can also mean the intended readers or users.
audience 指“观众、听众”，也可指文本或产品预期面向的“受众”。
majority: The majority is the larger part or more than half of a group; in voting it may have a technical meaning.
majority 指“多数、大部分”；在投票等制度中可能有特定的法定含义。
senior: Senior can mean older, higher in rank, or more experienced; as a noun it may refer to an older person or a final-year student.
senior 可表示“年长的、级别较高的、资深的”，作名词还可指长者或毕业年级学生。
key: A key opens a lock; figuratively it is something essential, and in computing it can be an input or identifier.
key 可指“钥匙”，引申为“关键、要点”，在计算机语境中也可指“键、键值”。
professional: Professional describes work requiring specialized training or someone paid to do it; as a noun it means such a worker.
professional 可表示“专业的、职业的”，作名词是从事专业工作的人员。
customer: A customer buys goods or services; a client more often receives ongoing professional services.
customer 指购买商品或服务的“顾客”，而 client 更常用于持续的专业服务关系。
participant: A participant is a person who takes part in an activity, event, or study.
participant 指参与活动、会议或研究的“参与者、参加者”。
video: Video is recorded moving imagery, or the medium used to record, transmit, and display it.
video 指录制的“视频、影像”，也指相关的记录与传输媒介。
restaurant: A restaurant is a business where food is prepared and served to customers.
restaurant 指为顾客制作和供应餐食的“餐馆、饭店”。
concerned: Concerned can mean worried about something or involved in a particular matter; the two senses should not be confused.
concerned 可表示“担忧的”，也可表示“有关的、涉及其中的”，两种用法需要按语境区分。
recall: To recall is to remember something or officially call a product back; recall is also a noun for memory or a product recall.
recall 可指“回忆起”，也指官方“召回”产品；作名词有“记忆、召回”等义。
version: A version is a particular form, edition, or interpretation of something.
version 指某事物的一个“版本、形式或解释方式”。
plane: A plane can be an aircraft, a flat surface in geometry, or a carpenter's tool for smoothing wood.
plane 可指“飞机”，也指几何中的“平面”，或用于刨木材的“刨子”。
client: A client is a person or organization receiving professional services; in computing, a client requests services from a server.
client 指接受专业服务的“客户、委托人”；计算机中指向服务器请求服务的“客户端”。
variety: Variety refers to diversity or a particular type; a variety of means several different kinds of.
variety 可表示“多样性、种类”；a variety of 表示“各种各样的”。
involved: Involved may mean taking part in something or being complicated and difficult to follow.
involved 可表示“参与其中的、有关的”，也可表示“复杂难懂的”。
investigation: An investigation is a systematic inquiry intended to establish facts, often about an incident or problem.
investigation 指为查明事实而进行的系统“调查、研究”，常涉及事件或问题。
nuclear: Nuclear refers to an atomic nucleus or to energy from nuclear reactions; nuclear family has a different social meaning.
nuclear 通常指“原子核的、核能的”；nuclear family 则是社会学中的“核心家庭”。
researcher: A researcher is someone who investigates a topic systematically to develop knowledge or evidence.
researcher 指系统研究某个主题以获得知识或证据的“研究人员”。
conflict: A conflict is a serious disagreement, struggle, or incompatibility; to conflict means to be inconsistent.
conflict 可表示“冲突、争执、矛盾”；作动词表示“不一致、抵触”。
crisis: A crisis is a moment or period of severe difficulty that requires urgent decisions or action.
crisis 指需要紧急判断或行动的严重“危机、紧要关头”。
stick: A stick is a long thin piece of material; to stick can mean to attach, remain fixed, or continue despite difficulty.
stick 作名词可指“棍、棒”；作动词可指“粘住、卡住、坚持”。
normal: Normal means usual or expected; in statistics it can specifically describe the normal distribution.
normal 通常指“正常的、通常的”；在统计学中可特指“正态分布的”。
driver: A driver operates a vehicle; in computing it is software that controls hardware, and figuratively it can mean a key cause.
driver 可指“司机”，计算机中指“驱动程序”，也可比喻某种变化的主要推动因素。
screen: A screen displays images, separates spaces, or shields something; to screen may mean to examine, filter, or show a film.
screen 可指“屏幕、隔板、屏障”；作动词可表示“筛查、筛选、放映”。
facility: A facility is a building or equipment provided for a purpose; the word can also mean ease or skill in doing something.
facility 常指为某目的提供的“设施、场所”，也可表示做事的“熟练、轻巧”。
identity: Identity is who or what someone is, or the characteristics that distinguish them; in mathematics an identity is an equality true for all allowed values.
identity 指“身份、同一性、特征”；在数学中“恒等式”是在允许取值下始终成立的等式。
border: A border is a boundary between areas or along an edge; to border means to share a boundary or decorate an edge.
border 指“边界、边境、边缘”；作动词可表示“毗邻、在边缘加饰”。
equipment: Equipment is the tools, machinery, and other items needed for a task; it is normally uncountable in standard English.
equipment 指完成任务所需的“设备、装备”，在标准英语中通常是不可数名词。
contrary: Contrary means opposite in nature or direction; “contrary to” contrasts with a claim, while “on the contrary” corrects a preceding claim.
contrary 表示性质或方向相反；contrary to 意为“与……相反”，on the contrary 通常用来直接纠正前述说法。
distortion: Distortion is a change that makes a shape, sound, measurement, or account inaccurate or misleading.
distortion 指形状、声音、测量结果或叙述发生失真、扭曲；不一定是故意歪曲。
prescribe: To prescribe is to authorize a medicine or treatment, or to set out a rule or required course of action.
prescribe 可指医生开具药物或疗法，也可指规则、制度规定必须采取的做法。
currently: Currently means at the present time; it does not imply that the situation will necessarily change soon.
currently 意为“目前、现在”，本身并不表示这种情况很快就会改变。
anymore: Anymore normally means 'any longer' in negatives and questions; in some regional varieties, affirmative 'anymore' can mean 'nowadays'.
anymore 常用于否定句、疑问句，表示“不再、如今还”；肯定句中的用法带有地区特点。
euphemism: A euphemism is a milder expression used instead of one that may sound harsh, direct, or embarrassing.
euphemism 指委婉语，用较温和的说法代替可能显得生硬、直白或令人尴尬的表达。
peruse: To peruse is to read or examine something; historically it often implied careful attention, but modern usage may simply mean looking through it.
peruse 指阅读、查看；传统用法常强调仔细研读，但现代英语里也可表示一般性浏览，需看语境。
notorious: Notorious describes someone or something widely known for a negative reason.
notorious 指“臭名昭著的”，强调因坏事而广为人知，而不是一般意义上的“著名”。
infamous: Infamous means famous for something disgraceful or shocking, often with stronger moral condemnation than notorious.
infamous 指因可耻、恶劣的事情而声名狼藉，通常比 notorious 带有更强的道德谴责。
circumspect: Someone circumspect is careful to consider risks and consequences before acting or speaking.
circumspect 指言行审慎、考虑周全，特别强调对风险和后果保持警惕。
complacent: Complacent means too satisfied with the current situation to notice problems or take needed action.
complacent 指自满、安于现状，以至忽视问题或不再采取必要行动。
complaisant: Complaisant means willing to please or accommodate others; it does not mean self-satisfied.
complaisant 指殷勤、乐于顺从他人意愿；与表示“自满”的 complacent 不是同义词。
dogmatic: Dogmatic describes a person who asserts beliefs as unquestionably true and resists discussion or counterevidence.
dogmatic 指武断、教条，把自己的观点视为不容质疑的真理，不愿考虑讨论或反证。
reticent: Reticent means reluctant to speak or reveal thoughts, often on a particular subject.
reticent 指不愿开口或不愿透露想法，常指对某一话题有所保留。
taciturn: Taciturn describes someone habitually inclined to speak very little.
taciturn 指生性寡言、沉默少语，强调一贯的说话习惯。
concurrence: Concurrence can mean agreement in opinion or the occurrence of events at the same time.
concurrence 可指意见一致、同意，也可指若干事件同时发生；两种用法不可混淆。
presuppose: To presuppose something is to assume it must be true or already exist before an argument or action can make sense.
presuppose 指预先假定某事为真或已存在，作为论证或行动能够成立的前提。
pretext: A pretext is a reason given to conceal the real motive for doing something.
pretext 指借口、托词，强调公开给出的理由掩盖了真正动机。
dwindle: To dwindle is to become gradually smaller in size, amount, strength, or importance.
dwindle 指数量、规模、力量或重要性逐渐减少、衰退。
degrade: To degrade is to lower quality, status, or performance, or to break down a material chemically or biologically.
degrade 可指使质量、地位或性能下降，也可指物质发生化学或生物降解。
disintegrate: To disintegrate is to break apart into smaller pieces or to lose cohesion and structure.
disintegrate 指分裂、瓦解，既可指物理碎裂，也可指组织或整体失去凝聚力。
contrive: To contrive is to devise or arrange something through ingenuity, sometimes in an artificial or manipulative way.
contrive 指设法构想或安排某事，有时暗示人为设计、刻意操纵或显得不自然。
specious: Specious describes an argument that appears convincing but is actually unsound or misleading.
specious 指论证“貌似有理而实则站不住脚”，不能简单译成“有说服力”。
ascetic: Ascetic describes severe self-discipline and the deliberate avoidance of comfort or pleasure, especially for spiritual reasons.
ascetic 指苦行、节欲、自我克制，常指出于宗教或精神追求而刻意放弃享受。
canonical: Canonical means accepted as authoritative or standard within a tradition, field, or system.
canonical 指被某一传统、学科或体系认可为权威、规范或标准的。
complicity: Complicity means involvement in another person’s wrongdoing, especially through cooperation or knowing assistance.
complicity 指共谋、串通或对不当行为的参与，通常包含明知而协助的意味。
unassuming: Unassuming describes someone modest who does not seek attention or emphasize their own importance.
unassuming 指谦逊、不摆架子、不刻意引人注目。
intractable: Intractable describes a problem that is very difficult to resolve, or a person who is hard to manage or persuade.
intractable 可指问题棘手、难以解决，也可指人难以劝服或管束。
obfuscate: To obfuscate is to make information or reasoning difficult to understand, sometimes deliberately.
obfuscate 指把信息或论证弄得含混难懂，有时暗示故意混淆视听。
illuminate: To illuminate is to light up something or to make an idea easier to understand.
illuminate 既可指照亮，也可指通过解释、证据使问题更清晰。
collate: To collate is to gather and arrange documents or information in a deliberate, comparable order.
collate 指汇集并按一定次序整理文件或资料，也可指核对不同文本版本。
aver: To aver is to state something confidently as true, often in formal or legal language.
aver 指郑重断言、坚称某事属实，多用于正式或法律语境。
outwardly: Outwardly describes how someone or something appears on the outside, possibly in contrast with an inner reality.
outwardly 指外表上、表面看来，常暗示与内心或实际情况可能不同。
prosaic: Prosaic means ordinary, practical, or lacking imagination; in literary contexts it can also relate to prose.
prosaic 常指平淡、乏味或缺乏想象力；在文学语境中也可表示散文式的。
stationary: Stationary means not moving or changing position; it is not a word for writing supplies.
静止的、不移动的；与表示文具的 stationery 发音相同，但拼写和意义不同。
stationery: Stationery means writing materials, such as paper, envelopes, and pens.
文具、书写用品，如纸张、信封和笔；不要与 stationary（静止的）混淆。
loose: Loose describes something not firmly fixed, fastened, or tight; it is usually an adjective.
松的、未固定牢的；通常是形容词。注意不要误写为 lose（失去）。
excess: Excess is an amount more than needed or allowed; as an adjective it means additional or surplus.
过量、超出所需或限额的部分；作形容词可表示额外的、剩余的。
convenient: Convenient means easy or suitable for a particular purpose, time, or person—not necessarily comfortable.
方便的、适宜的，强调时间、地点或安排省事；不一定表示身体上的舒适。
ironic: Ironic describes a contrast between what is said, expected, or intended and what is actually true.
具有反讽或讽刺意味的；强调说法、期待或意图与实际结果之间的反差。
sarcastic: Sarcastic remarks often use cutting or mocking irony to criticize or ridicule someone.
挖苦的、尖刻讽刺的；通常带有嘲弄或批评他人的意图。
immigrant: An immigrant is a person who moves into another country to live there; the viewpoint is the destination country.
移民（迁入者）；从迁入国角度描述来到当地定居的人。
emigrant: An emigrant is a person who leaves their home country to live elsewhere; the viewpoint is the country of departure.
移民（迁出者）；从原居国角度描述离开本国定居他处的人。
ingenious: Ingenious describes a clever, original solution or device that shows inventiveness.
巧妙的、有独创性的，尤其形容办法或设计富有创造性。
ingenuous: Ingenuous describes someone innocent, frank, or lacking in worldly sophistication.
天真坦率的、不谙世故的；并非 ingenious（巧妙的）。
affective: Affective concerns emotions, feelings, or mood; it differs from effective, which means producing results.
情感的、情绪方面的；与 effective（有效的）不同。
exasperate: To exasperate is to make someone extremely annoyed or impatient, often through repeated behavior.
使十分恼怒、使不耐烦，常指反复发生的事情令人生气。
obsolescent: Obsolescent means becoming outdated or falling out of use, but not necessarily obsolete yet.
正在过时的、逐渐被淘汰的；程度上比 obsolete（已过时的）更强调过程。
disprove: To disprove a claim is to show, using evidence or reasoning, that it is false.
证伪、证明某个主张不成立；不同于仅仅尚未得到证明。
prejudice: Prejudice is an unfair preconceived judgment or attitude, especially toward a person or group.
偏见、成见，指未充分依据事实就形成的判断或态度。
practise: Practise is the usual British spelling of the verb meaning to rehearse or carry out an activity; American English normally uses practice.
练习或从事某项活动（英式英语动词拼写）；美式英语通常写作 practice。
equivocate: To equivocate is to speak ambiguously or evasively, often to avoid committing to a clear answer.
含糊其词、闪烁其词，常为了回避明确答复。
determinate: Determinate means having a definite or fixed form, extent, or outcome; in technical contexts the meaning depends on the field.
确定的、有明确界限或形式的；在专业语境中还可能有特定定义。
injection: Injection is the act of introducing a substance, signal, or input into a system; in medicine it often means giving a shot.
注入、注射；也可指向系统输入物质、信号或测试激励，含义取决于语境。
detector: A detector is a device or system that senses and identifies a signal, event, substance, or particle.
探测器、检测装置，用于感知或识别信号、事件、物质或粒子。
latch: A latch is a fastening device; in electronics, it is a circuit that holds a state until its control condition changes.
门闩、搭扣；电子学中指在控制条件改变前保持状态的锁存器。
exactitude: Exactitude means the quality of being highly accurate or exact, especially in measurement or expression.
精确、严谨，强调测量或表达达到高度准确的程度。
abnegate: To abnegate is formally or deliberately to reject or give up a right, desire, or responsibility, especially through self-denial.
正式放弃、克制或否定（权利、欲望、责任等）；常带有主动自我克制的意味，不只是“丢失”。
abdication: Abdication is the formal act of giving up a throne, office, or important responsibility.
退位、让位；也可引申为放弃本应承担的重要责任，通常强调主动退让。
abstemious: An abstemious person practices restraint in eating or drinking, and more generally avoids indulgence.
饮食节制的、不贪杯的；引申为克制享乐的。侧重点是自律而非贫困。
abject: Abject describes an extremely miserable, degraded, or humiliating condition, or an attitude of complete submission.
极其悲惨的、卑微屈辱的；也可形容彻底屈服。常见搭配 abject poverty（赤贫）。
abolitionist: An abolitionist actively advocates ending an institution or practice, especially the historical system of slavery.
废除主义者；历史语境中尤指主张废除奴隶制的人，而非一般改革支持者。
acclamation: Acclamation is an enthusiastic public expression of approval, sometimes used to select or endorse someone without a formal vote.
欢呼赞同、热烈拥护；也指以鼓掌或欢呼方式推举、通过，而非逐一正式投票。
accoutrement: An accoutrement is an accessory or piece of equipment used for a particular activity, often appearing in the plural.
（某活动的）装备、配件或行头；常用复数 accoutrements，可带幽默或正式文体色彩。
accession: Accession can mean formally coming to a position of authority, joining a treaty or organization, or the addition of an item to a collection.
就任、即位；加入条约或组织；（馆藏等）新入藏物。具体义项依制度或专业语境而变。
accounting: Accounting is the process or profession of recording and reporting financial transactions; in other contexts it can mean explaining or taking account of something.
会计、财务核算；accounting for 还可表示解释、说明或把某因素计入考量，不能一律译成“会计”。
acerbic: Acerbic speech or criticism is sharp, biting, and often harsh; the word can also mean sour or acidic in taste.
（言语、批评）尖刻犀利的；也可形容味道酸涩。比单纯的“直接”更有锋芒。
acquit: To acquit someone is to find them not guilty in a court of law; it does not necessarily prove what actually happened.
宣判无罪、裁定罪名不成立；这是司法结论，不能据此断言事实已被完全查清。
acquisition: Acquisition is the act of obtaining something or the thing obtained; in business it often means one company taking ownership of another.
获得、习得、收购；可指获得的物品，也可指公司并购。language acquisition 指语言习得。
acquisitive: Acquisitive describes an eagerness to obtain possessions, wealth, or companies, sometimes suggesting excessive materialism.
渴望获取或占有的，尤其偏向财物、资产；可能含贪得之意，与 inquisitive（好奇好问）不同。
acumen: Acumen is the ability to make sound judgments quickly, especially in business or a specialized field.
敏锐的判断力、洞察力，强调对复杂情况作出准确决策的能力；business acumen 为商业眼光。
adamant: Someone who is adamant is firm and unwilling to change an opinion or decision, even under pressure.
态度坚决、毫不动摇的；强调不愿改变立场，不必然意味着正确或顽固。
adaptation: Adaptation is a change that makes something suitable for new conditions; it can also mean a new version of a work in another medium.
适应、调整；也指改编作品。biological adaptation 为生物适应特征，film adaptation 为影视改编。
adapted: Adapted means modified to suit a purpose or new conditions; as a participle it can describe how something has become adjusted.
经过调整或改造的、适应了的；可用于改编文本、适配设备或环境适应，须结合语境选择。
additive: An additive is a substance added to change a product’s properties; as an adjective, additive means involving addition or cumulative effects.
添加剂；作形容词表示加法性的、可累加的。additive effect 指效应相加，不等于增强作用。
adept: Adept describes someone who is highly skilled at an activity; as a noun, an adept is a skilled practitioner.
熟练的、擅长的；常接 at 或 in。作名词可指能手、行家。
adieu: Adieu is a farewell, usually formal, literary, or final-sounding; it is borrowed from French.
告别、再见，语气较正式或带终别意味；不像日常 bye 那样随意。
adjournment: Adjournment is the formal suspension or postponement of a meeting or legal proceeding, often until a specified time.
休会、休庭或延期；通常强调程序性的暂停，未必意味着会议或审理彻底结束。
advocacy: Advocacy means public support or active campaigning for a cause, policy, or group, not necessarily legal representation.
倡导、支持和游说某项事业或政策；不一定是律师在法庭上的代理。
aggrandize: To aggrandize is to increase the power, status, or reputation of someone or something, often excessively.
扩大权势、提高地位或声望；self-aggrandize 常有自我吹捧、自抬身价的贬义。
alacrity: Alacrity is cheerful readiness or prompt enthusiasm in taking action, not simply high physical speed.
欣然敏捷、爽快积极；强调乐意立即行动，而不单是动作迅速。
antithesis: An antithesis is a direct opposite or sharply contrasting idea; in rhetoric, it can also refer to a balanced contrast of clauses.
正相反的人或事物、对立面；修辞学中指对照、对偶式的反衬结构。
antiquated: Antiquated means old-fashioned and no longer well suited to present needs; it often carries criticism.
陈旧过时的、不合时宜的，往往带批评意味；与 antique（古董）并非同义。
arcane: Arcane means known or understood by only a few people, especially because the subject is highly specialized or obscure.
晦涩冷僻、只有少数内行懂的；不一定是故意保密，也不等同于“神秘主义”。
arduous: Arduous work or a journey demands prolonged effort because it is difficult, exhausting, or complex.
艰苦费力的、耗费巨大精力的；可形容工作、训练或旅程，而非只有危险。
asperity: Asperity means harshness in tone or behavior; it can also refer to roughness or difficult conditions.
言辞或态度的尖刻严厉；也可指粗糙、环境艰难，具体含义由搭配决定。
auspicious: Auspicious describes signs, timing, or events that seem favorable and promise future success.
吉兆的、预示顺利的；常形容开端、时机或征兆，而非单纯“幸运”。
afflict: To afflict someone is to cause persistent suffering, distress, or hardship, especially from illness or misfortune.
使长期遭受痛苦、疾病或困境；通常是较持续的折磨，不只是使人短暂不快。
affront: An affront is an action or remark perceived as a deliberate insult to dignity or respect; as a verb, to affront is to offend.
冒犯、侮辱，尤指伤害尊严或受尊重感的行为；可作名词或动词。
ailment: An ailment is a physical disorder or health complaint, often less serious than a major disease.
小病、身体不适或疾患；常指相对轻微的问题，但不表示一定无需治疗。
sex: Sex can refer to a biological classification, sexual activity, or the sex of an individual; the intended sense depends on context.
可指生物学上的性别类别，也可指性行为；具体含义要根据上下文判断，不能把不同概念混为一谈。
tow: To tow a vehicle is to pull it with another vehicle; in tow can also mean accompanying or following someone.
拖曳、牵引车辆；in tow 也可表示有人或某物跟随、随行，不一定在实际拖拉。
adventure: An adventure is an unusual, exciting or sometimes risky experience; the word may emphasize discovery rather than danger.
冒险经历、奇遇；通常具有新鲜或刺激的特点，但不意味着一定有危险。
commend: To commend is to praise or formally recommend someone or something; commendable means deserving praise.
称赞、表扬；也可正式推荐某人或某事。与 command（命令）不能混淆。
nurse: A nurse is a professional who provides nursing care; as a verb it may mean to care for someone or harbor a feeling.
护士；作动词可指护理、照顾，也可指怀有某种情绪或想法，如 nurse a grudge（心怀怨恨）。
papers: Papers may mean documents, academic articles, or newspapers; in some contexts they are official identification documents.
文件、资料；学术论文（复数）；也可能指报纸或证件。不要固定译为“纸张”。
settled: Settled can describe a dispute that has been resolved, a person who has become established, or a place that is inhabited.
可表示争议已解决、生活或工作已安顿，也可表示有人定居；含义取决于搭配。
tongue: Tongue is the organ in the mouth; figuratively it can mean a language, way of speaking, or sharp speech.
舌头；引申为语言、说话方式或尖刻的言语，如 mother tongue（母语）。
astonish: To astonish is to surprise someone greatly, often with something unexpected or remarkable.
使大为惊讶、使震惊；程度通常比普通的 surprise 更强。
cheek: A cheek is either side of the face; informally cheek can also mean impudence or disrespectful boldness.
面颊；在英式口语中也可指厚脸皮、无礼的大胆，如 have the cheek to do something。
estate: An estate is property, especially land and buildings; it can also mean the assets left by someone after death.
地产、庄园或不动产；也指死者留下的全部财产。real estate 是房地产。
flash: A flash is a sudden brief burst of light; it can also mean a sudden appearance or an instance of quick inspiration.
闪光、瞬间出现的亮光；还可指突然闪现或灵光一现。flash memory 则是闪存。
knight: A knight was a mounted warrior in medieval Europe; today knight can also denote an honorary title in some countries.
骑士，最初指中世纪骑马作战的武士；现代也可指授勋获得骑士称号的人。
ward: A ward is a section of a hospital, a local electoral district, or a person under another's legal guardianship.
病房或医院科室、选区；法律语境中也可指受监护人。ward off 表示抵挡、防止。
divine: Divine means relating to a god or gods; it can also describe something exceptionally pleasant or beautiful.
神的、神圣的；口语或文学中也可表示极美好、令人陶醉的。作动词可指推测或占卜。
drama: Drama refers to plays or the art of theater; informally it may describe an emotionally intense event or conflict.
戏剧、戏剧艺术；日常语境中也可指一场充满冲突或情绪起伏的事件。
empty: Empty means containing nothing or lacking people; figuratively it may mean meaningless or emotionally unfulfilled.
空的、没有内容物的；也可指空无一人，或言语空洞、内心空虚。
protest: To protest is to express strong disagreement, publicly or formally; a protest can be a demonstration or an objection.
抗议、提出异议；名词既可指示威活动，也可指正式反对意见。
row: Row /roʊ/ means a line of things or seats; in British English row /raʊ/ can mean a noisy argument.
读 /roʊ/ 时多指一排、一行；在英式英语中读 /raʊ/ 时可指吵架、争执，注意读音与词义。
shoot: To shoot can mean to fire a weapon, photograph or film a scene, or grow quickly from a plant.
射击；也可指拍摄照片或影片，或植物迅速抽芽。具体含义须看宾语。
upper: Upper means situated above something else; it can also refer to the top part of an object or a social class.
上部的、较高的；也可指物件的上层部分或社会阶层，如 upper class（上层阶级）。
hearing: Hearing is the ability or act of perceiving sound; in law it is a formal session where evidence or arguments are heard.
听力、听见的过程；法律语境中还指听证会或法庭审理。
impression: An impression is an idea or feeling formed about something; it may also be a physical mark or a printed copy.
印象、感觉或初步看法；也可指压痕、印迹或印刷的一次印次。
intellect: Intellect is the ability to think, understand and reason; it emphasizes mental capacity rather than learned facts alone.
理解、思考和推理的智力；重在心智能力，而不只是已掌握的知识。
tradition: A tradition is a belief or practice passed down through generations; it may also mean an established custom within a group.
传统、世代传承的习俗或观念；也可指某个团体长期形成的惯例。
altogether: Altogether means completely or in total; it differs from all together, which means in one group or place.
完全地、总共；要区别 all together（所有人或事物在一起）。
err: To err is to make a mistake or reach a wrong judgment; err on the side of caution means to choose the safer option.
犯错、判断失误；err on the side of caution 表示宁可更加谨慎。
footnote: A footnote is a note printed at the bottom of a page; figuratively it may mean a detail of lesser importance.
脚注，通常位于页底；比喻用法中也可指不太重要的附带事项。
avail: Avail means use or benefit, especially in to no avail (without success); avail oneself of means to make use of something.
效用、帮助；to no avail 表示徒劳无功，avail oneself of 表示利用某种机会或资源。
innocent: Innocent can mean not guilty of wrongdoing; it can also mean harmless, inexperienced or unaware.
无罪的、清白的；也可指无害、天真、不谙世事的，并不一定涉及法律责任。
intention: An intention is a plan or purpose behind an action; it does not necessarily imply that the action was carried out.
意图、打算或目的；有意图并不代表行动已经实施。
plenty: Plenty means a large amount or more than enough; plenty of works with countable and uncountable nouns.
大量、充足；plenty of 可修饰可数与不可数名词，通常表示数量足够有余。
pointed: Pointed can mean having a sharp end; of a remark or question, it means direct and deliberately critical.
尖的、有尖端的；形容评论或提问时表示尖锐、直截了当，往往带有批评意味。
shade: Shade is an area protected from direct light; it can also be a color variation or a subtle difference in meaning.
阴凉处、遮阴；也可指某种色调或细微差别，如 shades of meaning（细微的词义区别）。
tower: A tower is a tall, narrow structure; to tower over means to be much taller or more imposing than others.
高塔、塔楼；tower over 表示高出许多，也可比喻远胜于他人。
vision: Vision means the ability to see, an imagined future, or a clear idea guiding action; distinguish it from actual sight.
视觉；也可指对未来的愿景、设想或明确的长远目标。
accuse: To accuse someone of something is to claim they did something wrong; an accusation is not proof of guilt.
指控、谴责某人做错事；accuse somebody of doing something，但指控本身并非定罪证据。
breast: Breast is the chest area or mammary organ; it may also mean the front part of a bird or an animal.
胸部、乳房；也可指鸟类或其他动物的胸肉部分，具体用法随语境变化。
flight: Flight can mean an aircraft journey, the act of flying, or escape from danger; a flight of stairs is a continuous set of steps.
飞行、航班；也可指逃离、逃跑；a flight of stairs 是一段连续楼梯。
folk: Folk can mean people collectively, family or parents informally, or traditional culture as in folk music.
人们、民众；口语中也可指家人或父母，folk music 则是民间音乐。
guilt: Guilt can mean responsibility for wrongdoing or the painful feeling of having done something wrong.
罪责、有罪状态；也可指内疚、负罪感，两者不是同一个概念。
reading: Reading is the act of interpreting written text; it can also be a measurement or someone's interpretation of a situation.
阅读；也可指仪表读数、测量结果，或对情形的一种解读。
touched: Touched can mean physically contacted; emotionally, it means moved by kindness or sympathy.
接触过的；形容情绪时指受到感动，与 touchy（易怒、敏感）不同。
arrest: To arrest someone is to take them into legal custody; arrest can also mean to stop a process or attract attention.
逮捕、拘留；还可指使进程停止，或引起注意，如 arrest attention。
rob: To rob is to steal from a person or place, usually by force or threat; steal normally takes the thing stolen as its object.
抢劫某人或某地，常涉及威胁或暴力；rob somebody of something 与 steal something from somebody 句法不同。
wounded: Wounded means injured, especially by weapons or in conflict; figuratively it can mean hurt emotionally.
受伤的，尤其指遭武器或冲突所伤；也可比喻感情受到伤害。
drawing: Drawing may mean the act of drawing or the resulting illustration; a drawing can also be a random selection or lottery.
绘画活动或图画；也可指抽签、抽奖活动，须结合语境判断。
load: A load is something carried or a quantity of work; to load can mean put things onto a vehicle or bring data into memory.
负载、装载物、工作量；作动词可指装货，也可指计算机加载数据。
marked: Marked means noticeable or pronounced; in another context it means carrying a label, mark or identification.
显著的、明显的；也可指有标记的、已标注的。a marked improvement 是显著改善。
novel: As a noun, a novel is a long work of fiction; as an adjective, novel means new, original or previously unknown.
名词指长篇小说；形容词指新颖的、前所未有的。词性不同，含义也不同。
shame: Shame is the painful feeling associated with dishonor or embarrassment; it can also mean something regrettable.
羞耻、羞愧；口语 a shame 也可指令人遗憾或可惜的事。
attach: To attach is to fasten or connect; it may also mean to assign responsibility or importance to something.
附上、连接；也可指把责任、重要性或某种属性归于某事，如 attach importance to。
brilliant: Brilliant means exceptionally clever or impressive; literally it can also mean very bright or shining.
杰出的、极聪明的、非常出色的；本义也可指明亮、闪耀的。
compel: To compel is to force someone to act, often by authority, necessity or strong pressure; it is stronger than encourage.
迫使、强制某人做某事，可能出于权威、现实压力或必要性；语气强于鼓励。
convict: As a verb, convict means find someone guilty in court; as a noun, a convict is a person found guilty of a crime.
作动词表示法庭宣判有罪；作名词指被判有罪的人。名词、动词重音有所不同。
furnish: To furnish means provide furniture, or more generally supply information, materials or something needed.
为房间配备家具；更广泛地指提供资料、物品或所需资源。
republic: A republic is a state whose head of state is not a hereditary monarch, although political systems vary greatly among republics.
共和国，通常指国家元首并非世袭君主的政体；不同共和国的政治制度可能差异很大。
savage: Savage can mean violently fierce or cruel; historically it was also used as a derogatory label for people and cultures.
凶猛的、残酷的；历史上也曾被用作贬低某些民族与文化的称呼，现代使用应注意语境。
tribe: A tribe is a social group often connected by ancestry, culture or community; meanings and preferred labels vary by context.
部落、族群或共同体；涉及真实族群时应尊重其自称，避免机械地以 tribe 概括所有群体。
vice: Vice is immoral conduct or a bad habit; in compounds such as vice president it means deputy or second in rank.
恶习、罪恶行为；在 vice president 等复合词中表示副职，与道德含义无关。
affection: Affection is a warm feeling of fondness or attachment toward someone or something, not necessarily romantic love.
喜爱、亲情或温情，强调亲近和关怀，不一定是恋爱关系。
carriage: A carriage is a vehicle, especially a horse-drawn one; in British English it can also mean a railway coach or manner of bearing oneself.
马车；英式英语中也可指火车车厢，或人的姿态、举止。
relief: Relief is the easing of distress, pain or pressure; it can also mean assistance, artistic raised forms, or a replacement worker.
缓解、宽慰；也可指救济、浮雕，或接替别人工作的人。
solemn: Solemn describes something serious, formal or grave, especially an occasion, duty or promise.
庄严的、严肃郑重的；常用于仪式、誓言或重要场合，未必表示悲伤。
faithful: Faithful means loyal or reliable; a faithful account or translation accurately reflects its original.
忠诚、忠实可靠的；形容记录或译文时表示忠于原文、准确再现。
beast: A beast is an animal, especially a large or wild one; figuratively it may describe cruelty or exceptional toughness.
野兽或大型动物；引申可指凶残的人，口语中也可能用来形容极强悍者。
heaven: Heaven can mean the sky or a religious realm of bliss; figuratively it may mean an extremely pleasant place.
天堂、天国；诗性或引申用法中也可指天空或令人无比愉悦的地方。
keen: Keen can mean eager or enthusiastic, sharp or intense, and sometimes strongly felt.
热切的、渴望的；也可指敏锐、锋利或强烈的，如 keen interest（浓厚兴趣）。
prime: Prime can mean most important or highest quality; it also refers to a number divisible only by one and itself.
主要的、最好的或全盛的；数学中 prime number 是质数，词义随领域改变。
intimate: Intimate means very close or personal; as a verb pronounced differently, it can mean to hint or make known indirectly.
形容词指亲密的、私人的；作动词时意为暗示、含蓄透露，重音和读音有所不同。
lesson: A lesson is a period of teaching or something learned from experience; it may be practical or moral.
课、课程；也可指从经验或错误中得到的教训、启示。
unknown: Unknown means not known or identified; an unknown in mathematics is a quantity whose value has not yet been determined.
未知的、不为人知的；数学中 an unknown 指未知量。
acting: Acting can mean performing in a play, or temporarily carrying out the duties of a position, as in acting director.
表演、演戏；用于头衔时可表示临时代理职责，如 acting director（代理主任）。
column: A column is a vertical structural support, an arrangement of text in a newspaper, or a vertical set of data in a table.
柱子；报刊的一栏或专栏；表格中纵向排列的一列。
discovery: A discovery is finding something that already existed but was unknown; an invention involves creating something new.
发现，即认识原本存在但未知的事物；区别于创造新事物的 invention（发明）。
engineer: An engineer applies technical knowledge to design or build systems; as a verb, engineer may mean to arrange or contrive an outcome.
工程师；作动词意为设计、策划或促成某事，语境中有时带“精心操纵”的意味。
retreat: To retreat is to withdraw or move back; a retreat can also be a peaceful place or organized period away for reflection.
撤退、退避；名词还可指静修活动或隐居休憩之所。
traditionally: Traditionally means according to established custom or practice, though the practice may change over time.
传统上、按惯例；描述既有做法，不表示这种做法永远不变。
assured: Assured can mean confident or guaranteed; an assured manner shows self-confidence rather than certainty about facts.
有把握的、自信的；也可表示得到保证的。举止自若不等于判断必然正确。
intense: Intense describes a high degree of force, feeling, activity or concentration; it does not always mean violent.
强烈的、密集的、专注的；可形容情感、训练、光线等，不一定含暴力。
poetry: Poetry is writing that uses language for concentrated imaginative, rhythmic or expressive effects; it is not limited to rhyming verse.
诗歌，以凝练、富表现力的语言和节奏组织内容；并非所有诗歌都押韵。
origin: Origin is the point or source where something begins or arises; it may refer to geographic, historical or causal beginnings.
起源、来源或发源地；可表示地理、历史或因果意义上的起点，不一定只指人的出身。
extent: Extent is how large, far or serious something is; to some extent means partly, not completely.
范围、程度；to some extent 表示在某种程度上，并非完全如此。
judgement: Judgment is a decision or opinion reached after consideration; it can also mean the ability to make sensible decisions.
判断、裁决或意见；也可指判断力。英式英语还常写作 judgement，但法律语境通常用 judgment。
warning: A warning is notice of possible danger or an unwanted consequence; it indicates risk, not certainty.
警告、预警，提醒可能出现的危险或后果，并不表示风险必然发生。
route: A route is a way from one place to another; it can also be a sequence of steps or a method of achieving a goal.
路线、途径；也可比喻达成目标的方法或流程。
shell: A shell is a hard outer covering; in computing a shell is a command interface, and in warfare it can mean an artillery projectile.
外壳、贝壳；计算机领域指命令行解释器，军事语境中可指炮弹。
application: An application can be a formal request, practical use of a method, or a computer program.
申请；也可指知识与方法的应用，或计算机应用程序。
mechanic: A mechanic repairs machines or vehicles; the plural mechanics can mean the principles of motion or how a process works.
机械修理工；复数 mechanics 还可指力学，或某种过程的运作机制。
magazine: A magazine is a periodical publication; in technical contexts it can also mean a storage compartment for ammunition.
杂志、期刊；某些技术与军事语境中也指弹药仓或弹匣。
ray: A ray is a narrow beam of light or energy; in geometry it is a half-line extending endlessly in one direction.
光线、射线；几何中指从一点出发向一个方向无限延伸的射线。
organ: An organ is a body structure with a particular function; it can also be a musical instrument or an official publication.
器官；也可指管风琴，或团体、机构的官方刊物。
plot: A plot is the arrangement of events in a story, a small piece of land, or a secret plan; to plot means to plan or graph data.
情节、小块土地或阴谋；作动词可指密谋，也可指绘制数据图表。
plate: A plate can be a dish or a flat piece of material; in science it may refer to a thin flat component or a tectonic plate.
盘子、薄板；在科学语境中可指实验用板、结构板或地质板块。
reflection: Reflection can mean an image in a mirror, the return of light or sound, or careful thought about an experience.
倒影；光或声音的反射；也可指反思、深思。
coverage: Coverage is the extent of something included or reported; in insurance it refers to risks or costs protected by a policy.
覆盖范围、报道情况；保险语境中指保障或承保范围。
construction: Construction is the building of something; it can also mean a grammatical structure or an interpretation of meaning.
建设、施工；语言学中可指语法结构，解释文本时也可指某种理解方式。
patience: Patience is the ability to wait or endure problems without becoming annoyed or giving up.
耐心、忍耐力；强调在等待或困难中保持镇定、不轻易放弃。
channel: A channel is a passage for water or communication; in electronics it can mean a separate path for signals.
水道、频道或传播渠道；电子系统中也指独立的信号通道。
related: Related means connected in some way, but does not specify whether one thing causes the other.
相关的、有联系的；不意味着一个事物必然导致另一个事物。
presupposition: A presupposition is a background assumption taken for granted by a statement or argument, rather than explicitly asserted.
预设是话语或论证默认成立的背景前提，并非直接陈述的主张。
intentional: Intentional means done on purpose, not merely foreseeable or accidental.
有意的、故意的；强调行为出于明确意图，而非仅仅可以预见其结果。
dispersion: Dispersion is the spreading or variability of values, particles, or people; in statistics it describes how widely data are distributed.
散布、扩散；统计学中指数据的离散程度，不等于平均值。
pulse: A pulse is a brief, often repeated signal or burst; it can also mean a heartbeat felt in an artery.
脉冲、短促信号；也可指脉搏。技术语境中常强调持续时间短。
compensation: Compensation can mean payment for work or loss, or an adjustment that offsets an unwanted effect.
报酬、赔偿；也指为抵消误差、偏移或其他影响所作的补偿。
amplification: Amplification increases the strength of a signal or effect; it does not necessarily improve its quality.
放大、增强信号或效果；放大的也可能包括噪声，并不必然提高质量。
propagate: To propagate is to spread, transmit, or reproduce something, such as a wave, signal, error, or plant.
传播、传递（波、信号、误差等）；也可指繁殖、增殖。
dependence: Dependence is the state of relying on something or the way one quantity varies with another.
依赖、依存关系；数学和科学中也指变量之间的依赖关系。
unconditional: Unconditional means not subject to specified restrictions or requirements; contrast with conditional.
无条件的、不附带限制的；与 conditional（有条件的）相对。
background: Background is the surrounding context or underlying signal against which a subject is observed; it can also mean a person's history.
背景、背景信息；测量中可指与目标信号区分开的背景成分。
contamination: Contamination is the introduction of an unwanted substance, signal, or influence into something.
污染、混入不需要的成分；实验中也可指样品、数据或信号受干扰。
numerical: Numerical concerns numbers or calculations; numerical results may be approximate rather than exact.
数字的、数值计算的；“数值解”往往是近似计算结果，不等同于解析解。
digital: Digital describes information represented in discrete values, especially binary data, rather than continuously varying values.
数字式的、数字技术的；信息以离散数值表示，通常采用二进制。
analogue: Analogue can mean a counterpart or a continuously varying signal; analogue is the usual British spelling of analog in the technical sense.
对应物、类似物；技术上也指模拟式信号，analogue 是常见英式拼写。
binary: Binary means involving two alternatives; in computing it commonly refers to base-two values or machine-readable data.
二元的、二进制的；计算机语境中也指二进制数据或可执行文件。
buffer: A buffer temporarily holds data or absorbs fluctuations between parts operating at different rates; it can also cushion an impact.
缓冲区、缓冲装置；在数据传输中临时存储数据，以协调速度差异。
queue: A queue is a line of people or a collection of tasks/data waiting to be processed, commonly in arrival order.
队列、排队人群；计算中通常指等待处理的数据或任务。
registration: Registration is the act of recording or enrolling something; in technical contexts it can mean spatial or temporal alignment of data.
登记、注册；技术语境中还可指数据或图像的配准、对齐。
detection: Detection means discovering the presence of something, not necessarily identifying exactly what it is.
检测、探测到某物存在；不一定已经识别其具体身份或类型。
realization: Realization is understanding something or making it real; in statistics it can refer to one observed outcome of a random process.
领悟、实现；概率统计中也可指随机过程或随机变量的一次实现值。
predecessor: A predecessor is a person, item, or state that came before another in a position or sequence.
前任、前身、前驱；指在职位、时间或序列中居前的对象。
successor: A successor takes the place of something or follows it in a sequence, office, or role.
继任者、后继、后续项；与 predecessor（前驱）相对。
preface: A preface is an introductory section of a book, usually explaining its purpose or background; as a verb it means to introduce remarks.
序言、前言；作动词时表示以一段说明作为话语的开头。
stem: A stem is the main supporting part of a plant, the base of a word, or the source from which something arises.
茎、词干、来源；在语言学中指词的核心形式。
composite: Composite means made of several parts; as a noun it can mean a combined material or image.
复合的、合成的；也指复合材料或合成图像，强调由不同部分构成。
collective: Collective means belonging to or done by a group as a whole rather than by individuals separately.
集体的、共同的；强调群体作为整体，并非一定由不同材料合成。
tier: A tier is one level within a system of ranks, prices, services, or layers.
层级、档次、阶层；强调分层体系中的某一级。
token: A token is a symbol, unit, or object used to represent something; in language processing it is a unit produced by tokenization.
标记、代币、凭证；自然语言处理中指分词/分词元处理得到的基本单元。
pronunciation: Pronunciation is the way a word is spoken, including its sounds, stress, and sometimes intonation.
发音、读法；包含语音、重音等，不等于单一的口音。
phonetic: Phonetic relates to speech sounds or their transcription, often representing the actual sounds produced.
语音的、音标的；侧重语音的实际发出与记录。
homograph: A homograph is a word written the same way as another but with a different meaning, sometimes with a different pronunciation.
同形异义词；拼写相同而意义不同，读音未必相同。
synonymous: Synonymous means having the same or nearly the same meaning, though usage and connotations may differ.
同义的、意思相近的；不表示在所有语境下都可互换。
comparison: A comparison examines similarities or differences between two or more things, not necessarily ranking them.
比较、对照；可以比较异同，不一定要进行优劣排序。
formal: Formal may mean official, rule-governed, or suited to a serious context; in language it contrasts with informal usage.
正式的、形式上的、规范化的；语言中通常与非正式表达相对。
dialect: A dialect is a language variety associated with a region or social group, including distinctive grammar and vocabulary as well as pronunciation.
方言、地域或社会语言变体；差异可能涉及语法和词汇，不只是口音。
idiomatic: Idiomatic means natural and typical in a language or characteristic of an idiom, rather than necessarily literal.
地道的、符合习惯表达的；也可指具有习语特征的。
scheme: A scheme is an organized plan or system; in some contexts it suggests a deceptive plan, but not always.
方案、制度、计划；某些语境带“阴谋”色彩，但并非所有 scheme 都是贬义。
tactic: A tactic is a specific action used to achieve a short-term goal within a broader strategy.
策略中的具体手段、战术；通常比 strategy（总体战略）更具体。
integration: Integration combines components into a functioning whole; it can also mean inclusion in a larger social or institutional system.
集成、整合；使各组成部分协同工作，也可指社会或制度的融入。
phrase: A phrase is a group of words functioning as a unit; in grammar it need not form a complete sentence.
短语、词组；语法上可以充当句子成分，但未必构成完整句子。
expound: To expound is to explain a theory or idea carefully and in detail, often in a formal setting.
详细阐述、论述（观点或理论）；通常比简单 explain 更正式。
characterize: To characterize means to describe the distinctive qualities of something, or to represent it in a particular way.
刻画、描述其特征；也可表示将某事界定为某种性质。
pinpoint: To pinpoint is to locate or identify something with great precision, such as a cause, place, or problem.
精确定位、准确指出；常用于位置、原因或问题。
specialize: To specialize means to focus on a narrow area of study, work, or function; in mathematics it can mean restricting a general result to a case.
专攻、专门研究；数学中还可指将一般结论特化到特定情况。
adjudicate: To adjudicate is to decide a dispute or claim through an authoritative, often legal, process.
裁决、判定争议或主张；通常带有正式法律或仲裁程序意味。
syllable: A syllable is a unit of pronunciation typically organized around a vowel sound, not necessarily one written character.
音节；发音上的节律单位，通常以元音为中心，不等于一个字母或汉字。
lexicon: A lexicon is the vocabulary of a language, speaker, or field, or a dictionary collecting those words.
词汇系统、专业词汇表、词典；可指某语言或领域的词语总和。
discourse: Discourse means connected spoken or written language, or discussion within a particular social or intellectual context.
话语、论述、语篇；也可指特定领域的讨论体系。
intonation: Intonation is the rising and falling pitch pattern of speech, which can convey emphasis, attitude, or sentence type.
语调；说话时音高的升降模式，常表达强调、态度或句式区别。
acronym: An acronym is an abbreviation formed from initial letters and pronounced as a word, such as NASA; not every initialism is an acronym.
首字母缩略词；通常像一个单词那样读出，不是所有字母缩写都属于此类。
glossary: A glossary is a list of specialized or unfamiliar terms with explanations, often placed at the end of a book.
术语表、词汇表；常附在书后，集中解释专业或生僻术语。
caption: A caption is explanatory text accompanying an image, table, or video; it can also mean on-screen subtitles.
图注、表注、说明文字；视频场景下也可指字幕。
quotation: A quotation is words repeated from a source, usually marked or attributed; it can also mean an estimated price.
引文、引用语；商务场景中亦可指报价。
bibliography: A bibliography is a list of books or sources consulted or cited, often at the end of scholarly work.
参考书目、文献目录；不一定每一项都在正文中直接引用。
entry: An entry is a recorded item, dictionary article, or act of entering a place or competition.
条目、记录、参赛/进入行为；词典中指一个词的条目。
normalization: Normalization means making things conform to a standard; in statistics/data processing it can mean rescaling or adjusting values.
规范化、归一化；在数据处理中可能指缩放到某一范围，也可能指按规则标准化。
classification: Classification assigns items to categories according to specified criteria; it does not inherently predict continuous values.
分类、归类；依据标准分配到类别，不等同于预测连续数值的回归。
emulate: To emulate means to imitate a system or behavior, often to match its function, or to try to equal someone's achievement.
仿真、模拟某系统的行为；也可指效仿某人以达到相同成就。
madame: Madame is a polite form of address for a woman, especially in French-speaking contexts; in English it can sound formal or deliberately foreign.
madame 是法语语境中对女性的礼貌称呼；英语中使用时往往带正式或外来语色彩，不能直接等同于所有场合的“女士”。
russian: Russian can describe the language, the nationality, or something associated with Russia; the noun also refers to a person or the language.
Russian 作形容词指俄罗斯的、俄罗斯人的或俄语的；作名词可指俄罗斯人或俄语，要根据语境区分。
famous: Famous means widely known, not necessarily respected or admired; it often takes for to introduce the reason.
famous 表示广为人知，并不必然意味着受尊敬；常用 be famous for 说明成名原因。
greatly: Greatly means to a large extent; it usually modifies verbs or participles in relatively formal English.
greatly 表示“极大地、在很大程度上”，常修饰动词或过去分词，语气通常比 very 正式。
threaten: Threaten can mean making an explicit threat or indicating that something harmful may happen.
threaten 既可表示威胁要采取某种行动，也可表示危险或不利情况即将发生，例如 threaten to collapse。
twice: Twice means two times, either on two occasions or as a multiplier; twice as ... as expresses comparison.
twice 既表示“两次”，也表示“两倍”；twice as ... as 是倍数比较结构，不能简单替换为 two times more。
wander: Wander is to move without a fixed route, or for thoughts and attention to drift away from a topic.
wander 可指漫无目的地走动，也可指思绪、注意力游离；wander off 表示走开或偏离主题。
county: A county is an administrative region, but its exact status differs by country, such as the UK and the US.
county 是行政区划名称，常译为“郡”或“县”，但英美制度并不完全对应，具体应依据国家和语境翻译。
hesitate: Hesitate means pausing because of uncertainty or reluctance; hesitate to do something often means being unwilling to act immediately.
hesitate 表示因犹豫、不确定或顾虑而迟疑；hesitate to do 表示犹豫是否采取行动。
nobody: Nobody is a pronoun meaning no person, but as a noun it may refer disparagingly to someone considered unimportant.
nobody 作代词表示“没有人”；作名词也可带贬义，指“无名小卒”，二者不应混淆。
tremble: Tremble is to shake slightly because of fear, cold, weakness, or strong emotion; it can also describe a vibrating object.
tremble 表示因恐惧、寒冷、虚弱或激动而发抖，也可描述物体轻微振动。
dangerous: Dangerous means likely to cause harm, not merely difficult or unpleasant.
dangerous 指可能造成伤害或危险的；不等于一般意义上的“困难”或“令人不快”。
ignorant: Ignorant can mean lacking knowledge, or being unaware of a particular fact; ignorant of is often more precise and less insulting.
ignorant 可指缺乏知识，也可表示“不知情”；be ignorant of 某事只说明不了解该事实，不一定评价一个人的智力。
occasional: Occasional means happening from time to time rather than regularly; an occasional event need not be rare.
occasional 表示“偶尔发生的、非经常性的”，强调频率不固定，不一定意味着极其罕见。
belief: Belief may be confidence that a proposition is true, a personally held conviction, or a system of religious ideas.
belief 可指认为某事属实的看法、个人信念，也可指宗教信仰；应区分 belief in 与 belief that 的结构。
interrupt: Interrupt means breaking the continuity of an action or speech; in computing, an interrupt is a signal that diverts processor execution.
interrupt 指打断讲话、活动或连续过程；计算机中的“中断”则是促使处理器暂时转去处理事件的信号或机制。
lovely: Lovely describes something beautiful, pleasant, or delightful; in conversation it can also express warm approval.
lovely 表示美好、可爱或令人愉快；口语中也可作为赞许回应，并非总要译作“漂亮”。
sentence: A sentence is a grammatical unit or a punishment ordered by a court; the verb means to impose such a punishment.
sentence 可指语法上的“句子”，也可指法院判处的“刑罚”；作动词表示“判刑”，两个义项须按语境区分。
hero: Hero is a person admired for courage or achievement; in stories it can simply refer to the principal male character.
hero 可指受到敬佩的英雄人物；文学中也可指男主人公，不一定具有道德上的英雄品质。
hole: A hole is an opening or empty space in a surface or object; figuratively it may be a flaw in an argument or plan.
hole 指孔洞、开口或空缺；在论证中 a hole in the argument 指“漏洞”，不是实物的孔。
newspaper: A newspaper is a publication reporting news, whether printed or digital; its name can also refer to the publishing organization.
newspaper 通常指报道新闻的报纸或新闻出版物，有时借指该媒体机构，不应只按纸张材质理解。
accident: An accident is an unintended event, often harmful, but by accident means something happened unintentionally rather than through design.
accident 常指意外事件或事故；by accident 表示“偶然、无意中”，未必指发生了危险事故。
climb: Climb means moving upward, physically or figuratively; numbers, prices, and temperatures can also climb.
climb 指攀爬、上升，也可用于价格、数字或温度上涨；不必有攀登动作。
lover: A lover can be a romantic or sexual partner; a lover of music or books simply means an enthusiast.
lover 可指恋人、情人；但 a lover of books 是“爱书的人”，不能误译为恋爱关系。
worship: Worship means showing reverence to a deity, or admiring someone to an excessive degree.
worship 可指宗教上的崇拜、礼拜，也可比喻对人的过度崇拜，语气通常强于 admire。
bread: Bread normally means food made by baking dough; in informal contexts it may refer to money or a livelihood.
bread 的本义是“面包”，也可在习语或非正式表达中指“生计、钱”，例如 earn one's bread。
cousin: Cousin refers to a relative such as a parent's sibling's child; standard English does not normally distinguish older/younger or maternal/paternal cousins.
cousin 指堂表兄弟姐妹等亲属；普通英语不区分性别长幼及父母哪一方的亲属，翻译时要结合上下文。
handsome: Handsome often describes an attractive man, but it can also describe an impressive amount or a well-proportioned object.
handsome 常形容男性英俊，也可形容报酬“可观”或物体“匀称大方”，不能一概译为“帅”。
harry: As a verb, harry means repeatedly troubling, attacking, or harassing someone; it is not the same as the given name Harry.
harry 作动词表示反复侵扰、骚扰或逼迫；与人名 Harry 同形但词义不同。
tired: Tired means needing rest, but tired of something means bored with or weary of it.
tired 表示疲倦；be tired of 则常表示“厌倦”，不必涉及体力疲劳。
telling: Telling, as an adjective, describes evidence or a remark that reveals something important or is particularly effective.
telling 作形容词表示“很能说明问题的、有力的”，如 telling evidence；不是单纯“正在讲述的”。
wash: Wash means cleaning with water or another liquid; it may also refer to waves washing over land or a substance being rinsed away.
wash 常指清洗；也可表示水流冲过、冲走或冲刷，具体宾语决定译法。
disappoint: Disappoint means failing to meet someone's hopes or expectations; disappointed describes a person's feeling, disappointing describes the cause.
disappoint 指未达到他人期待而使其失望；disappointed 是感到失望，disappointing 是令人失望。
dust: Dust may mean fine dry particles, or the act of removing or applying a powder; the verb's meaning depends on the object.
dust 作名词指灰尘、粉末；作动词既可指“除尘”，也可指“撒粉”，需看宾语与搭配。
fourth: Fourth is the ordinal form of four; a fourth can also mean one of four equal parts.
fourth 表示“第四”，也可表示“四分之一”，应结合是否在说顺序或比例判断。
supreme: Supreme means highest in rank, authority, or degree; in institutional names the translation is often fixed.
supreme 指最高级别、最高权威或程度极高；用于机构名称时通常采用约定译名，如 Supreme Court。
consideration: Consideration means careful thought; in other contexts it can mean a factor to weigh or, in contract law, something exchanged for a promise.
consideration 可指“考虑”，也可指应权衡的“因素”；合同法中还可指“对价”，属于专业义项。
naturally: Naturally can mean in a natural manner, as expected, or as a conversational marker meaning of course.
naturally 可指“自然地”，也可指“理所当然、正如预期”；用作话语副词时常表示“当然”。
poem: A poem is a literary composition organized as verse or with poetic language; it need not rhyme.
poem 指诗歌作品，不要求必须押韵；与 poetry（诗歌这一文学类别）应区别。
relations: Relations can mean connections between people or organizations, while relatives means family members; relations also has a less common kinship use.
relations 常指人际、外交或组织之间的“关系”；虽然有时可指亲属，但通常不要与 relatives 混用。
preach: Preach means delivering a religious sermon, or telling people what they should do in a moralizing manner.
preach 可指布道、讲道，也可指居高临下地说教；后者常带负面语气。
song: A song is a piece of music intended to be sung, while an instrumental piece is not usually called a song in precise usage.
song 通常指供人演唱的歌曲；纯器乐作品一般称 piece 或 composition 更准确。
breakfast: Breakfast is the first meal of the day after waking; have breakfast is a natural collocation.
breakfast 指早餐；表示“吃早餐”常说 have breakfast，不必使用 eat the breakfast。
display: Display can mean showing information, exhibiting objects, or behaving in a way that reveals a quality; the noun can mean a screen.
display 可指显示信息、陈列物品或表现某种特质；作名词还可指显示屏、展示活动。
justice: Justice refers to fairness or the legal system's administration of law; a justice may also be a judge in certain courts.
justice 可指正义、公平或司法；在部分法域，a justice 还指法官，不应一概按抽象品质解释。
library: A library is a collection of books or a place providing them; in software it is reusable code or other organized resources.
library 可指图书馆或藏书；编程语境则常指“库”，包含可复用代码或资源。
spiritual: Spiritual concerns the human spirit or religion, rather than merely mental activity; context determines whether to translate it as 精神的 or 宗教的.
spiritual 指精神、心灵或宗教层面的事物；不能无条件等同于 psychological（心理的）。
unfortunate: Unfortunate means unlucky or regrettable; an unfortunate remark may be ill-judged rather than unlucky.
unfortunate 可指不幸，也可指“令人遗憾、不妥当”；an unfortunate remark 常是“不恰当的话”。
celebrate: Celebrate means marking an event with festivities or praise; it may also mean publicly recognizing an achievement.
celebrate 指庆祝节日、事件或成就，也可指公开赞颂、表彰；不必都有聚会。
truly: Truly means genuinely or in fact; it can intensify a judgment or assure the listener of sincerity.
truly 表示真正地、确实地，也可加强态度或强调真诚，不能在所有句子中机械译为“真实地”。
advanced: Advanced can mean technologically developed, higher-level, or farther along in time or progress.
advanced 可指技术先进、课程高级，或处于较晚阶段；advanced age 则指高龄。
contact: Contact can mean physical touching, communication, or a person who can provide information or help.
contact 可指物理接触、联系交流，也可作名词指“联系人、人脉”。
knock: Knock means striking a surface, often to attract attention, and can also mean criticizing or damaging something.
knock 可指敲击、敲门，也可在非正式英语中表示批评或撞坏，不能只译作“敲”。
mental: Mental relates to the mind, cognition, or psychological condition; it is not always a reference to mental illness.
mental 指心理、心智或认知方面的；单独出现时并不必然表示“精神疾病”。
offend: Offend means causing someone to feel insulted; in legal contexts it may mean committing an offense.
offend 可指冒犯、使人不快；在法律语境也可指违法、犯罪，需要与 insult 区分。
roof: A roof is the top covering of a building or vehicle; figuratively a roof over one's head means shelter.
roof 指屋顶或遮盖；a roof over one's head 比喻有栖身之所，并非只强调建筑材料。
sand: Sand is granular material composed of tiny particles of rock or minerals; it can be a verb meaning to smooth a surface with sandpaper.
sand 作名词指沙；作动词也可指“用砂纸打磨”，与撒沙的动作不同。
spare: Spare can mean extra, available, or allowing someone to avoid harm; spare time is free time, while spare someone means refrain from harming or troubling them.
spare 可指备用、多余或空闲；spare time 是空闲时间，spare someone 则可表示饶恕或让某人免受麻烦。
defeat: Defeat means winning against an opponent or preventing a plan from succeeding; defeat as a noun means loss in a contest.
defeat 作动词指击败对手、使计划落空；作名词指失败、败北，未必与战争有关。
endure: Endure means tolerating something unpleasant or continuing to exist through difficulty or time.
endure 既指忍受痛苦、艰难，也指经受考验而持续存在，语气强于普通的 continue。
enthusiasm: Enthusiasm is strong interest and excitement, often expressed for an activity or idea.
enthusiasm 指对活动或想法的热忱与积极兴趣，常搭配 enthusiasm for。
eternal: Eternal means lasting forever or seeming to have no end; everlasting is close but can have different stylistic uses.
eternal 表示永恒的、无尽的；有时带夸张意味，不一定是严格的哲学或宗教主张。
excuse: Excuse as a noun is a reason or justification; as a verb it means forgiving an action or allowing someone to leave.
excuse 作名词可指理由、借口；作动词可指原谅、准许离开，excuse me 还常用于礼貌打断。
fleet: A fleet is a group of ships, aircraft, or vehicles operated together; it does not always refer to warships.
fleet 指统一管理的舰船、飞机或车辆群；fleet of buses 是公交车队，不专指舰队。
rage: Rage is intense anger, but as a verb it can also describe a storm or fire continuing violently.
rage 指盛怒；作动词也可形容暴风雨、火灾等猛烈持续，不一定涉及人的情绪。
shock: Shock can mean sudden emotional upset, a physical jolt, or a medical state of dangerously inadequate circulation.
shock 可指震惊、冲击、电击；医学上的“休克”有特定含义，不能与一般“受惊”混同。
weapon: A weapon is an object used to attack or defend, but the term may also be used metaphorically for a powerful means.
weapon 指武器，也可比喻用于达成目标的有力手段；不能把所有出现都当作实体兵器。
yesterday: Yesterday refers to the day before today; figuratively it can represent the recent past.
yesterday 指昨天；在比喻用法中也可指不久之前的过去，如 yesterday's methods。
breathe: Breathe is a verb meaning taking air into and out of the lungs; breath is the corresponding noun.
breathe 是“呼吸”的动词，breath 则是名词“气息、呼吸”，拼写和发音不同。
conscience: Conscience is one's moral sense of right and wrong, not simply being conscious or awake.
conscience 指良心、道德判断感，与 consciousness（意识、知觉）不是一回事。
deck: Deck means a floor on a ship or an outdoor platform; it can also mean a set of playing cards.
deck 可指船甲板、露台或一副纸牌，计算机或演示语境中还可能指幻灯片组。
description: A description is an account of what someone or something is like; it is not the same as an evaluation or explanation of causes.
description 是对外观、特征或情况的描述，不等同于评价，也不一定提供原因解释。
electric: Electric describes equipment powered by electricity or something causing excitement; electrical refers more broadly to electricity and electrical systems.
electric 常指用电驱动或带电的，也可比喻气氛令人兴奋；与 electrical（电气系统相关）用法有区别。
manufacture: Manufacture means making goods on a large scale; figuratively it can mean inventing evidence or a story dishonestly.
manufacture 指工业生产、制造，也可贬义表示“捏造”证据或说辞。
murmur: A murmur is a low, soft sound or quiet complaint; a heart murmur is an abnormal heart sound heard on examination.
murmur 指低语、窃窃私语或轻声抱怨；heart murmur 是心脏杂音，不是情绪上的“抱怨”。
ocean: An ocean is a very large body of salt water; figuratively an ocean of something means an enormous amount.
ocean 指海洋；an ocean of ... 可比喻数量极大，不必涉及地理意义。
pound: Pound can mean a unit of weight, the British currency unit, or a heavy repeated strike; context is essential.
pound 可指重量单位“磅”、英国货币单位“英镑”，也可指重击或连续敲打，不能混译。
temper: Temper can mean a person's mood or anger; as a verb it means moderating something or heat-treating metal.
temper 可指脾气、心境；作动词既可指缓和，也可指金属回火处理，属于不同语境。
bridge: Bridge is a structure crossing an obstacle; it can also mean a connection between groups or a network device linking segments.
bridge 是桥梁，也可比喻沟通纽带；计算机网络中指桥接设备，与 bridge a gap 的比喻义应区分。
edition: An edition is a particular published form or release of a book, newspaper, or other work.
edition 指书报或其他作品的某个版本、版次，不等同于一次编辑动作。
friendly: Friendly describes kind or supportive behavior; user-friendly means easy to use and environmentally friendly means less harmful to the environment.
friendly 表示友好、亲切；组合词 user-friendly 指易用，environmentally friendly 指相对环保，不能一概译为“友善”。
hunger: Hunger is the physical need for food, and figuratively a strong desire for something.
hunger 本义是饥饿，也可表示强烈渴望，如 hunger for knowledge（求知欲）。
instrument: An instrument is a tool or device for a particular purpose; it can also be a musical instrument or a means of achieving something.
instrument 指仪器、工具，也可指乐器或实现某目的的手段；不同领域译法差异很大。
leap: Leap is to jump a long distance or move suddenly to a new level; prices and technology can make a leap.
leap 指跳跃，也可表示数量、技术或认识上的突然跃升；a leap in performance 是性能大幅提升。
passion: Passion is a strong feeling or enthusiasm, not necessarily romantic desire.
passion 指强烈情感或热爱，可以针对工作、艺术或理想，不一定是爱情或欲望。
rapidly: Rapidly means quickly, often describing change or development; it need not imply physical movement.
rapidly 表示迅速地，常修饰增长、变化和发展，并非一定指移动速度。
steam: Steam is water vapor produced by boiling, and as a verb it can mean cooking with steam or moving with apparent force.
steam 指蒸汽；作动词可指蒸煮，也可形容车辆行进或人怒气冲冲地前进。
trail: Trail can mean a path, a track left behind, or following at a distance; trail behind means lagging behind.
trail 指小径、踪迹，也可指尾随或落后；trail behind 常是“落后于”，不是“开辟道路”。
verse: Verse can mean poetry in general, a line or stanza of a poem, or a section of a song.
verse 可指韵文、诗行或诗节，也可指歌曲中的一段主歌；与 chorus（副歌）不同。
abase: To abase someone is to lower their status or dignity deliberately; the verb is formal and often implies humiliation.
abase 指故意贬低他人的地位或尊严，语体较正式，常含“羞辱”意味；并非一般意义的降低高度。
abasement: Abasement is the experience or act of being humiliated or reduced in dignity, sometimes voluntarily.
abasement 指受辱、人格被贬低，或主动使自己卑下；不等于单纯的谦虚。
abash: To abash someone is to make them feel embarrassed, disconcerted or ashamed, especially unexpectedly.
abash 表示使人突然窘迫、羞惭或不知所措，通常比一般的 surprise 更强调自尊受到影响。
abashed: Someone who is abashed feels embarrassed, self-conscious, or temporarily at a loss for confidence.
abashed 形容因尴尬或羞愧而局促不安的人，不等同于长期缺乏自信。
abatement: Abatement is a reduction in intensity or amount; legally it may refer to a tax reduction or removal of a nuisance.
abatement 指程度或数量的减轻；法律与财税语境还可指减税、消除妨害等，需根据对象翻译。
abduct: To abduct is to take someone away unlawfully by force or deception; it is not simply to accompany someone.
abduct 指以暴力或欺骗手段非法掳走、绑架他人；不等于普通的带走或陪同。
abduction: Abduction generally means unlawful kidnapping; in anatomy it means moving a limb away from the body's midline.
abduction 常指绑架；解剖学中指肢体向远离身体正中线方向运动的“外展”，两个义项差别很大。
aberrant: Aberrant means departing noticeably from an accepted pattern or expected behavior; the tone may be negative or technical.
aberrant 表示明显偏离常态或预期行为；既可能带贬义，也可作为描述异常数据的中性术语。
abhorrent: Abhorrent describes something morally repugnant or deeply offensive, stronger than merely unpleasant.
abhorrent 表示在道德上令人极度厌恶、深恶痛绝的，语气强于 unpleasant。
ablution: An ablution is a washing, especially a ritual washing for religious or ceremonial purposes.
ablution 指洗涤，尤其是宗教仪式中的净身或洗礼行为；不能一概当作普通洗澡。
abrade: To abrade is to wear away a surface by rubbing or scraping; the word is often used for materials and skin.
abrade 指通过摩擦或刮擦磨损表面，常用于材料、皮肤等语境。
abrasion: Abrasion is either superficial damage caused by scraping or the process of wearing a surface away by friction.
abrasion 可指皮肤擦伤，也可指材料表面因摩擦产生的磨损过程。
abrasive: Abrasive means capable of grinding or wearing a surface away; figuratively it describes an unpleasantly harsh manner.
abrasive 可指有研磨作用的磨料或表面，也可形容人言语尖刻、生硬，不能只译成“粗糙”。
abscission: Abscission is the natural separation of a plant part, such as a leaf or fruit, from the plant.
abscission 是植物学中的“脱落”，指叶片、果实等器官自然与植株分离，不是一般意义的切除。
abscond: To abscond is to leave secretly and often unlawfully, especially to avoid arrest or responsibility.
abscond 指偷偷逃离，通常为了逃避逮捕、债务或责任，含有规避义务的意味。
absence: Absence can mean not being present, or the nonexistence or lack of something; absence of evidence has a specific logical meaning.
absence 可指缺席，也可指某物不存在或缺乏；absence of evidence（缺乏证据）不一定等同于 evidence of absence（证明不存在的证据）。
absolution: Absolution is forgiveness or release from guilt, especially in a religious or formal moral context.
absolution 指罪责的赦免或解除，尤其用于宗教赦罪与道德责任语境，不是普通的道歉。
absorb: To absorb can mean taking in liquid, energy or information; in physics it can mean transferring incident energy into matter.
absorb 可指吸收液体、能量或知识；物理学中涉及入射能量被材料吸收，与反射、透射有区别。
absurd: Absurd means wildly unreasonable or contrary to common sense; in philosophy the absurd can refer to a tension between human meaning and an indifferent world.
absurd 表示荒诞、不合情理；在哲学语境中“荒诞”还可能特指人的意义追寻与世界的冷漠之间的张力。
accumulation: Accumulation is a gradual buildup of quantity, material, evidence or wealth over time.
accumulation 指随时间逐步累积的过程或结果，可用于物质、资本、证据等，不一定只指堆积实物。
acknowledgment: Acknowledgment can be an admission, a confirmation of receipt, or an expression of thanks or credit.
acknowledgment 可指承认事实、确认收悉，也可指致谢或鸣谢；在通信与论文中应区别翻译。
acquainted: Being acquainted with someone means knowing them, usually not intimately; acquainted with a subject means familiar with it.
acquainted with someone 表示与某人认识但未必亲密；acquainted with a subject 表示了解某一主题。
activate: To activate is to make something operational or trigger a process; it does not necessarily mean increasing its power.
activate 指启用装置、激活机制或触发过程，并不必然表示提高功率或增益。
addictive: Addictive describes a substance or behavior with the potential to cause dependence; informally it may mean hard to stop enjoying.
addictive 可指容易导致依赖或成瘾的物质与行为；口语中也可泛指“让人停不下来”，两种程度不可混淆。
adhesion: Adhesion means sticking or attaching to a surface; in medicine it can mean an abnormal band of tissue joining structures.
adhesion 指黏附、附着；医学中可指组织间的“粘连”，不总等于普通的胶水黏合。
adolescent: An adolescent is a person in the transition from childhood to adulthood; the adjective describes this developmental stage.
adolescent 指青少年或青春期的人，也可作形容词表示青春期的；与 teenage 的年龄范围不完全相同。
adoption: Adoption can mean legally taking a child into a family or choosing to start using a method, policy or technology.
adoption 可指法律上的收养，也可指采纳方案、政策或采用新技术；须结合宾语确定意义。
affected: Affected can mean influenced by something; when describing speech or behavior it can mean artificial or pretentious.
affected 可指“受到影响的”；形容言谈举止时也可指“做作的、矫揉造作的”，两个义项不可混淆。
aggravated: Aggravated can mean made worse; in legal usage it often means an offense involving specified serious circumstances.
aggravated 可指情况“加重的”；法律上如 aggravated assault 指具有加重情节的犯罪，不一定表示情绪恼怒。
agriculture: Agriculture includes growing crops and raising livestock for food or other products; it is broader than crop cultivation alone.
agriculture 指农业生产，包括种植作物与饲养牲畜等，不限于耕种田地。
airborne: Airborne means carried by air, transmitted through air, or in flight; its exact sense depends on context.
airborne 可指在空中飞行的、空气传播的或空降的；airborne particles 通常是空气中悬浮的颗粒物。
aircraft: Aircraft is a collective term for machines capable of flight, including airplanes and helicopters; its singular and plural forms are identical.
aircraft 是飞行器的总称，涵盖飞机与直升机等；单复数同形，不能直接等同于 airplane。
aisle: An aisle is a passage between rows of seats or shelves; it differs from an isle, an island.
aisle 指座位或货架之间的通道；与意为“岛”的 isle 同音但词义不同。
alight: Alight can mean getting off a vehicle, landing on something, or (in some uses) burning brightly.
alight 作动词可指下车、降落或停落；作形容词可指燃烧着的、明亮的，需区分词性。
alloy: An alloy is a mixture of metals, or of a metal with another element, designed to change material properties.
alloy 是金属与其他金属或元素组成的合金，通常为了改变强度、耐蚀性等性质；作动词亦可指掺合。
allied: Allied means joined by a common purpose or association; Allied with an initial capital can refer to historical military alliances.
allied 指结盟的、关联的；特定历史语境中大写 Allied 可指盟军，不能一概译成泛泛的“联合”。
altitude: Altitude is height above a specified reference level, often sea level; it is not identical to distance from the Earth's center.
altitude 指相对于指定基准面（常为海平面）的高度；与离地高度 height above ground、地球中心距离并不相同。
amendment: An amendment is a formal change to a law, document, proposal or constitution; it may add, revise or remove provisions.
amendment 指正式的修正案或修改条款，可用于法律、合同及宪法；既可增补也可改写、删除内容。
animation: Animation is the creation of apparent motion from a sequence of images; it also refers to animated productions and lively behavior.
animation 可指动画制作、动画作品，也可指“活力、兴奋”；计算机图形中强调逐帧或连续运动呈现。
annotate: To annotate is to add explanatory notes or labels to text, data or images rather than rewriting the original material.
annotate 指为文字、数据或图像加注释、标记，通常并不改写原始内容。
anonymity: Anonymity is the condition of a person's identity being unknown or undisclosed, and should be distinguished from data confidentiality.
anonymity 指身份不公开或不可识别的状态；与信息保密 confidentiality 是不同的概念。
anticipation: Anticipation can be expectation of a future event, or a preparatory action taken in advance.
anticipation 指期待、预期，也可指提前准备或预先考虑；语气可积极也可焦虑。
apology: An apology is an expression of regret or acknowledgment of wrongdoing; in some historical uses apologia means a formal defense.
apology 通常指道歉；与辩护文 apologia 的历史义不同，道歉是否承担责任须看具体措辞。
appendix: An appendix can be an additional section of a book or report, or the anatomical organ attached to the large intestine.
appendix 可指书籍、论文末尾的“附录”，也可指人体“阑尾”；复数形式因语域不同可用 appendices 或 appendixes。
appointment: An appointment is a scheduled meeting, or an act of selecting someone for a position.
appointment 可指预约、约会，也可指任命职务；doctor's appointment 与 appointment to the board 不是同一义项。
appreciation: Appreciation can mean gratitude, an informed understanding of value, or an increase in an asset's market value.
appreciation 可指感激、鉴赏能力，也可指资产升值；经济语境下与 depreciation（贬值）相对。
ardent: Ardent means passionate or intensely enthusiastic, often about a belief, cause or relationship.
ardent 表示热烈、热情坚定的，常形容支持者、信念或情感，不必指脾气暴躁。
arsenal: An arsenal is a store of weapons, or figuratively the range of tools and resources available for a purpose.
arsenal 本义是武器库；比喻时可指解决问题的工具、技能储备，不一定与军事有关。
asteroid: An asteroid is a relatively small rocky or metallic body orbiting the Sun, distinct from a comet's typical icy composition.
asteroid 是围绕太阳运行的较小岩质或金属天体“小行星”；与彗星的典型组成和活动特征不同。
astronomy: Astronomy is the scientific study of celestial objects and the universe; it is distinct from astrology, which makes claims about human affairs.
astronomy 是科学研究天体与宇宙的“天文学”；与占星术 astrology 不同。
attainment: Attainment is the achievement of a goal or level, often through effort; educational attainment refers to completed education.
attainment 指目标、水平的达成；educational attainment 常指受教育程度或已完成的教育阶段。
auction: An auction is a sale in which buyers bid competitively; the winning offer depends on the auction's rules.
auction 是通过竞价出售物品的拍卖活动；具体成交规则取决于拍卖形式。
audacious: Audacious means daring and bold, often in a way that is surprising or regarded as presumptuous.
audacious 表示大胆、敢于冒险，有时带“鲁莽、放肆”的评价，须看语境。
augment: To augment something is to increase its size, amount or effectiveness by adding to it; the addition is often supplementary.
augment 指通过增加或补充使数量、规模、效果增强；比普通 increase 更常暗含“添补”的方式。
automate: To automate a process is to make it operate with reduced direct human intervention, not necessarily without any human oversight.
automate 指使流程自动化，减少人工直接操作；并不必然意味着完全无人监督。
availability: Availability means whether something is accessible or ready for use; in engineering it can be the fraction of time a system is operational.
availability 可指可获得性或可用状态；工程中的系统可用度通常指系统能够提供服务的时间比例，不能与可靠性完全等同。
axis: An axis is a reference line for rotation, coordinates or a graph; axes is its plural form.
axis 可指转轴、坐标轴或图表基准轴；复数 axes，不能与斧头 axe 混淆。
diligent: A diligent person works carefully and persistently, paying attention to what a task requires.
diligent 强调做事勤勉、持之以恒且认真细致；不只是“忙碌”。
formidable: Something formidable is difficult to deal with or inspires respect because of its strength or scale.
formidable 表示困难巨大、令人生畏，或因实力强大而令人敬畏；并不一定含贬义。
daunting: A daunting task appears difficult enough to make someone apprehensive.
daunting 指任务看起来艰巨、使人畏难，强调面对它时的心理压力。
capricious: A capricious person or process changes unpredictably, without a consistent reason.
capricious 指反复无常、变化难以预测，常暗示缺少稳定的依据。
erratic: Erratic behavior or movement is irregular and difficult to predict.
erratic 指行为、轨迹或结果不规则且难以预测，不一定像 capricious 那样涉及主观任性。
mundane: Something mundane belongs to ordinary daily life or lacks excitement.
mundane 指日常、平凡，也可以指乏味；并不等同于“低劣”。
tedious: A tedious activity is tiring or boring because it takes a long time or repeats excessively.
tedious 指冗长、重复、令人厌倦，重点在过程使人疲乏。
monotonous: Something monotonous lacks variety or changes very little.
monotonous 指单调、缺乏变化，可用于声音、工作或日常生活。
judicious: A judicious choice shows careful thought and sound judgment.
judicious 指经过审慎权衡、判断得当，不仅表示“聪明”。
reckless: A reckless action shows little regard for danger or consequences.
reckless 指鲁莽、不顾风险或后果，与有勇气的 daring 不同。
rash: A rash decision is made too quickly without sufficient consideration.
rash 指决定仓促、欠考虑；通常强调判断过急。
impulsive: An impulsive action is done suddenly because of an immediate urge rather than careful planning.
impulsive 指一时冲动而行动，强调即时冲动的驱使，不必然造成严重后果。
favorable: Favorable conditions support a desired result; a favorable opinion expresses approval.
favorable 可指条件有利，也可表示评价赞许；美式拼写为 favorable，英式常写 favourable。
expedient: An expedient action is convenient or useful for an immediate goal, sometimes at the cost of principle.
expedient 指为了当前目的而权宜、方便；有时暗含牺牲原则或长期考虑。
frugal: A frugal person uses money and resources carefully, avoiding unnecessary waste.
frugal 指节俭且重视资源利用，不意味着吝啬。
miserly: A miserly person is excessively unwilling to spend or give money.
miserly 指过度吝啬，通常含明显贬义。
precarious: A precarious position is insecure or unstable and could deteriorate suddenly.
precarious 指处境不稳、岌岌可危，强调可能突然恶化的风险。
perilous: A perilous situation involves serious danger.
perilous 指具有重大危险，程度一般强于单纯的 risky。
cogent: A cogent argument is clear, logical, and convincing.
cogent 形容论据清晰、推理有力且令人信服，并非仅指表达流畅。
counterfeit: A counterfeit object is made to imitate something genuine in order to deceive.
counterfeit 指以假冒真、意图欺骗的物品或货币；强调仿冒。
repudiate: To repudiate a claim or relationship is to reject it firmly and explicitly.
repudiate 指明确而坚决地否认、拒绝承认某项主张、责任或关系。
impede: To impede progress is to slow or obstruct it without necessarily stopping it completely.
impede 指阻碍或拖慢进展，不一定完全阻断。
thwart: To thwart a plan is to prevent it from succeeding.
thwart 指使计划或企图落空，重点是最终未能成功。
persevere: To persevere is to continue trying despite difficulties or discouragement.
persevere 指即使遭遇困难或挫折仍坚持努力，常带积极评价。
apportion: To apportion something is to divide and allocate it among different parties.
apportion 指按一定标准分摊或分配费用、责任、资源等。
mishap: A mishap is a minor accident or an unfortunate incident, often without serious consequences.
mishap 指意外的小事故或不顺利的事件，通常比 disaster 轻。
prototype: A prototype is an early working model used to test or develop a design.
prototype 指用于验证和改进设计的早期原型，不等于已经量产的产品。
knack: A knack is a special practical skill or natural ease at doing something.
knack 指做某事的诀窍或特别擅长的本领，语气较口语化。
flair: Flair is a natural talent or distinctive stylish ability in an activity.
flair 指天赋、特别的眼光或有风格的才华，常用于设计、语言或表演。
outlook: Outlook can mean an attitude toward the future, the expected prospects, or the view from a place.
outlook 可指对未来的看法、发展前景，也可指从某处望出去的景观。
champion: To champion a cause is to support and defend it publicly and actively.
champion 作动词表示积极倡导、支持某项事业；作名词还可指冠军或拥护者。
instigate: To instigate an event is to deliberately cause it to begin, especially something troublesome.
instigate 指蓄意挑起、促成某件事，常用于争端或不良事件。
bestow: To bestow an honor or gift is to confer or present it formally.
bestow 多用于正式授予荣誉、头衔或赠予礼物，语体较庄重。
sever: To sever a connection is to cut it off, physically or figuratively.
sever 表示切断连接或关系，可以是物理上的，也可以是抽象的。
instantaneous: An instantaneous change happens at once or is treated as having no appreciable duration.
instantaneous 指瞬时发生或在某个瞬间定义的量；物理语境中常译为“瞬时的”。
instinct: Instinct is an inborn tendency to behave or react in a particular way, without deliberate reasoning.
instinct 指不经有意识推理而表现出来的本能倾向；不同于基于经验的直觉判断。
refinement: Refinement is the process of improving something in small, deliberate steps; it can also mean polish or sophistication.
refinement 指对事物不断进行细致改进，也可表示举止或品味的精致、优雅。
limpid: Limpid describes liquid that is clear and transparent, or prose that is exceptionally clear.
limpid 形容液体清澈透明，也可形容文字明晰、通透，语体通常偏文学。
allegory: An allegory is a story or representation whose characters and events convey a second, often moral or political, meaning.
allegory 是寓言式叙事：人物与情节除了字面故事之外，还系统地承载道德、政治等象征意义。
etymology: Etymology is the study of a word’s history, including its origins and changes in form and meaning.
etymology 指词源学，研究词语的起源、形式演变和语义变迁；词源线索不一定等于现代词义。
cognate: Cognates are words in different languages that descend from the same historical source, whether or not they still look alike.
cognate 指不同语言中源自同一历史词根的同源词；外形相似未必意味着同源。
derivation: Derivation is the formation of a new word from an existing base, often by adding an affix; it also means origin or the process of deriving a result.
derivation 在构词法中指通过词缀等方式派生新词；在其他语境中还可指来源或推导过程。
inflection: Inflection is a change in a word’s grammatical form that expresses features such as tense, number or case without usually creating a new lexical item.
inflection 指屈折变化：改变词形以表达时态、数、格等语法信息，通常不创造新的词汇单位。
inflect: To inflect a word is to change its form to express grammatical information; to inflect a voice is to vary its tone.
inflect 可以指使词形发生语法变化，也可指改变说话的语调。
conjugate: To conjugate a verb is to list or produce its different grammatical forms, especially for person, number, tense or mood.
conjugate 指按人称、数、时态、语气等将动词变位；与一般的构词派生不同。
preposition: A preposition expresses a relation between its complement and another part of a sentence, often involving time, place or an abstract relation.
preposition 即介词，用于表示其补足语与句中其他成分之间的时间、空间或抽象关系。
conjunction: A conjunction links words, phrases or clauses and may express coordination or subordination.
conjunction 即连词，连接词、短语或分句，可表示并列关系或从属关系。
vocabulary: Vocabulary means the words known or used by a person, group or language; it can also refer to a selected set of words for study.
vocabulary 可指个人、群体或语言所使用或掌握的词汇，也可指学习用的特定词汇表。
dictionary: A dictionary records words and their senses, often with pronunciation, grammar, usage and etymology.
dictionary 即词典，记录词语及其义项，也常提供发音、语法、用法和词源信息。
thesaurus: A thesaurus organizes words by meaning and commonly supplies synonyms and related expressions; it is not a substitute for a usage dictionary.
thesaurus 是按语义关联组织词语的同义词词典；仅凭同义词列表不能判断词语在具体语境中的可替换性。
affix: An affix is a word part added to a base, such as a prefix or suffix, to create or modify a word.
词缀是附着在词基上的构词成分，包括前缀和后缀；它可以改变词义或语法功能。
adjective: An adjective describes or limits a noun or pronoun, for example precise in a precise measurement.
形容词描述或限定名词、代词，例如 a precise measurement（一次精确的测量）中的 precise。
adverb: An adverb modifies a verb, adjective, another adverb, or a clause; it does not always end in -ly.
副词修饰动词、形容词、其他副词或整个分句；副词并不一定以 -ly 结尾。
adjoin: To adjoin is to share a boundary with something or lie directly next to it, often of buildings or land.
adjoin 指与某物接壤或紧邻，常用于房屋、土地和空间位置关系。
accretion: Accretion is a gradual increase caused by the accumulation of material or small additions over time.
accretion 指材料或少量增量不断聚集而造成的逐渐增长；天体物理中也指吸积。
abstinent: An abstinent person deliberately refrains from an activity or substance, especially alcohol or sexual activity.
abstinent 指有意识地戒绝某种行为或物质，尤指戒酒或禁欲；不等同于仅仅使用较少。
administrator: An administrator manages the operation of an organization, institution, system, or a particular set of tasks.
administrator 指组织、机构或计算机系统的管理者；根据语境可译为行政人员、管理员或系统管理员。
authenticity: Authenticity is the quality of being genuine or true to its claimed origin or identity; it does not guarantee factual accuracy.
authenticity 指真实性或真品属性，即来源、身份与所宣称的一致；不等于内容必然准确。
avoidance: Avoidance is the act or pattern of staying away from something, rather than necessarily preventing it from occurring.
avoidance 指避开某事物的行为或习惯；不同于 prevent 所强调的阻止事件发生。
bewildered: Someone bewildered is deeply confused or unable to make sense of a situation, often because it is unexpected.
bewildered 表示困惑不解、摸不着头脑，常因情形突然而难以理解。
ceiling: A ceiling is the upper interior surface of a room or an upper limit on an amount, price, or achievement.
ceiling 可指房间天花板，也可引申为价格、数额或能力的上限。
chaotic: A chaotic situation lacks clear order or predictability; in mathematics, chaos may arise from deterministic dynamics.
chaotic 日常指混乱无序；在动力系统中，混沌可以源于确定性规律，并非完全随机。
circular: Circular means round in shape; applied to reasoning, it describes an argument that assumes what it claims to prove.
circular 可指圆形的；修饰论证时指循环论证，即把待证明的结论当作前提。
consolation: Consolation is comfort offered or received after disappointment, loss, or distress.
consolation 是失望、失落或悲伤之后得到的安慰，也可指聊以自慰的事物。
contaminate: To contaminate is to make something impure or unsafe by introducing unwanted material, organisms, or influence.
contaminate 指使物质、样本或环境受到污染；也可引申为外来因素干扰数据或判断。
contraction: Contraction is a process of becoming smaller or tighter; in grammar, it is a shortened form such as do not → don’t.
contraction 指收缩、紧缩；语法中指缩约形式，如 do not 缩为 don’t。
contributor: A contributor is someone or something that helps produce a result, supplies content, or gives resources.
contributor 可指参与者、供稿人或贡献因素；a contributing factor 指促成结果的因素。
deficient: Something deficient lacks enough of a required quality or quantity; it is more precise than merely being imperfect.
deficient 指缺乏必要数量或质量、不足或有缺陷，常与 in 连用表示“缺乏某方面”。
delimit: To delimit is to establish the boundaries or scope of something, such as a region, concept, or study.
delimit 指划定边界或限定范围，例如界定研究对象、概念或地理区域。
demise: Demise is the end, failure, or death of someone or something; in formal usage it can refer to the end of an institution.
demise 表示死亡、终结或消亡，常用于制度、企业或某种安排的结束。
